News.title: Incel or blood lust? What was ‘puppet master’ Bryan Kohberger’s real motive & how appeal shows Ted Bundy-style craving
News.content:
DEPRAVED murderer Bryan Kohberger may have wanted to emulate infamous serial killer Ted Bundy — and is now struggling with losing control behind bars, a violent crime expert has claimed.

Kohberger, 31, admitted to the brutal slayings of four University of Idaho students on November 13, 2022, as part of a plea agreement that spared him the death penalty.



But despite sitting silently through hours of emotional victim impact statements and admitting to the murders, Kohberger has now made a dramatic U-turn and is seeking to withdraw his plea and face trial.

The move comes as the Netflix documentary The Idaho Murders: College Nightmare reaches number one on the streaming platform.



The one question that still hasn’t been answered is why he targeted victims Kaylee Goncalves, 21, Madison Mogen, 21, Xana Kernodle, 20, and Ethan Chapin, 20.

The U.S. Sun spoke with Dr. Gary Brucato, a clinical psychologist, researcher and author who helped profile the person responsible for the murders before Kohberger was identified and arrested.

Brucato, who specializes in early psychotic illness, violent crime and mass or serial murder, believes Kohberger’s actions may have been influenced by notorious killers such as Ted Bundy.

Bundy, a rapist and necrophile, kidnapped, sexually assaulted, and murdered dozens of young women and girls across the US between 1974 and 1978.

Dr. Brucato believes Kohberger’s crimes had a sexual component, despite there being no evidence that he sexually assaulted any of the victims.

He said the killings may have been driven by a desire to imagine himself as “a powerful, virile figure” acting out a psychologically exciting scenario, possibly inspired by violent offenders he had studied.



“I have a very strong sense that Kohberger was so much like a serial offender rather than a mass murderer, where you do something once and either take your own life or get incarcerated and that’s the end of it.

“I think this is somebody who was sort of trying to master it and lost control the first time he did it.

“I think it’s possible that if he hadn’t been caught, [he] might have thought about doing it again.”

Prosecutors alleged Kohberger entered the King Road home intending to attack specific targets, but encountered more people than expected, including Ethan.

Digital forensics experts previously hired to examine the case have said Kohberger had researched Bundy, along with Danny Rolling, known as the Gainesville Ripper, and other serial killers.



His reported porn search history also included terms such as “raped,” “forced,” “passed out,” “sleeping” and “voyeur.”

Dr. Brucato believes Kohberger’s alleged fascination with notorious killers may reveal a desire for recognition and control — traits often seen in offenders who seek to build a notorious legacy.

While there is no public evidence that Kohberger stalked the victims in the traditional sense, prosecutors alleged he had visited the King Road home area before the murders, including cellphone data that placed his phone near the residence on multiple occasions.



Dr. Brucato said, “I was fascinated by the alibi that was given by Kohberger because he claimed that he was looking at the stars at Wawawai Park.

“First of all, on a psychological level, this notion of studying something that you can never touch the way an astronomer studies a star, but he can’t touch it.”

Dr. Brucato suggested Kohberger may have approached his victims in a similar way — observing and studying them from a distance.

He also pointed out that Wawawai Park is near the site where the remains of Joyce LePage, a Washington State University student whose 1971 disappearance has been considered by some as a possible Bundy case, were discovered.

Bundy was never charged or confirmed as LePage’s killer.



The documentary also explores the suggestion that Kohberger, who appeared to have no close friends and struggled with romantic relationships, may have identified with the incel movement (involuntary celibate).

The term refers to people who say they are unable to find a romantic or sexual partner, and some online incel communities have become known for promoting misogynistic and extremist views.

However, Dr. Brucato doesn’t believe Kohberger fully fits that profile.

“I had an issue with that from the beginning, because Kohberger, we know, was somebody who did have some date experiences,” he said. “He was just extremely weird on them.

“For example, the date that he reportedly had where he told the woman that he wanted to tickle her or that she had, you know, nice birthing hips.



“He was a sort of weird person, more than somebody who couldn’t get a date.

“And so I don’t think of him so much as an involuntary celibate.

“I think of him more as a person whose detached, peculiar mechanical quality and his desire to render relationships predictable, almost like a scientist thinks, weirded people out.”

Dr. Brucato also recalled how Kohberger had few contacts saved in his phone, which included impersonal labels like “girl I ran with” and “second girl I ran with.”

“I think that this is precisely the kind of person who would have been frustrated that he couldn’t make a science out of women and other people, and how to get people to like him and so forth,” he said.



Dr. Brucato believes Kohberger’s frustration at being unable to shape how others saw him may have contributed to his decision to become violent.

Bundy famously pleaded not guilty and represented himself during his trial, turning the courtroom into a stage as he fought to control his own narrative.

Dr. Brucato believes Kohberger has felt powerless since he was sentenced to life behind bars, and is the reason behind him suddenly seeking a trial.



He said, “If he is found guilty, what will he do? Probably write a book or start telling the story to manipulate the public that way.

“I think ultimately, one way or another, he always seems to be the puppet master.”

He went on, “I’m sure he feels extremely out of control in prison.

“I know he’s been upset over silly things like not getting the bananas he wants and things like that. And I’m sure he’s probably being picked on.”

But Kohberger will have a legal mountain to climb to try and get a trial.



Ada County District Judge Steven Hippler previously asked him in court, “I want to make sure that your plea is given voluntarily.

“I want to make sure that you actually committed the crimes to which you’re pleading guilty, because I don’t want you to plead guilty to a crime you didn’t commit.”

Hippler then asked, “Are you pleading guilty because you are guilty?” before reading out the murder charges tied to each victim.

Kohberger stood up and replied confidently, “Yes.”

Despite this, Kohberger’s request for new court-appointed counsel has been granted and a new filing shows he will be represented by public defender Gregory Rauch.



Kohberger filed a handwritten petition seeking to withdraw the guilty plea, which was entered to escape the death penalty.

He alleged that he was subjected to “coercion, disinformation, false promises” and the withholding of evidence he considered favorable to his defense.

Kohberger also claimed he was told that whether he was actually guilty was “not an important factor” when considering the deal.

Dr. Brucato worries about Kohberger getting pleasure out of having a trial.

“Let’s say he gets rid of all his attorneys and he wants to represent himself, that’s a little too Bundy-like for my taste,” he said.



“But then he’s allowed to have access to all kinds of evidence and think about the perversion of this person having crime scene photos and information and so forth.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“You almost wonder if, in some twisted way, there’s also an element of reliving [the murders] and then the family being dragged back and having to listen to it.”

To watch the full interview with Dr. Gary Brucato, visit The U.S. Sun’s YoTube channel.

News.title: Labour sparks ‘dumbing down’ row as Tories blast plans to make schools less academic
News.content:
LABOUR wants to dumb down classrooms while refusing to take the blame for the youth jobless crisis, Tories say.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell was criticised for saying the “one-size-fits-all” approach to learning has led to a million UK youngsters not being in training or in work.



She was attacked for taking a “fresh look” at what children were being taught as she tried to walk back reforms by Michael Gove, who ran her department in the 2010-14 coalition years.

Ministers are considering curriculum changes so teenagers take fewer GCSEs to stop them becoming stressed.



Ms Powell says schools have been stuck in a straitjacket of prioritising academic subjects for pupils.

She said: “We can no longer ignore that too many get left behind or are turned off by an education system that’s become too single-minded.”

She went on: “One million.

“That’s how many young people from the education system Michael Gove presided over who are now left outside education, not in employment and not training.”

“That is not a coincidence – it’s a consequence. It’s his legacy.”

But Laura Trott, the Tories’ Shadow Education Secretary, said: “Labour is using education as a smokescreen for its failures on tax and welfare.



“Labour is ignoring both recent history and the evidence.”

Tory peer Baroness Spielman, former head of schools watchdog Ofsted, said Ms Powell is trying to “deflect responsibility” from tax and minimum wage rises which have reduced job prospects for youngsters.

News.title: PC Harper’s ‘disgusted’ widow’s fury as hero cop’s killers WILL be released early despite PM’s pledge to keep them caged
News.content:
FURY erupted as it emerged two killers of hero PC Andrew Harper WILL still get early release.

Soft-justice plans to free Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole halfway through 13-year jail terms were paused last month.



But following a review, there will be no change to manslaughter cases, which means the two thugs could be out in months.

Furious widow Lissie Harper, 35, said: “This is disgusting.



“I’m beyond appalled and bristling with anger to hear Andrew’s killers are soon to be free.

“The level of disrespect the Government are showing to Andrew and other victims, and their loved ones such as me, is beyond contempt.”



“What abhorrent message does this send?

“How dare ministers say the killing of a police officer isn’t enough of a ‘sickening crime’ that deserves the stiffest of punishments.

“Andrew’s killers have shown no remorse.

“To release them early from their already pitiful sentences is an affront to justice.



“The Government and justice system have not just let me down, they have added insult to injury.

“This is an utter betrayal, one I will not be able to forgive or forget.”

In 2019 PC Harper, 28, was fatally dragged by a car driven by Henry Long, 18, as it towed a stolen quad bike.



Long, Bowers and Cole, then 17, were found guilty of manslaughter. The younger pair got 13 years’ jail, Long got 16 and will stay in prison.

Mr Burnham, who is taking a holiday after two weeks in No 10, launched an urgent review of Sir Keir’s plan which aimed to ease pressure on packed jails.

Early releases will begin in October.

Mr Burnham said: “I wanted to go even further as I know there will still be concerns about other offenders having their sentence shortened.

“But it’s not possible without the prison system reaching capacity and collapsing, which would put public safety at much greater risk.”



Tiff Lynch, National Chair of the Police Federation of England and Wales, branded the pairs release as “deeply disappointing” and “impossible to justify”.

“The Government has recognised that some offenders are simply too dangerous to benefit from early release, yet those convicted of killing police officers have been left off that list”, she said.

“We recently spoke out against the early release of the men responsible for PC Andrew Harper’s death, and officers, their families and the public will be asking why those who murder police officers can still qualify for reduced time behind bars.”



Freeing the two prisoners early “gravely risks undermining not only public safety but public confidence”, Lynch added.

She urged the government to “rethink” the decision in the face of “real distress” it will cause to bereaved families.

There will be an extra 14,000 new prison places by 2031 with the fastest prison building programme since the Victorian era.

Beefed-up community monitoring will help probation staff track movements and see random drug testing for 1,000 offenders every month.

The number of regions using chemical suppression to manage sexual offending will be doubled.



Tory leader Kemi Badenoch condemned the PM’s move, which adds to the 70,000 who have been released early under various Labour schemes.

She said: “Andy Burnham wants a round of applause for agreeing not to release rapists and child sex offenders.

“He’s not getting one. This is only a partial climbdown.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Killers, violent offenders, men who have terrorised their partners and more will all still walk out of prison in October.”

Shadow Justice Secretary Nick Timothy added: “Burnham must go further and block the early release of killers too.”

News.title: ‘Precious angel’, 5, who was ‘found dead in water’ after going missing is pictured as ‘devastated’ family pay tribute
News.content:
'UNIMAGINABLE LOSS' ‘Precious angel’, 5, who was ‘found dead in water’ after going missing is pictured as ‘devastated’ family pay tribute

A FIVE-year-old “precious angel” who was “found dead in the water” has been pictured as her devastated family pay a touching tribute.

Little Letti Cole was discovered dead in a body of water in Badsey, Worcestershire, on July 29 after a desperate search by the cops.



Many villagers came out to help with the search for the youngster, who her family described was their “most precious angel”.

The family have set up a GoFundMe page with the aim to create a memorial for the young girl.



Letti’s aunt Hayley Cole said: “On Wednesday evening, we lost our most precious angel in the most tragic circumstances.

“Our family is completely heartbroken, devastated, and still in shock. No family should ever have to go through such an unimaginable loss.



“The kindness, compassion, and support shown by the people of Badsey has restored my faith in humanity.

“I want to thank every single person who gave up their time and made every effort to help look for our beautiful Letti.

“Your love and support will never be forgotten.”

The idea to set up a memorial came from a person on Facebook who got in touch with the family and suggested the tribute.



So far, more than £7,000 has been raised.

Hayley said: “I thought perhaps people would donate a few hundred, but I never expected anything like this.

“These are people we don’t even know.

“I mean Badsey Butchers; as soon as I set it up, they donated £1,000.

“We are in complete shock at everyone’s kindness and grateful to everyone who gave up their time to help in the search.



“There is a memorial set up at Badsey Church, which is beautiful. Badsey is an amazing village.”

Writing on the GoFundMe page, Hayley added: “Please don’t feel under any obligation to donate.

“Your love, prayers, and support have already meant the world to our family.

“Thank you from the bottom of our hearts.”

West Mercia Police have said there was no third-party involvement in Letti’s tragic death and warned the public not to speculate online.



A spokesperson for the force said last week: “Sadly, the child was found unresponsive in a body of water, and a short time later was pronounced dead.

“There is no third-party involvement in the child’s death, and a report will be prepared for the coroner.

“This is an incredibly tragic incident.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We ask the public to avoid speculation online as this is incredibly distressing to the family, and we ask that their privacy is respected at such a difficult time.”

Anyone who wants to donate to the appeal can click here.

News.title: Moment clueless TikTokker calls notorious killer Kenneth Noye an ‘old-school gangster’ without realising who he is
News.content:
MURDERER Kenneth Noye boasted about his fitness to a clueless TikTokker who jokingly branded him an “old-school gangster” — despite not knowing he was.

The Brink’s-Mat villain chatted to Gymskin — real name Jack Smith — in a greasy spoon in Sevenoaks, Kent.



Footage shows the conversation turning to Essex, as Jack says he lives in Brentwood.

He briefly mentions “all the old Essex Boys” and someone says off camera: “Yeah, he (Noyes) knows them.”



Noye was associated with Pat Tate, one of the Essex Boys to die in a 1996 gangland killing.

Jack points at Noye and says: “Old school gangster.”



Noye, 79, gives a knowing grin in response.

The gangster, jailed for a 1996 road rage murder, says he has been visiting the café since the 1960s.

Jack asks if he works out, telling Noye: “You’re in good shape.”

He walks off, still unaware who he was speaking to, adding: “They were nice.”



After serving almost two decades behind bars, he was released on licence in 2019.

His criminal career has since been dramatised in the BBC series The Gold, which charted the Brink’s-Mat robbery, the laundering of the stolen bullion and the long-running investigation into those involved.

News.title: Toddler dies of heatstroke after being left in car on Canary Islands despite ‘extreme heat’ red weather warning
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

HORROR FIND Toddler dies of heatstroke after being left in car on Canary Islands despite ‘extreme heat’ red weather warning

A TODDLER has tragically died after being left inside a car in the Canary Islands amid a heatwave.

The 20-month-old boy had been in a motor in Fuerteventura but was rushed to hospital in a serious condition on Saturday after he was found.



He was then air-lifted to Gran Canaria for specialist care as doctors raced to save his life.

But the tot passed away in the early hours of Sunday morning at the Materno Infantil University Hospital in Las Palmas.



According to local reports the tot was left inside a vehicle, although no further details have been released.

The youngster’s nationality is not yet known.

The tragic death follows an “extreme heat” warning for the Canary Islands, where officials warned of “extraordinary danger.”

Gran Canaria was placed on red alert for the beginning of this week with temperatures forecast to exceed 40C.



Elsewhere in the archipelago Tenerife was put on orange alert, while Lanzarote, Fuerteventura, La Palma, La Gomera and El Hierro were placed on yellow.

It comes amid a series of record-breaking heatwaves across several other European holiday hotspots which have sparked wildfires and evacuations.

In early July another toddler died after being “forgotten” inside a car in Spain.

The boy, who was around age 2, was left in his dad’s car on an industrial estate in the Costa Dorada town of Valls near the east coast city of Tarragona.

Despite the best efforts of emergency services the young boy died following a cardiac arrest.



He was pronounced dead at the scene.

Two children aged two and four were found dead in their family’s car in the town of Carpentras in southeastern France in June during the ferocious heatwave.

The two young brothers, four-year-old Kassim Benouali and two-year-old Sadek, were among the first victims of France’s brutal heatwave.

By the end of June more than 5,700 excess deaths were recorded, according to The Guardian.

The two children climbed into the car without their mother knowing, according to prosecutors.



Police say that the extreme heat is “the leading theory” for their deaths.

The mother discovered her two children in her car at their home in Carpentras, southern France.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Temperatures inside a sealed car can reach up to 70C – easily enough to kill someone.

Tragically, the smaller size of children makes them more likely to die in extreme heat.

News.title: Chilling moment ‘Afghan wheels suitcase down street with body of Brit woman he killed inside before abandoning it’
News.content:
THIS is the horror moment a 26-year-old Afghan drags a suitcase with the body of a British woman stuffed inside through the streets of Greece, it is alleged.

Chilling CCTV footage reportedly shows Sharif Ahmadzai wheeling the large, black case in the centre of Athens.



Dressed in a black T-shirt and shorts and carrying a blue rucksack, Ahmadzai allegedly dumped the bag in an abandoned building in Kypseli before fleeing the scene.

The grim video reportedly shows Ahmadzai’s movements on July 16, two days before Elisabeth-Jane Ross’ body was discovered by a homeless man.



Ahmadzai has been charged with the murder of the 38-year-old, as well as robbery and illegal possession of a weapon.

The boxing champion ran a charity helping refugees in the Greek capital and is believed to have known Elisabeth through work.



He also had a key to the flat she was staying in – which was owned by his organisation, Love Every Nation Athens.

Ahmadzai travelled to Greece on a small boat in 2016, and later married US-born Alaina Hall in 2023.



Alaina allegedly reported her husband to cops after she became suspicious he was involved in Elisabeth’s death.

She said she woke up on the evening of July 15 to find him missing, but when she checked his shared location it showed him at Elisabeth’s apartment.

Ahmadzai had also given her 2,550 euros (£2,200) and a new iPhone 17 Pro, which she believed was bought using money stolen from Elisabeth’s bank accounts.



A Greek police source told The Times: “The testimony of the wife has been crucial and it would appear that she did not want to be part of the crime committed by her husband.

“Without her and CCTV evidence, we would not have been able to find this man.”

Ahmadzai’s website states his father, a military commander in Kabul, was shot dead in a Taliban ambush when he was four.

Five years later his older brother was kidnapped by the Taliban and when he was 15 the rest of his family was wiped out in a suicide car bomb, the website says.

Elisabeth regularly travelled to Greece to volunteer with NGOs, working with refugee centres including the One Heart organisation in Athens.



She arrived in the Greek capital on a flight from Edinburgh on June 26.

Police believe she was killed not far from where her body was found in the abandoned building in Kypseli.

Initial medical reports suggest Elisabeth died from asphyxiation, The Times reports, citing a case file.



Her phone was used to send messages and mislead her loved ones until her identity was made public on July 29.

Her dad, a lawyer from Edinburgh, said he received texts claiming she needed to be alone for a while up to two weeks after her death.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Foreign and Commonwealth Office said earlier: “Our thoughts are with Elisabeth’s family during this difficult time.

“We are providing consular support and are in contact with the local authorities.”

News.title: Number of pensioners in Britain’s prisons reaches record levels – including 28 aged in their 90s
News.content:
RECORD numbers of OAP inmates are in jails — including 28 in their 90s.

There were 456 in their 80s and 1,625 in their 70s in England and Wales last year.



The 2,109 total aged 70+ account for one in every 40 inmates.

It is more than double the 1,028 in 2014.



The stats suggest justice is catching up with those guilty of historical crimes.

The oldest lag is paedo Sidney Cooke, 99, suspected of up to 20 deaths in the 1970s and 1980s.



His parole bid failed last year.

Pop paedo Gary Glitter, 82, was jailed for historic sex abuse in 2015, freed on licence in 2023 but recalled after the Sun investigated his activities at a bail hostel.

Glitter, real name Paul Gadd, was charged with historical offences including unlawful sex with a girl under 13 last month after a fresh investigation.

Separate Home Office figures show police recorded more than 9,000 sex offences last year where the alleged crime took place more than 20 years earlier.



Campaigners say the ageing jail population is a major headache for prison bosses battling overcrowding, violence, staff shortages and crumbling Victorian jails.

The trend has also created pressure for more adapted cells, medical care, social care support and end-of-life planning inside jails.

At HMP Leyhill, Gloucs, inspectors said elderly and disabled inmates made up more than half the population.

It offers activities including indoor bowls.

The Ministry of Justice said: “It is absolutely right vile perpetrators of sexual abuse face the full force of the law and their victims receive justice — no matter how long ago the crime.”

News.title: Moment foolish driver tries 'frighteningly stupid' bid to dodge paying his Jaguar finance
News.content:
Moment foolish driver tries 'frighteningly stupid' bid to dodge paying his Jaguar finance

Nathan Owen, 33, told 999 call handlers his car was accelerating on its own, triggering a huge police response that saw motorways closed - but was later discovered to have faked the incident

View 3 Images Dashcam footage shows the driver racing down a busy motorway after claiming his car was out of control (Image: Merseyside Police)

Bizarre new footage shows the moment a man slams into the back of a police car after faking an emergency to try and have his car written off.

‌



Nathan Owen, 33, collided with a police car 31 times after he phoned emergency services to tell them his electric Jaguar was accelerating on its own and he could not stop, Liverpool Crown Court heard on Monday.

‌



He drove at speeds of up to 86mph on the M58, M57 and M62 in Merseyside for about 35 minutes, over a distance of about 38 miles, during the incident on March 6, 2024.

‌



It triggered a “significant“ police response as officers tried to stop what they were told was a runaway vehicle - but investigations later showed there was nothing wrong with the car, and that Owen was in full control the entire time.

He went on to plead guilty to dangerous driving and two counts of fraud, and sentenced to four years and three months in prison on Monday.

‌



Sentencing him, Judge Ian Unsworth KC said: “You set in train a course of conduct which caused a significant police traffic operation to be deployed, undoubted alarm to the public and very substantial loss and disruption to others.”

The judge said police officers placed themselves in danger because they believed they were dealing with a genuine emergency.

He added: “You, meanwhile, sought to profit from a lie.”

‌



View 3 Images Nathan Owen, 33, was sentenced to four years and three months in prison (Image: Merseyside Police)

Eric Lamb, prosecuting, said Owen, of Prestatyn, North Wales, had entered into a finance agreement in September 2023 for the Jaguar I-Pace.

He ran into “financial difficulties” and was in arrears with CA Auto Finance by March the following year with about £5,000 left to pay, the court heard.

‌



On the day of the incident, he called loan company Plata to ask if he would be able to borrow more on top of the £3,000 he had already loaned from them, but was told he could not.

Five minutes later, shortly after 2pm, he called 999 claiming his car would not brake and he had no control over the vehicle, which he said was accelerating.

Mr Lamb said: “In fact, his car was stationary at the time of that call.”

‌



View 3 Images He was found to have faked the incident to have the car written off (Image: Merseyside Police)

Police responded and the car, which was then travelling at speeds of up to 86mph, had to be boxed off by emergency service vehicles to keep other road users safe before it came to a stop on the M62 near Warrington, Cheshire.

However, investigations found there was no fault with the car, the court heard.

‌



Mr Lamb said: “He had fabricated the events in order to enable him to get rid of the vehicle.

“He had full control of the vehicle and with full control of the vehicle he travelled at excessive and extreme speeds.”

Motorways had to be closed as a result of the incident, the court heard.

‌



Footage of the police pursuit was played in court along with the audio from his 999 call, in which he was heard telling an operator he was “shaking” and the car had “gone crazy”.

When the car was eventually brought to a stop, the brake lights could be seen turning on.

Owen contacted the finance company 40 minutes after the incident.

‌



He was later paid £300 by The Sun and £500 by the Daily Mail for his story, the court heard.

In a statement, Murray Paul, from Jaguar Land Rover UK, said the firm had spent an extra £50 million in marketing to try and counter the publicity from the false allegations, which they said generated 180 pieces of adverse coverage.

Daniel Travers, defending, said Owen’s actions were “frighteningly stupid”.

‌



He said Owen, who had no previous convictions and came from a “successful, stable family”, had been described by his father as a Walter Mitty character who “lives in a fantasy world”.

He added: “He had grand ideas and things just went wrong.”

Owen pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and two counts of fraud in June. He was banned from driving for a period of five years after his release from custody.

Article continues below

Speaking after the sentencing, Merseyside Police's Detective Constable Michael Doyle said: “It was clear from our investigations that he was in full control of his vehicle throughout the duration of the incident.

“By his own admission there were workers on the hard shoulder of the motorway and he clearly put them and other road users in danger with his reckless actions.”

A charge of causing a public nuisance was ordered to lie on the file.

News.title: Thousands more students to get half price train tickets under Railcard extension
News.content:
Thousands more students to get half price train tickets under Railcard extension

In a boost to youngsters, ministers said the 16-17 Saver Railcards will be valid for a full year from the date of purchase, rather than expiring when the holder turns 18

View 2 Images Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander's department is trying to ease rail prices for youngsters (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News)

Thousands more students will be able to get half price train tickets under an extension of railcards eligibility.

‌



In a boost to youngsters, ministers have announced that the 16-17 Saver Railcards will be valid for a full year from the date of purchase, rather than expiring when the holder turns 18.

‌



Under the changes, which will come into force on August 17, young people will be able to access the railcard up until the day before their 19th Birthday. It means they can apply for a new annual railcard up to the day before their 18th Birthday and it will still be able to be used for the full 12 months.

‌



The 16-17 Saver Railcards, which can be accessed by those in education or training, cost £35 a year and provide 50% off rail tickets to support youngsters with their commute to school, college or work. A separate 16-25 Railcard offers a third off rail prices.

Previous rules meant over 70,000 students annually were left on average £175 worse off than their peers as they lost out on the maximum discount available, the Department for Transport said.

Andy Burnham to bring back £2 bus fare cap slashing travel costs for millions READ MORE :

Penkridge incident: Services cancelled and passengers scrambled off trains on tracks READ MORE :

View 2 Images Andy Burnham also announced a £2 bus fare cap to come into effect next year (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Transport costs are among barriers young people face when entering the workplace. It is hoped that expanding access to discounted rail fares, alongside the £2 bus fare cap recently announced by Andy Burnham from next year, will help more young people access opportunities.

Rail Minister Lord Peter Hendy said: "This kind of common-sense change is exactly what passengers should expect from the railway. I'm proud that this change will support young people and their families to lower the cost of travel at a critical time for teenagers, whether they’re pursuing further education, vocational pathways or getting their footing in the jobs market.

"Making travel fairer and more affordable is central to the vision for Great British Railways. By delivering simpler fares and putting passengers first, we're creating a railway that's easier to use, better value for money and focused on meeting the everyday needs of the people who rely on it."

‌



These changes come alongside a raft of fare and ticketing reforms ahead of the introduction of Great British Railways. Contactless options like Pay-As-You-Go and trials of innovative Digital ticketing are being expanded outside of London to Manchester, Yorkshire and the East and West Midlands.

And plans are underway to develop a GBR website and app which will act as a one-stop-shop for passengers to buy tickets, check train times and claim Delay Repay.

The revised rules bring the 16-17 Saver into line with other youth Railcards. Passengers are already able to buy the 26-30 Railcard the day before their 31st birthday and it remains valid for a full year.

Article continues below

Jacqueline Starr, Executive Chair & Chief Executive of the Rail Delivery Group, said: "By enabling customers who turn 18 during their academic year to receive a full year of savings from the date of purchase, we’re ensuring that young people can continue to benefit from 50% off rail travel throughout this important stage of their education. Whether it’s getting to school or college, seeing friends, or exploring new places, this change provides greater flexibility and more opportunities to make the most of their journeys."

Kaynat Ahmad, National Union of Students’ Vice President Further Education, said: “The 16-17 Saver is essential for young people reliant on trains to get to college, work or training. Allowing young people to access the savings past their 18th birthday will ease the financial pressures that commuting brings – whether that is money back into the pockets of young people and their families or preventing someone from being forced to drop out.

“Opportunity should never be defined by what is affordable but, too often, transport costs have been a barrier to education, employment and training for young people. With the extension of the 16-17 Saver, alongside the £2 capped Bus Fares, we welcome this Government’s commitment to addressing the challenges that young people are facing right now."

News.title: Andy Burnham announces rape and grooming offenders banned from early prison release scheme
News.content:
Andy Burnham announces rape and grooming offenders banned from early prison release scheme

It comes after the new Prime Minister Andy Burnham paused the early prisoner release scheme and ordered an urgent review in a dramatic intervention earlier this month

View 3 Images Andy Burnham ordered a review into the early prisoner release scheme (Image: Jack Taylor/Reuters Pool via AP)

Andy Burnham has announced anyone found guilty of rape, serious child sexual offences and grooming will be blocked from being released early from prison under a sentencing shake-up.

‌



The new Prime Minister, who paused an early release scheme earlier this month, admitted he wanted to go even further and ban other offenders from having their time in prison shortened.

‌



But he said it would not be possible without the crisis-hit prison system collapsing.

‌



Under the new Sentencing Act - originally set to come into force in September - some 6,000 criminals were due to be released under the programme.

It was designed by the Labour government to ease the prison overcrowding crisis left behind by the Tories and amid fears jails could run out of spaces completely.

Andy Burnham announces 'pause' on early prisoner release scheme READ MORE :

Probation service to get real-time tag data and issue random drug tests in crime crackdown READ MORE :

View 3 Images The PM is pictured speaking to reporters (Image: Jack Taylor/PA Wire)

‌



But in his first week in power, Mr Burnham paused the scheme and ordered an urgent review to “minimise risks to the public”. On Monday evening the PM said he had listened to victims’ concerns as he announced changes to the scheme.

He said in a statement: “I fully understand the anger, anxiety and distress that’s been caused. I’ve heard that loud and clear. That’s why we’re making significant changes: offenders who have been sentenced for rape, serious child sex offences and other grooming offences will be excluded from the changes.”

He added: “I want to be honest - I wanted to go even further as I know there will still be concerns about other offenders having their sentence shortened. But it’s not possible without the prison system reaching capacity and collapsing, which would put public safety at much greater risk.

‌



“That’s why we will also be introducing much tougher community measures. There will be a presumption that all offenders are tagged, longer periods of supervision and tough new rules, including restriction zones for offenders.”

“As a country, we haven’t invested in the prison estate when we should have, going back over a decade. This has created an unacceptable situation, with our adult male prisons now at 98 per cent capacity.

“For too long, the problems facing our prison system have been ignored – and it’s the victims who have been paying the price. That is not good enough. My government will deliver the fastest prison building programme since the Victorian era and do what’s necessary to fix the prison crisis.”

‌



View 3 Images Lissie Harper, wife of killed police officer PC Andrew Harper, said the early release of prisoners was 'deplorable' (Image: Lissie Harper)

The review was ordered amid outcry over the potential release of two of PC Andrew Harper’s killers. The hero police officer's widow, Lissie Harper, said it was "deplorable" that Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers could be released within months.

Both were passengers in a car that dragged PC Harper, 28, for more than a mile down a country road as he responded to a burglary report. Cole and Bowers were both jailed for 13 years after being convicted for manslaughter in 2020.

‌



It is understood neither will be impacted by the latest exemptions announced on Monday evening.

Driver Henry Long did not qualify for early release under the government's criteria.

Changes in the Sentencing Act mean that prisoners on standard determined sentences can be released after serving a third of their term - instead of 40% of their sentence. Those released early would be subject to strict conditions or face recall to prison, the government has previously said. Measures would include curfews and electronic tagging.

‌



Those found by a court to be the most dangerous or serving a life sentence were already banned from the scheme.

Alex Norris, who recently replaced David Lammy as Justice Secretary, added: “The Prime Minister and I have reviewed these reforms, listened to the concerns and gone further to protect victims

“These are decisions no minister would ever want to take but it is right these sickening crimes are excluded from these reforms. Victims will also have access to better support and reassurance that offenders leaving prison face tougher supervision and punishment.”

Article continues below

The government also announced that wider releases from prison under the Sentencing Act would be delayed from September to October. There will also be random drugs testing for 1,000 offenders released every month, and alerts warning offenders if they risk breaching an exclusion zone.

News.title: Girl, five, found dead in water pictured as family pay tribute to 'precious angel'
News.content:
Girl, five, found dead in water pictured as family pay tribute to 'precious angel'

Letti Cole had been reported missing from Badsey, a village in Worcestershire - this is a breaking story

View Image Letti Cole was five years old (Image: GoFundMe)

A five-year-old girl who was found unresponsive in water has been pictured.

‌



Letti Cole was reported missing from Badsey, a village in Worcestershire, on Wednesday evening. Despite emergency services rushing to the scene, including an air ambulance, Letti was pronounced dead.

‌



No third party was involved in her death, West Mercia Police said. The force asked people not to speculate online about the incident.

‌



A fundraising page has now been launched to create a memorial for the young girl as her family deals with the "unimaginable loss". Hayley Newton, the organiser of the page, wrote: "On Wednesday evening, we lost our most precious angel in the most tragic circumstances.

"Our family is completely heartbroken, devastated, and still in shock. No family should ever have to go through such an unimaginable loss.

"The kindness, compassion, and support shown by the people of Badsey has restored my faith in humanity. I want to thank every single person who gave up their time and made every effort to help look for our beautiful Letti. Your love and support will never be forgotten."

‌



Ms Newton explained that the "beautiful and thoughtful" idea for a memorial was suggested by one of the volunteers who helped look for the "precious girl".

So far, the fundraiser has received more than £7,300 from 409 donations, taking it close to its £8,000 goal. A spokesperson for West Mercia Police previously said a report was going to be prepared for the coroner, who will establish the exact circumstances of the death.

The force said: "Officers were called to a report of a missing child in Badsey yesterday evening (Wednesday 29 July). Sadly, the child was found unresponsive in a body of water, and a short time later was pronounced dead.

‌



"There is no third-party involvement in the child's death, and a report will be prepared for the coroner. This is an incredibly tragic incident.

"We ask the public to avoid speculation online as this is incredibly distressing to the family and we ask that their privacy is respected at such a difficult time."

West Midlands Ambulance Service were called to the area at 6.50pm and dispatched an ambulance, two paramedic officers and the Midlands Air Ambulance Critical Care Car. A West Midlands Ambulance Service spokesperson said: "On arrival we discovered one patient, a young child.

Article continues below

"Ambulance staff and police worked quickly to treat the patient, but sadly, it became apparent nothing could be done to save them and they were confirmed dead at the scene."

The Mirror has launched the Save Lives For Sam water safety campaign to tackle the UK's growing drowning crisis. Backed by MPs, Olympic champions, national water safety organisations and bereaved families, the campaign is calling for urgent action to make our waters safer.

That includes compulsory water safety lessons in schools, a nationwide public awareness campaign, better lifesaving equipment at high-risk waterways, the introduction of Sam's Law, and a dedicated Minister for Water Safety. Find out more about the campaign and how you can support it here.

News.title: UK wildfires: Flames rage near Shrewsbury as major incident also declared in Wales
News.content:
Firefighters are battling wildfires in Shropshire and South Wales, with crews declaring a major incident as they tackle the blaze in the Rhondda Valley

Firefighters in Shropshire are tackling a large blaze near a historic site, while crews in South Wales have declared a major incident as they battle a wildfire close to homes.

The blaze at Battlefield Heritage Park, a country park north of Shrewsbury, broke out on Monday afternoon. It is understood to be just a few fields away from the site associated with the 1403 Battle of Shrewsbury, fought between King Henry IV and a rebel army led by Henry "Harry Hotspur" Percy.

Meanwhile, crews from South Wales Fire and Rescue Service are battling a wildfire in the Llanwonno area of Rhondda Cynon Taf. The blaze, which began on Saturday afternoon, has already spread across around 150 hectares - roughly the size of 210 football pitches.

No homes have been evacuated, but Rhondda Cynon Taf Council said a rest centre has been set up at a local sports centre for residents affected by smoke and poor air quality from the fire.

News.title: Astonishing moment ram-raiding thieves drag cash machine away in a matter of seconds
News.content:
Astonishing moment ram-raiding thieves drag cash machine away in a matter of seconds

The Metropolitan Police is investigating the footage, which shows brazen thieves tow the cash machine away after attaching it to a car in Teddington, southwest London

Ram-raiding thieves try to break into cash machine with hammer - before towing ATM out of the ground

Shocking new footage shows the moment a band of ram-raiding thieves tow away a cash machine after trying to smash through it with a hammer.

‌



The brazen theft in Teddington, southwest London, was captured by a young woman on her mobile phone early on Wednesday morning, with police now hunting four men after seizing an abandoned vehicle.

‌



In CCTV footage, one man dressed in a black top, jeans, and a beanie hat, appears to use a hammer to try to smash the back of the machine.

‌



A few seconds later, a man is seen reversing from the busy road onto the pavement close to the standalone ATM, which was on the pavement outside a Londis.

View 2 Images One of the men attempted to smash into the cash machine with a hammer before it was taken by thieves (Image: / SWNS)

Man accused of killing Brit woman and stuffing body in suitcase is professional boxer READ MORE :

The same man then works with an accomplice to attach leads to the machine, after taking them from the boot of the car.

‌



A few seconds later, the car pulls away at speed, tearing the entire cash machine from its mounting on the pavement and onto the tarmac, sending sparks flying in its wake.

One of the men remains at the scene, standing over the empty space with a hammer in his hands.

View 2 Images Police said they are looking for four men in connection with the incident (Image: / SWNS)

‌



A local resident said: “I couldn’t really understand what had happened because I saw the machine lying on its side on the pavement on Tuesday morning and I assumed someone had crashed into it, not tried to take it away.”

No one has been arrested, though police have seized an abandoned vehicle believed to be connected with the incident.

A spokesperson from the Metropolitan Police said: “Police are investigating the theft of a cash machine from the outside a shop in Kingston Road, Teddington at 00:53hrs on Wednesday, 29 July.

Article continues below

“Although no arrests have been made at this stage, an abandoned vehicle has been seized in connection with the incident, and officers continue to work at pace to identify the four men believed to be involved.

“Anyone with information is asked to contact police on 101, quoting 302/29JUL.

“Anonymous reports can be shared via Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 using the same reference number.”

News.title: Children at nursery where man drove off with wrong child 'put at significant risk of harm'
News.content:
Children at nursery where man drove off with wrong child 'put at significant risk of harm'

Jody Riley, from Merseyside, will now take care of her daughter Rosie full-time after the toddler was handed to the wrong grandad by staff at Kids Planet Crosby

View 2 Images Kids Planet Crosby (Image: Google Maps)

Staff at a Merseyside nursery where a grandad was given the wrong child and drove away are not consistently keeping children safe, Ofsted have found.

‌



An inspection from the education watchdog, found that safeguarding standards are not met at Kids Planet Crosby. The nursery referred itself to the watchdog after a two-year-old was handed to the wrong grandad on June 10.

‌



Jody Riley, 37 and from Formby, Merseyside, previously told the Liverpool ECHO that she received a call from the nursery saying her daughter Rosie was picked up by another child's grandfather. Two-year-old Rosie was driven away for at least 10 minutes before the man noticed the mistake and returned her to the nursery.

‌



The mother explained she was not going to take her daughter to Kids Planet Crosby again, adding she would be looking after her child full-time. An Ofsted inspection followed as a result with the findings published today, Liverpool ECHO reports.

View 2 Images Jody Riley pictured with her daughter, Rosie (Image: Liverpool Echo)

Two areas that require improvement are "children's welfare and wellbeing" and "leadership and governance", inspectors found. The report states: "Leaders have not ensured that safeguarding procedures are implemented consistently to keep children safe.

‌



"Weaknesses in staff deployment, supervision and collection procedures place children at significant risk of harm. As a result, children do not consistently benefit from the robust systems needed to protect their safety.

"During the inspection, children's privacy was not consistently considered during toileting and intimate care. The provider took immediate action to address this. However, children do not consistently experience the safe and well-organised environment they deserve."

Despite the "weaknesses", Ofsted stated that children develop warm and secure relationships with staff members, who know the kids' care routines, including sleeping, feeding and emotional needs, well. The report reads: "These positive aspects do not outweigh the significant weaknesses in the promotion of children's welfare and wellbeing."

‌



Regarding safeguarding, inspectors explained that leaders have not ensured that there is "an open and positive culture" around this. The report states: "This puts children at significant risk of harm.

"Weaknesses in the implementation of safeguarding policies and procedures mean children are not consistently kept safe. Staffing arrangements do not always assure children's safety and risk assessment arrangements are not sufficiently effective in identifying, managing and reducing known risks.

"As a result, children are exposed to unnecessary risk and their safety and welfare are not consistently promoted." It added: "Following a significant safeguarding incident, leaders took prompt action to strengthen safeguarding arrangements.

‌



"They improved collection procedures and restricted access to nursery rooms to reduce the risk of a similar incident occurring again. Furthermore, during the inspection, leaders took immediate action to ensure children's privacy is consistently maintained during toileting and intimate care.

"However, leaders cannot demonstrate that safeguarding arrangements consistently protect children from harm." The nursery failed to meet safeguarding standards and the requirements of the compulsory or voluntary part of the Childcare Register.

Due to this, the watchdog now plans to take enforcement action. The report said a Welfare Requirements Notice requiring the provider to undertake a four-point action plan had an assigned completion date of July 20, 2026.

‌



Across the four other areas inspected by Ofsted, which included achievement, behaviour, curriculum and inclusion, the nursery achieved expected standard. A spokesperson for Kids Planet said: "We remain deeply sorry for the serious safeguarding incident at Kids Planet Crosby. This was an isolated and unprecedented incident, caused by human error when relevant and well established procedures were not followed.

"We cooperated fully with the relevant authorities and police, all of whom have concluded their independent investigations and are satisfied the matter was handled appropriately. We also immediately reviewed collection procedures and security arrangements and carried out an extensive internal investigation.

"We take Ofsted’s findings extremely seriously and have implemented a comprehensive action plan covering safeguarding, training, supervision, staffing and risk assessments. Ofsted returned on 22 July to review this work, with its outcome summary to follow.

Article continues below

"Ofsted’s report recognises our prompt response to the incident while also highlighting the setting’s strengths, including children’s progress, warm relationships with staff, inclusive practice and strong partnerships with parents and professionals.

"Children’s safety and wellbeing remain, and will always remain, our absolute priority. We are committed to learning fully from this incident and ensuring that the improvements made are rigorously and consistently upheld."

News.title: DARREN LEWIS: 'Stop and search bias is leaving kids with lasting pain'
News.content:
Scrolling through the news on my break last week, I came across some footage that has stayed on my mind. It was of a bewildered young Black boy, who looked no older than 10 or 11, forced to lie face down by a Metropolitan Police officer who’d handcuffed him ­unnecessarily in East London.

The child was found to be entirely innocent but not before a trauma all too often dismissed by the advocates of stop and search targeting Black young men.

“What have I done? Why am I being arrested?” he pleaded with a voice yet to break, his hands locked behind his back and an officer crouched over him.

Witnesses claim the youngster had been among a group of white and Black kids play-fighting who’d dispersed at the sight of the officers approaching. The kind of harmless thing lots of mischievous young boys have done over the years.

‌



View 2 Images Darren says: "The data shows clearly that even as youngsters, Black people are seen by police as more of a threat." (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

“You’re not being arrested, you’re being detained,” said the officer who was handcuffing him.

So why shackle him? If the kid was simply being given “words of advice about his behaviour” as the Met Police claim, why embarrass and dehumanise him in order to do so?

Here’s where the term adultification bias comes into play. It describes the practice of harshly treating young boys and girls as though they are adults. A breach of child safeguarding and equalities legislation and guidance.

‌



In policing, adultification disproportionately affects Black ­children who are perceived as less vulnerable, and more culpable, than their white peers.

It resurfaced a few years ago with the horrendous case of Child Q, the 15-year-old Black schoolgirl ­wrongfully and traumatically ­strip-searched while menstruating by Metropolitan Police officers at her school in East London.

Statistics reveal Black children are up to eight times more likely to be strip-searched, face higher rates of stop-and-search and experience inflated risk assessments in the justice system – where their chance of ­reoffending is weighed up. In other words, the data shows clearly that even as youngsters, Black people are seen by police as more of a threat.

Mercifully last week, a white man passing by stopped to intervene. Widely praised for his role in ­de-escalating the incident, which went viral on social media, the man warned the officer repeatedly: “Be gentle with him, he’s a child.”

‌



Yet to be identified, the man calmed the distressed youngster down, comforted him and remained on the scene to, in effect, act in loco parentis.

A Met Police statement later claimed the officers on patrol had spotted “a group fighting” and that “from a distance it was not possible to tell how old they were”. The statement continued: “On noticing the police officers, the group ran from the area and dispersed, discarding items – including a balaclava – as they did so.

“Officers pursued two of the group on foot and detained one boy…[and] a stop and search was carried out.” Now, again. Why handcuff him? Why not just question him with the man who’d ­advocated for him as a witness?

“That decision [to stop and search] wasn’t based on race, [one] other boy just got away from a second officer,” said the statement. “The stop and search was done respectfully and officers fully explained why they had chased and stopped the boy.”

‌



So, “we humiliated and dehumanised him unnecessarily – but we did it respectfully”. As the Met admit themselves: “No offences were identified and all involved were given words of advice around their behaviour.”

We obviously support the police position of not wanting the public intimidated. But there has to be a better way.

Because proponents of the ­handcuff-first-ask-questions-later approach couldn’t care less about the lasting effects on those Black boys and girls, more often than not, found ­innocent. And those children matter. Their self-esteem matters. Their mental health matters. Their dignity matters.

News.title: Rapists and child sex offenders to be barred from early release scheme
News.content:
Prisoners who committed rape, grooming, and serious child sex offences will be excluded from the forthcoming early release scheme for England and Wales, the government has said.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham paused plans to release some prisoners in September as part of a bid to stop unprecedented prison overcrowding after backlash from survivors and victims. The scheme will now restart in October.

Burnham said he "wanted to go even further", but that would not possible without the prison system collapsing and putting the public "at much greater risk".

Lissie Harper, the widow of police officer Andrew Harper, said it was "disgusting" that his killers could be eligible for early release.

PC Harper, 28, was killed in 2019 when he was dragged by a car down a country road as three teenagers fled the scene of the quad bike theft in Berkshire.

His family previously said they had received a letter from the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) confirming the offenders who killed the officer could be included in the scheme.

Burnham had paused the scheme on 23 July to conduct an urgent review.

In a statement announcing the changes on Monday, he said: "I fully understand the anger, anxiety and distress that's been caused. I've heard that loud and clear."

But Lissie Harper said that she was "beyond appalled and bristling with anger to hear the Andrew's killers are soon to be free to roam the streets".

Under the government's changes, it also announced an extra Â£10 million will go to frontline victim support services, including a new national helpline.

The Sentencing Act was amended in January, with the eligibility for early release based on the length of fixed sentence, rather than the type of offence.

The act already excluded some of the most serious and dangerous offenders, such as murderers serving life sentences or those on extended sentences.

Under Burnham's announced changes, rape and child sexual offences will now also be excluded.

The government said this move does not require changes to the existing legislation before October, though it may make amendments in the future to exclude certain offenders from being released.

Offenders of other crimes serving longer sentences of four years or more will be eligible for release halfway through their sentences rather than two-thirds as had previously been the case.

Those serving less serious sentences could be freed after a third of their time, rather than half.

The changes are due to be phased in, beginning with prisoners serving sentences of less than 575 days, going up to inmates jailed for 12 years or more being eligible for early release in June 2027.

The "presumption" will be that offenders are tagged and will face longer periods of supervision and tough new rules including "restriction zones", Burnham said.

The number of individuals released each time will depend on the make-up of the prison population, which the government says will evolve between now and implementation.

Reacting to the announcement, a prison officer told the BBC that they were "creaking at the seams" and that "delaying the releases until October could mean we simply run out of space".

A probation officer said it is "not clear there's anything actually new here in terms of how probation staff are going to manage people being released earlier".

Separately, those who serve the full sentence and are convicted of rape or serious child sex offences will face stronger surveillance after leaving prison, the government said.

This includes 12 months of GPS monitoring and strengthened community supervision.

Calling the announcement a "U-turn", Shadow Justice Secretary Nick Timothy said it "doesn't go far enough".

"Some child sex offenders and killers ... will still be released early. And the trauma of victims being told their abusers may be released can't be undone," he said.

Domestic Abuse Commissioner Dame Nicole Jacobs criticised the decision to not exclude domestic abuse perpetrators.

"It is critical that no abuser is released in October unless I am confident that victims' safety is not being compromised," she said.

News.title: France hits out at Reform UK plan to return migrants using Navy
News.content:
France has hit out at a Reform UK plan to return migrant boats using the Navy, saying the proposals would violate its sovereignty and breach international law.

Nigel Farage's party announced that if it was in power it would intercept boats crossing the English Channel and return migrants to French ports, even if France disagreed.

Opposition parties branded the plan unworkable, while a Labour minister said it would lead to "a lot of time arguing with France" instead of "actually getting to grips with the problem".

Responding to the French government, a Reform spokesperson said: "We will always stand up for British interests and protect our people, whether Emmanuel Macron likes it or not."

The spokesperson added: "Humanitarian missions do not violate maritime or international law."

Under the plans, which Reform said it would bring in if it entered government after the next election, military-crewed inflatable boats deployed from 10 Navy patrol vessels would be used to "come alongside" migrant boats crossing the English Channel.

Border Force officers and police stationed onboard would be tasked with arresting people in the boats, and they would then be returned to France or Belgium by Navy personnel or Marines.

The party said returns operations would be conducted by military personnel with Border Force officers on hand in case of "non-compliance", with a Bay Class landing ship providing "detention capacity at sea" for up to 700 people.

Speaking at a news conference on Monday, Reform's home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf said the party would aim to get agreement to disembark arrested migrants at French ports.

He added: "If the Elysee Palace refuses, make no mistake - His Majesty's Royal Marines will disembark them safely on the very shore they left that morning".

Speaking alongside him, Farage played down the prospect of a diplomatic confrontation with the French, claiming that attitudes in France towards the idea were "softening".

But in a statement issued later on Monday, the French interior ministry said: "This would constitute a violation of French sovereignty, as well as a violation of the law of the sea and international law."

A spokesperson for the department added that measures agreed with the UK, as well as "operations deployed at the local level", had already led to a reduction in crossings so far this year compared to the same period in 2025.

News.title: West Ham co-owner David Sullivan advised to stay away from home matches
News.content:
The recommendation from London Stadium comes after a joint investigation by BBC Panorama and The Times revealed that seven women have accused Sullivan of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour. He has categorically denied the allegations.

He stood down as joint chairman of the club shortly before the investigation was broadcast, saying he wanted to focus on fighting what he called "factually incorrect and entirely false, decades-old allegations concerning my personal life". He remains the club's largest shareholder.

The investigation also revealed that Sullivan has been banned from contact with West Ham's women's and youth teams for three years due to safeguarding concerns. London Stadium were unaware of the restrictions until the BBC's report.

Sullivan was banned after a historic allegation about his conduct was raised with the Football Association in 2023. He has previously said the allegation was false and that because he had never met any academy or women's team players "1-2-1" during his 16 years at the club, he accepted what he saw as a "meaningless restrictionâ¦for a quiet life".

West Ham were relegated from the Premier League in May and are due to play their first home game of the new season, a Carabao Cup match against Portsmouth, on Saturday.

Sullivan was a regular attendee at the London Stadium last season, where he was photographed watching games from the directors' box.

A spokesperson for London Stadium, the operator of the publicly owned venue, said that "following media reports at the end of the season regarding a safeguarding matter being managed by the club, London Stadium sought further information to ensure it could fulfil its own safeguarding responsibilities".

It said that West Ham had told it that the "matter was investigated and that the club does not consider there to be an ongoing safeguarding risk associated with Mr Sullivan attending the stadium".

However it said that, despite this, it had recommended the businessman stay away from games because of the "potential for demonstrations and anti-social behaviour by some spectators".

Sullivan has previously faced criticism from fans over his running of the club, with thousands joining a protest in September last year calling for his departure.

West Ham declined to comment. It is understood that the club intends to work with the stadium operators to facilitate Sullivan's attendance at games.

Sullivan has not responded to a request for comment.

Meanwhile, presenter Tony Livesey left BBC Radio 5 Live on Monday after 16 years at the station, the corporation announced.

Livesey stepped back from his weekday late night talk show in June, following allegations made against Sullivan. He had previously worked as editor-in-chief of Sullivan's Daily and Sunday Sport publications.

One alleged victim said that Livesey had arranged a meeting between her and Sullivan in 1999.

Livesey said he had "no recollection" of introducing the young woman to Sullivan and that it was "not part" of his job to do so.

He added that he had "great sympathy for a woman who may have become a victim", but rejected any suggestion that he had played "any role whatsoever in that scenario" and said he found the allegation "abhorrent".

News.title: Inside city gripped by deadly protests in Pakistan-administered Kashmir
News.content:
Dozens of people have been killed in clashes between security officials and protesters across Pakistan-administered Kashmir over the last two months, following a crackdown that left the city of Rawalakot mostly sealed off from the world.

Leading the demonstrations is the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), which says it is protesting for rights including healthcare and electricity.

Authorities say the JAAC is trying to disrupt the current regional elections, that the group is armed, and will not be allowed to leave Rawalakot.

The JAAC was banned in June; they have been labelled foreign-funded terrorists by the government. They reject this characterisation, saying they are peaceful and - though funded from the Pakistan-administered Kashmir community abroad - not sponsored by India.

The BBC is the first media to gain access to the city and speak to people on the ground about what is going on at the heart of the protests. Pakistan correspondent Caroline Davies reports from Islamabad.

News.title: Son who kept mum's body in freezer for years collected £78k of her benefits
News.content:
The court heard Phillips moved downstairs to sleep next to his mother's body. At times he would open the freezer and hold her hand.

Sylvia Phillips had 26 appointments with her local GP practice in 2021, and six in 2022, after which there was no further contact.

The court heard she was last seen in A&E on 24 September 2022 and her local GP made a house call on 26 September but her son continued to pick up her prescriptions.

Sylvia Phillips was invited to a review by the practice, but her son said she would not come to the surgery and she did not need the blood tests.

Christopher Phillips received a total of Â£78,190.92 in state pension, pensions credit, attendance allowance, winter fuel payments, cost-of-living payments and housing benefit payments, which would have ceased had the death been reported.

He had been her primary carer since 2008, and the court heard he had resigned from his job in late 2022 when her health declined further. The pair were described as "somewhat isolated".

Ruth Smith, defending, said Phillips had told police: "I basically didn't want to let her go."

She added: "He described talking to her as if she was still aliveâ¦ Sitting next to her, talking to her about television programmes, Coronation Street, the horse racing, just as they always did," she said, adding that he was a "vulnerable individual".

Phillips sobbed in the dock as Smith said her client was "extremely close to his mother" and was in "extreme grief" following her death.

She said he showed a "lack of acceptance" about her passing and "had almost created a false narrative that she was still alive".

Sentencing Phillips to two years and four months - of which he will spend 40% in custody and the rest on licence - Judge Lloyd-Clarke said he had "deliberately concealed" his mother's death and "took steps to give the impression that she was still alive".

"You continued to collect her prescription and lied to medical professionals and eventually the police," Lloyd-Clarke added.

"Rather than notify the authorities and make arrangements for her lawful burial, you purchased a chest freezer on March 10th and concealed her body within it," she said.

Lloyd-Clarke added that a timescale for confiscation proceedings would follow.

News.title: X Factor finalist denies murdering influencer by running her over with car
News.content:
A former X Factor finalist has denied murdering a social media influencer by running her over with a car in central London.

Gabrielle Carrington of Manchester, allegedly struck Klaudia Zakrzewska outside Inca nightclub in Argyll Street, Soho, at 04:30 BST on 19 April.

The 29-year-old appeared at the Old Bailey by video link from Bronzefield prison to deny the charge. She had been initially charged with attempted murder but that was changed to murder after Zakrzewska died from her injuries six days later.

Carrington, who was not represented in court by a barrister, also denied a second charge of causing grievous bodily harm with intent to security guard Anoush Chyche.

The defendant was not asked to enter a plea to a third charge of driving with excess alcohol.

Family members of the victims shook their heads as the accused read out her pleas.

Judge Sarah Whitehouse KC confirmed the trial would be held at the same court from 5 January.

Carrington appeared emotional on the video link, wiping tears from her face throughout the hearing and was placed into custody afterwards.

News.title: Newspaper columnist and broadcaster Rod Liddle dies aged 66
News.content:
Newspaper columnist and broadcaster Rod Liddle has died aged 66 after a short illness.

Liddle's children paid tribute to their father, who they described as their guide "on how to live an extraordinary life", while CEO of News UK, Rebekah Brooks, called him "an inimitable journalistic force."

Brooks added that "he challenged conventional thinking and left an indelible mark on British journalism."

Liddle, a columnist for the Sun and the Sunday Times, died at The James Cook University Hospital in Middlesbrough on Sunday evening.

A former editor of BBC Radio 4's flagship Today programme, he also had a weekly column in the Spectator, as well as a show on Times Radio.

His children, Wilder, Tyler and Emmy, said: "We're all very saddened and shocked at the sudden passing of our wonderful father.

"He raised us much as you might imagine, to be inquisitive, brave and always humorous.

"Even in hospital in the last few weeks, he consistently held the room and never let the awful situation show.

"He has left a legacy that we are all incredibly proud of, he will always be our guide on how to live an extraordinary life."

News.title: Farage says he discussed return to politics months before general election
News.content:
Nigel Farage has told the BBC he discussed the "potential liabilities" of returning to politics before the 2024 general election.

It comes after The Sunday Times, external reported Farage had negotiated a deal in March and April 2024 with then-Reform leader Richard Tice to return to lead the party.

Farage confirmed he spoke with Tice in spring 2024 to scope out what would happen to Reform's finances if he returned but said it "wasn't a deal, it wasn't an agreement", adding that talks came "quite some time after" he received a Â£5m gift from a billionaire donor.

Labour said Farage's remarks had "blown a gaping hole" in his argument for not declaring the gift after becoming an MP in July 2024.

Farage has repeatedly argued the Â£5m from British cryptocurrency investor Christopher Harborne was an "unconditional gift", was intended for his personal security, "wasn't political in any sense at all" and he was not an MP when he received it.

Reform's opponents have said he should have declared it in the MPs' register of interests when he was elected to Parliament.

The Parliamentary Standards Commissioner was investigating whether Farage broke the rules, but the process was suspended when he stood down as Clacton MP last month to force a by-election.

Farage said he took this decision as the "people of Clacton should be the judges of my actions". The investigation will be resumed if Farage wins the by-election, which is taking place on 13 August.

Farage left frontline politics in 2021 and embarked on a broadcasting career.

In May 2024, Farage was serving as Reform's honorary president but announced he would not be standing as a candidate in the general election in July of that year.

He reversed this position at the beginning of June and took over the leadership of the party.

Appearing at a press conference on Monday, Farage was asked if he had negotiated a deal on what would happen to Reform's finances if he came back as leader - in light of the report in The Sunday Times.

He replied: "I had no intention of returning to politics or as leader of Reform, but in the spring of that year I did talk to Richard Tice about what the liabilities would be if I was to come back to that position.

"And you'd be a bit of a mug, wouldn't you, to walk into a job and not find out what the potential liabilities were, and they were substantial.

"But without Richard, the party wouldn't have even survived, so that was useful for me to know. But it wasn't a deal, it wasn't an agreement, it was subject to if I came back."

He added: "If you want clarification on this, that came quite some time after the gift, which is perhaps the important point."

Bridget Phillipson, chair of the Labour Party, said: "Nigel Farage has blown a gaping hole in his excuse for why his secret Â£5m 'gift' from a crypto billionaire did not need to be declared."

The Commons code of conduct states that new MPs "must register all their current financial interests, and any registrable benefits (other than earnings) received in the 12 months before their election within one month of their election".

The rules say "purely personal gifts or benefits" from family or commercial loans would not normally have to be registered.

The rules also say "both the possible motive of the giver and the use to which the gift is to be put should be considered", adding "if there is any doubt, the benefit should be registered".

A full list of the candidates standing in the Clacton by-election can be found here.

News.title: Woman has pioneering womb surgery to fix 'miracle' baby with intestines outside its body
News.content:
Doctors have used ground-breaking surgery on an unborn baby to successfully correct a birth defect while he was still inside the womb.

His mother, Maisie Savage, from London, was operated on by doctors in the US while she was 26 weeks pregnant.

Baby Theo, who is now five months old and thriving, had gastroschisis, where the belly button does not develop properly, causing the intestines to grow externally.

Doctors partially exposed his mother's womb and then gently pushed his organs back inside his abdomen using keyhole surgery.

He was the third baby in the world to benefit from the first-of-its-kind clinical trial.

Maisie, 29, and Theo's father, Josh French, 36, both teachers, say they are incredibly relieved by the success of the pioneering surgery.

"He's a little miracle, isn't he?" Maisie told BBC News.

But they both know things could have been very different.

The serious birth defect affects one in 3,000 UK babies each year. In the best-case scenarios, babies can require weeks in intensive care and nutritional feeding through a tube or IV and corrective surgery.

For the most complex cases, like Theo's, outcomes are far more serious with up to six months in neonatal intensive care, multiple surgeries, IV nutritional feeding for up to two years, and a possible intestinal transplant.

Even with the highest level of medical care, one in 10 babies will die.

News.title: Author La Plante banned from driving for six months
News.content:
The court heard she already had nine points on her licence, from three speeding offences in June 2023 and then June and July 2025.

She told the court she believed she would have to have the dog rehomed if she was unable to drive him to his daily walks, saying: "I think the emotional turmoil of that would truly damn my career as a writer.

"It's very, very solitary and I work exceptionally hard and I would just stop."

La Plante, who is best known for creating Prime Suspect's no-nonsense Det Ch Insp Jane Tennison, admitted driving at 24mph twice, 25mph, 26mph and 27mph in the latest offences, which all happened as she was on her way to take her dog for his daily walk.

Giving evidence, La Plante said she got her dog Theo after suffering the devastation of the untimely death of another dog, Hugo.

Fighting back tears, she said she "lost it" when Hugo died and she "didn't know what to do with [her] life".

She added her new dog had helped her through the grieving process.

News.title: Driest July on record for England and Wales
News.content:
July 2026 was the driest for England and Wales since records began 190 years ago, according to the Met Office, external.

England recorded just 6.5mm of rainfall and Wales had 9.3mm, both less than half of the previous records for the nations.

The dry conditions have been accompanied by exceptional warmth across much of the UK. It was the second warmest July for the UK as a whole and Wales' warmest ever.
