The month was also the UK's sunniest July on record. For England and Wales, it was the sunniest calendar month ever observed.

So far this year, six months of 2026 have seen above average sunshine hours for the UK, with just February seeing below the monthly average.

News.title: Man sniffed out by police dog while hiding behind fake wall on 300-plant cannabis farm
News.content:
A man has been jailed for six months after being found by a sniffer dog behind a fake wall on a cannabis farm.

Albert Hysaj, 42, pleaded guilty to producing cannabis and was sentenced at Cardiff Crown Court on Friday.

Hysaj was caught after a police dog named Asko located him in the commercial property on the Bowen Industrial Estate, in Aberbargoed, Caerphilly county, in May.

Gwent Police found 313 cannabis plants inside two linked units over three rooms, which included a living area with kitchen and bathroom.

News.title: Presenter Tony Livesey leaves BBC Radio 5 Live after 16 years
News.content:
Presenter Tony Livesey has left BBC Radio 5 Live after 16 years at the station, the corporation has announced.

Livesey stepped back from his weekday late night talk show in June, following allegations made against his former newspaper boss David Sullivan.

He had previously worked as editor-in-chief of Sullivan's Daily and Sunday Sport publications.

Several women have accused Sullivan, a billionaire businessman and West Ham co-owner, of abusing his power and preying on them for sex, in some cases when they were teenagers. Sullivan has strongly denied the allegations.

The claims against Sullivan were made in a joint investigation by the Times and BBC Panorama.

The BBC previously said Livesey had asked to take a break from presenting his programme while the issues raised by the investigation were being examined.

One alleged victim said that Livesey had arranged a meeting between her and Sullivan in 1999.

Livesey said he had "no recollection" of introducing the young woman to Sullivan and that it was "not part" of his job to do so.

He added that he had "great sympathy for a woman who may have become a victim", but rejected any suggestion that he had played "any role whatsoever in that scenario" and said he found the allegation "abhorrent".

In an email sent to 5 Live staff on Monday morning, the station's controller Heidi Dawson said he had now decided to leave.

"Tony has asked me to pass on his heartfelt thanks to the brilliant colleagues at 5 Live who he has had the pleasure of working with over the years," she wrote.

"I know many of you have also really enjoyed working with Tony, and we wish him well for all his future endeavours."

The award-winning presenter worked for the BBC from 2006 - the same year he left the newspapers - appearing on 5 Live from 2010 onwards, including a successful stint hosting its drivetime show.

He won radio awards - ARIA and APAs - for his reporting on how it feels to lose your mother as a child, and an ARIAS gold award after he was asked by the late Dame Deborah James to conduct her final interview.

His topical three-hour programme was broadcast on 5 Live from Monday to Thursday, featuring interviews and phone calls from listeners.

News.title: Comedian Jimmy Cricket dies aged 80
News.content:
Comedian Jimmy Cricket has died aged 80 after a short illness, his family said.

In a statement posted to social media they said Cricket spent his last few days surrounded by his family, love, laughter and songs.

"Forever our clown, he was cracking jokes to the wonderful NHS staff and to us all, right until the end. His courage, dignity and positivity through all he endured was inspirational," they added.

The comedian, from Northern Ireland, became a household name in the 1970s.

James Joseph Mulgrew was born in Cookstown, County Tyrone in 1945, Cricket left school at 16 and started the summer season of 1966 as a Redcoat for Butlins.

He worked the comedy club scene in the 1970s and 1980s, going on to win LWT's Search for a Star talent contest and eventually getting his own TV show on ITV and a radio series on BBC Radio 2.

Cricket's family said he had been a "force for joy" and the world was a "far less sillier place today".

"We were going to end by using his famous catchphrase and say: 'There's no More'.

"But Jimmy was a man of great faith and a Papal Knight of the Catholic Church.

"He believed that death is not the end and was looking forward to eternity, so reallyâ¦ And there's more."

News.title: I didn't know I'd been hosting a parasite for years - until the most intense pain of my life
News.content:
Jones remembers the May 2016 night when he went into hospital â he was supposed to go out to a dinner with his wife Eileen, but he stayed at home as he felt unwell.

"I hadn't been able to control the pain, and it was more intense than anything I had before.

"Then about midnight, we had to call the ambulance, and they took me to Nevill Hall. Whatever they gave me there cured the pain. I haven't experienced pain like that before."

Jones was in hospital for 10 days, and says the doctors there suspected he had hydatid cysts immediately.

He said: "There was a lot of it around this area at the time, and I remember the Ministry of Agriculture giving worming treatment to the dogs on the local farms.

"Whether they could see that I was an old sheep farmer or not, that might have had a bearing on it. We had plenty of experience in this area â Breconshire as a whole â of hydatid cysts, people that have suffered through it, numerous examples."

Jones was then referred to "the main expert on hydatid cysts" in London where he had two operations in 2018 and 2019 to remove them, one from each lung.

"I swapped two cysts for two scars on the ribs," he said, adding that he still has a cyst on his liver, which surgeons decided not to remove.

News.title: Grooming gang found guilty of exploiting teenage girls for sex
News.content:
Four men and a woman have been found guilty of being part of a grooming gang that exploited teenage girls for sex.

Mustafa Iqbal, Mohamed Arshad, Ziaullah Badshah, Jaswinder Singh were convicted of conspiracy to traffic their victims, who were aged 14,15 and 16.

At Caernarfon Crown Court on Monday, Iqbal, Arshad and Badshah were also found guilty of rape while another member of the gang, Sarah Gray, was found guilty of perverting the course of justice and assisting an offender.

The men were remanded in custody ahead of sentencing on 25 September, while Gray was released on bail.

Prosecutor Owen Edwards KC said the men had used the three girls - named only as Child A, B and C - like "sexual commodities".

"They took full sexual advantage of Girl B in particular," he said.

The jury was told Child A had been treated as a "sexual plaything", who finally had gone to the police after having been handcuffed by Iqbal and had been raped.

The court heard the teenagers were given drugs and sexually abused in cars, homes and businesses in Rhyl, Denbighshire and the surrounding area between April 2022 and March 2024.

The first two victims, Child B who was 15 and Child C who was 14, were approached by Iqbal, 43, near a petrol station in the town, and he persuaded them to come back to his home.

They were later joined by local coffee shop owner Arshad, 36, and his friend Badshah, 25.

During the trial the jury had been told how the two girls stated they were 17, had smoked cannabis with the men and had played a game of spin the bottle.

Badshah, who came to Rhyl as a refugee from Pakistan when he was 15, admitted kissing Child B and Child C, and on later occasions having sex with Child B at his home.

Badshah, of Brighton Road, Rhyl, was found guilty of two counts of rape, two counts of conspiracy to traffic, two counts of conspiracy to require a person to perform compulsory labour, supplying cannabis to another.

Arshad, 36, of Clifton Grove, Rhyl, was found guilty of three counts of rape, two counts of conspiracy to traffic, two counts of conspiracy to require a person to perform compulsory labour, and supplying cannabis to another.

The court heard one of the counts of rape happened in an alleyway outside his former business, Zayn's Coffee House.

Iqbal, of Trellewelyn Road, Rhyl, was found guilty of raping Child B and also sexually assaulting Child C. He was also found guilty of raping another teenager, Child A, who was 16 and lived in a care home.

Described as a drug dealer during the trial, he supplied Child A with crack cocaine and cannabis in return for sex.

Iqbal was convicted of 21 offences, including four of rape and three of sexual assault. He was also found guilty of conspiracy to traffic and conspiracy to supply cannabis and cocaine, breaching a trafficking risk order, and he pleaded guilty to possessing a prohibited weapon.

The gang was unmasked after another friend of the men took Child B to London.

Former builder Singh, 61, claimed the girl was looking after his dog and there was no sexual motive in taking her on the trip to see his family in the capital, but a concerned adult was alarmed by Singh's intentions and reported him to the police.

Singh, of River Street, Rhyl, was found guilty of two counts of conspiracy to traffic and one count of supplying cannabis to another.

Gray, 53, of Llanasa Road, Gronant, was also found guilty of conspiracy to supply cocaine to another and conspiracy to supply cannabis to another.

After the guilty verdicts Det Ch Insp Richard Sidney said his thoughts were the three young victims.

"They were children, aged just 14 to 16, when they were subjected to exploitation and abuse by adults who took advantage of their vulnerabilities and sought to manipulate and control them for their own gain," he said.

"No child should have to experience what these young women endured."

He said that the five defendants had denied almost every allegation against them from the outset.

"I hope today's outcome sends a clear message that those who seek to groom and exploit vulnerable children will be relentlessly pursued," he said.

A spokesperson for Denbighshire council said its thoughts were with the young women at the centre of the case, adding that it wanted to "recognise the courage and bravery they have shown".

The spokesperson said the council would work with the North Wales Safeguarding Board on a review, separate to the criminal process, that would "examine agencies' involvement with the young people and to identify what lessons can be learnt for the future".

"We understand that this case has been challenging and has brought up strong feelings. We ask that everyone respects the legal process and each other as we process this outcome," they added.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line

Rapists and serious child sex offenders, including those convicted of grooming offences, will be excluded from upcoming plans to release certain prisoners early.

Andy Burnham said he understood the “anxiety and distress” caused by the scheme and insisted he “wanted to go even further”, but that this would risk the collapse of the entire prison system. He assured the public that offenders will face tighter community supervision, including new GPS monitoring for rapists to restrict movements.

It comes after Mr Burnham paused plans to release prisoners early in September to ease overcrowding in jails following outcry from the public, including from survivors of sexual violence.

The scheme will now be delayed until October.

Pc Harper’s widow Lissie said she is “beyond appalled and bristling with anger”, while Thames Valley Police Chief Constable Jason Hogg said the decision not to exclude them is “demoralising for all police officers”.

In an announcement on Monday night, the prime minister said: “Keeping the public safe is my top priority. That’s why I asked for an urgent review of the prisoner release scheme.

“I fully understand the anger, anxiety and distress that’s been caused. I’ve heard that loud and clear. That’s why we’re making significant changes: offenders who have been sentenced for rape, serious child sex offences and other grooming offences will be excluded from the changes.”

He added: “I want to be honest – I wanted to go even further as I know there will still be concerns about other offenders having their sentence shortened.

“But it’s not possible without the prison system reaching capacity and collapsing, which would put public safety at much greater risk.”

open image in gallery Andy Burnham had previously paused the scheme to review it ( PA )

Mr Burnham said he also intends to introduce “much tougher” community measures including a “presumption” that all offenders are tagged, longer periods of supervision and new restriction zones for offenders.

Under changes in the Sentencing Act, some 6,000 offenders were set to be let out of prison in September after serving a third of their sentence – rather than half – in a bid to ease prison overcrowding.

Prisoners serving longer sentences of four years or more would be eligible for release at the halfway point of their term, rather than at two-thirds as had previously been the case.

The changes were due to be phased in, beginning with prisoners serving sentences of less than 575 days, going up to inmates jailed for 12 years or more being eligible for early release in June next year.

The government has said that, after listening to victims’ concerns, rapists and child sexual offenders will not be eligible for the sentencing changes.

These will be added to the exclusions already in place for 18,000 offenders, including those who have been found by a court to be the most dangerous or anyone serving a life sentence.

The government has also announced a new package of victim support, backed by £10m, to provide better trauma-informed contact.

A new national helpline will also be established and efforts made to contact all affected victims to offer information and support.

Mr Burnham added: “As a country, we haven’t invested in the prison estate when we should have, going back over a decade.

“This has created an unacceptable situation, with our adult male prisons now at 98 per cent capacity. For too long, the problems facing our prison system have been ignored – and it’s the victims who have been paying the price. That is not good enough.

“My government will deliver the fastest prison building programme since the Victorian era and do what’s necessary to fix the prison crisis.”

Labour aims to have 14,000 new prison places by 2031.

open image in gallery Kemi Badenoch held a press conference with survivors who had been told their abusers could be released early under the scheme in June ( PA Wire )

Mr Burnham has also asked justice secretary Alex Norris to look at how the UK can remove foreign offenders faster and in greater numbers, review outdated Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentences and free up space in women’s prisons.

Mr Norris said: “The prime minister and I have reviewed these reforms, listened to the concerns and gone further to protect victims.

“These are decisions no minister would ever want to take, but it is right these sickening crimes are excluded from these reforms.

“Victims will also have access to better support and reassurance that offenders leaving prison face tougher supervision and punishment.”

Wider releases under the Sentencing Act have been delayed from September to October, giving probation staff time to plan for releases and to ensure victims can have a say in restrictions placed on offenders.

The changes also introduce a new progression model which will end automatic release for badly behaved offenders.

Those who break the rules or are violent behind bars face spending 100 per cent of their sentence locked up.

Shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy said the U-turn is a “victory for victims” but said it “doesn’t go far enough”.

Domestic abuse commissioner Dame Nicole Jacobs said not excluding domestic abusers is “wrong and puts victims lives at risk”.

She said: “It is critical that no abuser is released in October unless I am confident that victims’ safety is not being compromised.”

Radio presenter Greg James has revealed the death of his dog in a heartbreaking social media post.

James, who hosts the Radio One breakfast show, shared a message on Instagram on Monday evening saying that his dog Barn was put to sleep on Monday.

After adding that he was “floored” by the news, James ended the post by saying he would not be on presenting duties on Tuesday morning.

“I’m sorry to bring such horrible news but we had to put our lovely Barn to sleep earlier today.

“I can’t really get my head around it. But he was peaceful, we were with him at home in the garden in the sunshine and I can’t stop crying.

“I know how loved this unbelievably daft farty brilliant dog was and I adored sharing him with everyone but can I just ask you to not send DMs or bring him up to me or Bella for a bit please.

“We’re completely floored by it and I can’t believe my little mate has gone and we just can’t talk about it for a bit.

“Lots of love xxPs.

“Not on the show tomorrow obvs x”

Earlier in the year, James raised over £4m for Comic Relief after an eight-day tandem bike challenge that saw him cycle 1,000km from Weymouth to Edinburgh.

James’ final fundraising figure was revealed in the Comic Relief charity telethon on March 20.

Speaking to host Davina McCall, the DJ said his £4,225,939 total had “snowballed” thanks to a huge donation from the band Coldplay, who sent £100,000.

James was supported by Prince William and comedian Joe Lycett for the cycle, both of whom joined him for a leg of his journey.

The widow of police constable Andrew Harper has said she is “beyond appalled” and “bristling with anger” after learning two of her husband’s killers will be allowed to be released from prison early.

Pc Harper, 28, was working for Thames Valley Police when he sustained fatal injuries while responding to a quad bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berkshire, in 2019. He was caught in a strap attached to the back of a car and dragged down a winding country road as the three teenage suspects fled the scene of the burglary.

Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole were jailed for 13 years in 2020 for manslaughter over his killing. But it is understood the pair will be eligible for early release under a new government scheme, despite Andy Burnham’s decision to bar some of the most serious sex offenders from qualifying.

open image in gallery Pc Andrew Harper with his wife, Lissie (Thames Valley Police/Family handout/PA) ( Thames Valley Police )

His widow Lissie Harper slammed the decision as “disgusting” and said it was an “utter betrayal” by the government.

“This is disgusting. I am beyond appalled and bristling with anger to hear that Andrew's killers are soon to be free to roam the streets,” she said in a statement.

"What abhorrent message does this send? How dare ministers say the killing of a police officer is not enough of a ‘sickening crime’ that deserves the stiffest of punishments. The level of disrespect the government are showing to Andrew and other victims - and to their loved ones such as me - is beyond contempt.

She added: "The killers of Andrew have shown no remorse... they robbed us of our future. They are vile criminals and they should remain in jail.

"To release them early from their already pitiful sentences is an affront to justice. The government and the justice system have not just let me down... they have added insult to injury. They are meant to be on our side.

"This is an utter betrayal - and it's one I will not be able to forgive or forget."

open image in gallery Pc Andrew Harper was killed in 2019 (Family Handout/PA) ( PA Media )

It comes after the prime minister paused plans to release prisoners early in September to ease overcrowding in jails following outcry from the public, including from survivors of sexual violence. The scheme will now be delayed until October.

In an announcement on Monday night, he said rapists and serious child sex offenders including those convicted of grooming offences will be blocked from early release.

He added he understood the “anxiety and distress” caused by the scheme and insisted he “wanted to go even further”, but that it is not possible without the prison system collapsing and putting the public “at much greater risk”.

However, he assured the public that offenders will face tighter community supervision, including new GPS monitoring for rapists to restrict movements.

Under changes in the Sentencing Act, some 6,000 offenders were set to be let out of prison in September after serving a third of their sentence – rather than half – in a bid to ease prison overcrowding.

Prisoners serving longer sentences of four years or more would be eligible for release at the halfway point of their term, rather than at two-thirds as had previously been the case.

The government has said that, after listening to victims’ concerns, rapists and child sexual offenders will not be eligible for the sentencing changes.

These will be added to the exclusions already in place for 18,000 offenders, including those who have been found by a court to be the most dangerous or anyone serving a life sentence.

The government has also announced a new package of victim support, backed by £10 million, to provide better trauma-informed contact.

A new national helpline will also be established and efforts made to contact all affected victims to offer information and support.

Shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy said the U-turn “doesn’t go far enough”, adding: “Some child sex offenders and killers, like those responsible for the death of Pc Harper, will still be released early. And the trauma of victims being told their abusers may be released can’t be undone.

“One of Andy Burnham’s first acts as prime minister will be to let thousands of criminals – including killers and paedophiles – out early.”

A great hammerhead shark has washed ashore on a North Carolina beach with a “deep laceration,” according to local experts.

The 14-foot female shark was first spotted at Carolina Beach, outside of Wilmington, at around 3 a.m. ET on Sunday, according to the North Carolina Shark Standing Hotline.

After being seen in the surf multiple times, it washed ashore at around 1:20 p.m., the North Carolina Shark Conservancy told The Independent.

Local officials disposed of the dead shark after the conservancy’s volunteers took samples from the animal.

“We did dispatch our volunteer team out to the shark to take measurements, photos and biological samples for genetics and educational purposes,” a spokesperson for the conservancy said. “We worked in collaboration with the local municipalities who were extremely responsive and helpful during the whole process.”

open image in gallery A great hammerhead shark has washed ashore on a North Carolina beach with a 'deep laceration,' according to local experts ( North Carolina Shark Conservancy )

Beachgoer Paige Furr called the shark’s discovery a “once-in-a-lifetime thing.”

“I’ve never seen anything like it, so yeah, it was pretty cool but sad, you know, at the same time,” Furr told local outlet WECT.

The North Carolina Shark Conservancy was unable to determine the shark’s cause of death, but offered some clues about the animal’s condition.

“It had a very deep laceration through the base of the tail hindering its swimming capabilities as well as fresh puncture wounds in its mouth associated with fishing gear,” the conservancy’s spokesperson said.

While the shark was considered a large female, the species can grow up to 16 to 20 feet long, the spokesperson noted.

open image in gallery While the 14-foot female shark was considered large, the species can grow up to 16 to 20 feet long, according to local experts ( AFP via Getty Images )

Great hammerheads can be found in coastal waters around the world, feeding on rays, small sharks, squid and bony fish, according to Oceana, the world’s largest ocean conservation group.

They grow the fastest and are the largest of all hammerhead species, the group says on its website.

A key feature that differentiates great hammerheads from other hammerheads is their broad, nearly straight cephalofoil — which is the flattened head of the shark that looks like the head of a hammer.

The animal’s cephalofoil gives them better vision and electroreception, allowing it to find prey hidden in the sand, according to the conservation group.

The great hammerhead shark is listed as “critically endangered” on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List of Threatened Species. But the animal is not on US federal officials’ endangered and threatened species list.

News.title: Lioness: The real military program that inspired Taylor Sheridan’s hit — and why it got shut down
News.content:

Taylor Sheridan’s thriller series Lioness centers on an all-female undercover CIA operation that is loosely based on a real-life U.S. Marine unit.

Lioness, which returned with its third season August 2 on Paramount+, follows Zoe Saldaña’s character Joe McNamara, a CIA operative who leads a top-secret group of female special operatives recruited from various branches of the military and tasked with infiltrating terrorist organizations by befriending their wives and daughters.

In real life, Task Force Lioness operated out of Iraq and Afghanistan to identify women who might have been used to carry out terrorist activities. The concept inspired Lioness executive producer Jill Wagner, who also acts in the show, and her husband David Lemanowicz to approach Sheridan to write a series about it.

“I feared that someone would get a hold of this idea and just create Barbies with guns or try to make the women feel too superhero-like,” Wagner told Decider. “People have to understand that there are many female heroes in the world, and they’re not necessarily in Marvel movies. They’re out there sacrificing for our country, and they have really interesting stories to tell. Because of Taylor’s voice and his mind, I knew he was the one person who could do them justice. So that’s why I went to him.”

Read on for the true story of the all-female Lioness team.

open image in gallery ‘Lioness’ is created by Taylor Sheridan, the mastermind behind ‘Yellowstone’ and its many spin-offs ( Paramount+ )

open image in gallery Zoe Saldaña and Nicole Kidman star in ‘Lioness,’ which is loosely based on a real military group used in the Iraq War ( Paramount+ )

Who were the real-life Lionesses?

During the Iraq War in 2003, the American military ran into a problem as male soldiers stationed in Iraq were not allowed to search female civilians due to strict Muslim beliefs that prohibited any man from touching an unrelated woman.

Rebels quickly caught on to the issue and began to use women to smuggle weapons and explosives for terrorist attacks.

Soon, the Marine Corps and the Army formed the Lionesses to conduct more thorough surveillance on hijabi women. Team Lioness consisted of boots-on-the-ground female soldiers — often mechanics, clerks and engineers — who were deployed to combat units in Iraq and Afghanistan.

The women accompanied male troops on patrols and house-to-house operations, conducted searches on women and children at checkpoints and established rapport with women in the community for the sake of disseminating information and identifying people who might be involved in terrorist activity.

The teams typically consisted of two to three female soldiers who joined combat and infantry units.

Eventually, the Lionesses trained local women on how to properly search other women and children so that they could take on the security responsibility after the troops left Iraq and Afghanistan.

Although women were prohibited from fighting in ground combat at the time due to the combat exclusion rule, many Team Lioness soldiers were caught up in conflicts like firefights and IED attacks that they were unequipped to handle as they were sent out to diffuse tensions between Iraqi citizens.

open image in gallery Team Lioness led to the establishment of the Female Engagement Team that was sent to Afghanistan in 2010 ( Getty )

A 2008 PBS documentary called Lioness, directed by Meg McLagan and Daria Sommers, examined five women who were unexpectedly drawn into battle while volunteering for the unit.

“This may come as a shock to America, but we went on lots of missions,” said Shannon Morgan, a Team Lioness soldier who served in the U.S. Army’s 1st Engineer Battalion, in the documentary, according to USA Today.

“But if our government is going to allow us to play infantry, they should start training us for it. We pretty much wing it.”

What happened to the Lioness program?

Although Team Lioness was successful, the initiative was eventually phased out because of its short-term tactics. However, the program led to the Marine Corps officially establishing Female Engagement Teams in 2009, which focused more on gaining access to the community rather than being attached to combat units.

The program’s success also paved the way for policy change. In 2013, the Department of Defense lifted the combat exclusion rule, which allowed female members of the military to join combat units and further eliminated the need for a separate female team.

Although hundreds of women cycled through the all-female unit Team Lioness, the characters in Sheridan’s show — which stars Saldaña, Nicole Kidman and Morgan Freeman — are fictionalized and not based on any specific person.

New episodes of Lioness air Sundays at 3 a.m. ET / 12 a.m. PT on Paramount+.

News.title: Watch: Driver calls 999 while speeding in Jaguar and claims brakes have stopped working
News.content:
A man who falsely claimed that his vehicle was out of control as part of a financial ploy has been jailed.

Nathan Owen, 33, told Merseyside Police on 6 March, 2024 that his Jaguar had malfunctioned and he was unable to stop. He drove at “extreme speeds” of up to 86mph as he travelled down the M57 and M58.

Footage released by the force shows police vehicles driving alongside Owen in an attempt to stop the car, with one police car being hit 31 times.

Owen had in fact “fabricated the events” to get rid of the vehicle, which he had missed multiple finance payments on, Liverpool Crown Court heard.

Judge Ian Unsworth said that Owen had “sought to profit from a lie” whilst officers risked their safety to help in what they believed was an emergency.

On Monday (3 August), Owen, of The Grove, Prestatyn, North Wales, was sentenced to four years and three months in prison. He was also disqualified from driving for five years and until an extended driving test has been passed.

Eighteen-year-olds will soon benefit from half-price train travel on most services, as the Department for Transport (DfT) announces a relaxation of Railcard rules.

From 17 August, the 16-17 Saver Railcard, which can be purchased by 16- and 17-year-olds, will remain valid for a full year from its purchase date, even if the holder turns 18.

Previously, the Railcards expired upon the holder's 18th birthday.

The DfT said that the existing rule left more than 70,000 students annually an average of £175 worse off than peers in the same academic year who had not yet reached adulthood.

The new policy aligns the 16-17 Saver with other Railcards.

The “common sense change” is “exactly what passengers should expect from the railway”, Rail Minister Lord Hendy said.

Passengers make their way through Paddington train station in central London ( AFP/Getty )

“I’m proud that this change will support young people and their families to lower the cost of travel at a critical time for teenagers, whether they’re pursuing further education, vocational pathways or getting their footing in the jobs market,” he said.

“Making travel fairer and more affordable is central to the vision for Great British Railways.

“By delivering simpler fares and putting passengers first, we’re creating a railway that’s easier to use, better value for money and focused on meeting the everyday needs of the people who rely on it.”



The 16-17 Saver Railcard costs £35 per year and entitles the holder to 50 per cent off most train fares.

Jacqueline Starr, the chief executive of industry body the Rail Delivery Group, said that extending the Railcard’s validity demonstrates the sector’s commitment to “offering better value fares and delivering a more joined-up railway”.

Kaynat Ahmad, the vice president for further education at the National Union of Students, described the Railcard as “essential for young people reliant on trains to get to college, work or training”.

Other Railcards available include those for young people under the age of 30, seniors, couples, families and veterans.

The announcement comes after the government said the cap on most single bus fares in England will be cut from £3 to £2 in 2027.

News.title: USPS driver rescued after mail van gets stranded in New York floodwaters
News.content:
A USPS driver had to be rescued from floodwaters after their delivery van became stuck.

Footage shared by the Chatham Fire Department on Friday (31 July) shows the worker being helped from the partially submerged vehicle and onto the back of a fire engine on Route 295.

New York has been battered by heavy downpours, resulting in widespread flooding, road closures and hundreds of calls for emergency assistance.

Heavy rain left parts of Route 295 flooded, making travel hazardous as vehicles had to navigate the water carefully.

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson's ex-assistant at Man Utd joins his son in new League One role
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson's ex-assistant at Man Utd joins his son in new League One role

Rene Meulensteen has taken on a senior role with Stockport County as the League One club bring in the man who previously served as Sir Alex Ferguson's assistant at Manchester United

View 2 Images Rene Meulensteen has taken on a role at Stockport County (Image: @StockportCounty)

Sir Alex Ferguson's former assistant at Manchester United, Rene Meulensteen, has landed a shock role at Stockport County.

‌



The Dutchman, who also served as Fulham's manager for a brief period, has been appointed at Edgeley Park taking on the role of director of football methodology.

‌



Stockport finished third in League One last season but lost out in the play-off final at Wembley. They've turned to Meulensteen for some top-flight experience and his new role will see him work closely with Stockport’s first-team staff, which will also allow him to collaborate with his son Joppe, who is a coach at the club.

‌



His remit will also involve a part in developing the football programme across both the academy and first team. The club's sporting director, Damien Allen, said: "Today marks a significant milestone in our club's history with the appointment of our first-ever director of football methodology.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Vinicius Junior to Arsenal, Man Utd exit confirmed, Guimaraes jets in
Sports.content:
The latest Manchester United, Liverpool, Arsenal transfer news and more as the likes of Bruno Guimaraes, Vinicius Jr and Bradley Barcola's futures remain up in the air

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal saga has Newcastle in contention for all-time worst transfer window
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal saga has Newcastle in contention for all-time worst transfer window

Newcastle's chief executive stated a desire to be amongst the best clubs in the world in four years - but a transfer window that has seen their best players leave and their captain wanting out is putting that ambition in question

View 3 Images Newcastle are desperate to keep hold of Bruno Guimaraes as they try to avoid a disaster summer (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes has reported for Newcastle's pre-season camp as talk over his sale continues - and his possible exit would make their summer go from bad to worse.

‌



The Magpies are currently fighting to keep their captain after two high-profile sales at St James' Park and the departure of their manager.

‌



So often poor transfer windows centre around dire recruitment, the expensive signings who fail to work out. But in terms of exits we could certainly be looking at one of the worst summers in the history of the Premier League.

‌



There's no doubt that the hangover from the poor summer of 12 months ago, which centred around Alexander Isak's desire to leave, eventually joining Liverpool on deadline day, has bled into the window we're currently in.

Newcastle's forgettable summer of 2025 set them on a path to a first bottom-half finish in recent years, and that had financial consequences which has seen players jump ship. The ripples are certainly being felt.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Arsenal target Bruno Guimaraes complies with Newcastle requests as midfielder boards flight READ MORE :

Arsenal receive immediate response after finally submitting first Bruno Guimaraes offer READ MORE :

Anthony Gordon's move to Barcelona can be written off as the one major deal that Newcastle were always going to have to sanction to remain financially compliant, especially after they missed out on European revenue. The £70million deal was one the majority could stomach.

Sandro Tonali's £100m switch to Tottenham is one that the balance sheet can live with, but what it says to the rest of the squad is perhaps more damaging than the exit itself. The Italian had been linked with Arsenal in January and given that Newcastle nearly doubled their money on the £55m they spent on him, you think fair play.

The issue is the likes of Guimaraes, who with Tonali alongside formed a midfield partnership that could genuinely be compared to any side in the Premier League. That was the only area where the Magpies could claim they were in the elite bracket, and that's a great foundation to build from.

‌



Instead it could implode. Tonali's departure doesn't send a message of ambition and Guimaraes has expressed a desire to move to Arsenal. Newcastle have stood firm, maintaining their talisman is not for sale.

View 3 Images Sandro Tonali joined Tottenham in a club-record deal (Image: Tottenham Hotspur FC)

The Brazilian's exit would leave Newcastle, entering a new era under Matthias Jaissle, looking more and more like a mid-table side. A number of their blockbuster arrivals under the Saudi Arabian regime will have moved on, and questioned will be asked of the project.

‌



Manchester United continue to track left-back Lewis Hall, who has just enjoyed the best season of his career to date. If Guimaraes were to be sold then Newcastle would be financially able to rebuff any offer that comes in for Hall - and they insist he's not for sale.

Even so, the player's head may well be turned, and a squad full of players who would rather be elsewhere isn't a recipe for success. Newcastle were quick to land a new manager, but he's an uphill task ahead of him.

Much has been made of Newcastle's failure to get deals over the line. James Trafford, Marc Guehi, Hugo Ekitike, Joao Pedro and Bryan Mbeumo have all opted for other Premier League rivals ahead of the Magpies.

‌



View 3 Images Eddie Howe has called time on five years at Newcastle (Image: PA)

Missing out on those names has certainly halted Newcastle's progress, but being able to retain their best players has meant that Howe, when he was in situ, had enough to work with that he could challenge England's best on their day. Consistency remained the problem, but a squad boasting Tonali, Guimaraes and Isak was able to end the club's 70-year wait for a trophy.

That was only 18 months ago and yet it seems like that was in a different era such has been the shift in the way many see Newcastle, even those within their four walls.

‌



Its not to say the club haven't spent money - upwards of £100m has been spent of summer arrivals that include Ewen Jaouen, Bazoumana Toure and Sean Steur. But the fact their signings have done nothing to mitigate the negative feeling around Newcastle says everything about the magnitude of the players they've let go - and those that could still follow them.

Only last year new chief executive David Hopkinson claimed Newcastle can be “in the debate about being the top club in the world ” by 2030. Make no mistake, four years out from that goal, no club sanctions the type of exits that the Magpies have without heavyweight names coming in to replace them.

Sports.title: Man Utd tell Ralf Rangnick's only signing he can leave permanently after brutal snub
Sports.content:
Man Utd tell Ralf Rangnick's only signing he can leave permanently after brutal snub

Ralf Rangnick could not impart many changes during his fleeting spell as manager of Manchester United, but even one of those is seemingly being rooted out of the club

View 3 Images Ralf Rangnick's only Man United signing has been told he can leave the club this summer (Image: 2022 Manchester United FC)

Ralf Rangnick's only transfer signing as interim manager of Manchester United has been told he is allowed to leave the club. Rangnick took over the Reds on a temporary basis after Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was sacked during the 2021-22 Premier League campaign.

‌



The Austrian was in charge during the following transfer window and while the club were linked with many players recommended by him, only one was brought to the club. That player was Toby Collyer, who arrived from Brighton and Hove Albion as an 18-year-old prospect.

‌



Four-and-a-half years later, Collyer has reportedly been informed he is allowed to depart the club permanently, having been left out of Michael Carrick's squad for the recent friendly over Atletico Madrid. His absence would have stung as the substitutes' bench was filled with plenty of young academy stars.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Instead, Collyer featured for the U21s side in a 1-0 defeat to Altrincham Town on Friday evening. Last season, Collyer was loaned to Championship side West Bromwich Albion, before being loaned to Hull City in the following transfer window.

Throughout his time at the club, he has only made 13 senior appearances for the Reds, with ten of those coming under Ruben Amorim. His loan spells with West Brom and Hull were both marred by injuries. Now, according to The Sun, the club have said he is free to leave.

‌



Despite United starting the summer short in central midfield, Collyer always seemed far away from Carrick's plans. They have since strengthened by signing Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively.

View 3 Images Toby Collyer featured against Altrincham Town when many other United youngsters were included in the squad against Atletico Madrid (Image: 2026 Manchester United FC)

A third midfielder is also expected to be brought in this summer. Meanwhile, fellow academy graduate Tyler Fletcher is believed to be ahead of the ex-Brighton prospect in the United pecking order.

‌



Against Altrincham, he was joined by fellow United U21 team-mates Dan Gore, Jacob Devaney and Chido Obi, who all featured in the friendlies against Wrexham and Rosenborg.

Collyer's loan spell with West Brom came to an end after he suffered an injury during a clash against Birmingham City towards the end of November. He was brought back to United to work on his recovery, before being loaned to Hull.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has made many big changes at Manchester United since taking over from Ruben Amorim (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



He hoped to be involved in Hull's promotion play-off final clash against Middlesbrough at Wembley but he could not recover from his injury in time. He made 12 appearances for West Brom before the loan was ended and he only made five at Hull.

Collyer's departure would also rip out the last bit of Rangnick's legacy at Old Trafford. The now Austria manager took charge of 29 matches, winning 11, drawing nine and losing nine.

He had been expected to take up a consultancy role at Old Trafford, but this did not transpire as he left the club completely upon the end of his caretaker deal.

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan's 'overwhelmed' family issue heartfelt statement and explain funeral plans
Sports.content:
Kevin Keegan's 'overwhelmed' family issue heartfelt statement and explain funeral plans

Kevin Keegan died on July 20 following a battle with stomach cancer and his family have now issued a statement to thank those who paid tribute and detail plans for his funeral

View 3 Images Kevin Keegan died aged 75 from cancer (Image: (Liverpool FC via Getty Images))

Kevin Keegan's family say they have been "truly overwhelmed" by the volume of tributes following the death of the football legend. England great Keegan passed away aged 75 last month from cancer.

It was announced on July 20 that the former Liverpool, Hamburg, Southampton and Newcastle striker had died following a battle with stomach cancer. The Newcastle hero left behind wife of 51 years Jean and their children Laura Jane, 47, and Sarah Marie, 43.

Tributes poured in from across the heartbroken football world for the double Ballon d'Or winner, who won 63 caps for England and managed the Three Lions, Newcastle, Fulham and Manchester City.

‌



A private funeral has now been arranged by the Keegan family, who have also set up a fundraiser in King Kev's honour, which will raise money for charities close to his heart.

Gianni Infantino's opponents prepared to launch rival competition to force out FIFA boss READ MORE :

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert says he received death threats after Spygate scandal READ MORE :

A statement from the Keegan family, issued by the League Managers Association, read: “Following the devastating news of Kevin’s passing, we would like to thank the vast number of people who have expressed condolences and shared their memories of Kevin in recent days.

“As a family we have been truly overwhelmed by the volume of tributes and are grateful for them all. We will be holding a small private funeral in the coming weeks and request ongoing privacy and respect whilst we navigate this extremely difficult period as a family.

“Details of a memorial service hosted by Newcastle United that will take place at a later date will be communicated in due course.”

The fundraiser states: "The Keegan family are deeply grateful for all the kind words and support received from far and wide. To honour Kevin’s memory, they feel there would be no more fitting gesture than to give.

View 3 Images Kevin Keegan touched the hearts of many

‌



"We are therefore raising money for two causes that were close to Kevin’s heart: The Christie Charity and Football Families for Justice. The Christie were an immeasurable help to Kevin and his family, as they are to many others. Football Families for Justice is a charity being set-up by John Stiles, son of the great Nobby Stiles, to support former players who are suffering from neuro degenerative diseases caused by heading the ball during their football career.

"A sporting superstar, but also a husband, father, grandfather and friend - Kevin gave so much to us all."

Keegan was most loved at Newcastle, where he enjoyed his most successful spell as a manager. "Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters," the club said in a statement.

‌



View 3 Images Kevin Keegan was a legend at Newcastle United (Image: PA)

"As a player, he brought world-class talent, ambition and belief to St. James’ Park, helping to transform perceptions of what Newcastle United could be. As a manager, he ignited our city. Kevin gave supporters hope and pride, and led a team whose style, spirit and passion captured the imagination of football fans around the world. He was so much more than an Entertainer.

"Kevin forged an extraordinary bond with Newcastle, built on the roots of his father, Joe. He understood our people. He embraced the North East with a passion that was genuine and unwavering, and in return, he earned his rightful place in the hearts of millions."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's opponents prepared to launch rival competition to force out FIFA boss
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's opponents prepared to launch rival competition to force out FIFA boss

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is holding on by his finger nails, but his opponents are trying to get rid of him and are ready to take extreme steps to ensure that he is ousted

View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino said the proposal will not proceed (Image: VCG via Getty Images)

The leaders of UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC are ready to take extreme measures to oust FIFA boss Gianni Infantino - which includes setting up their own rival competition.

‌



The days of the FIFA president appear numbered in the wake of his failed plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup, but Infantino is determined to fight on. He's tried to lean on old acquaintances, but he's lost the faith of several of the world's major organisations.

‌



UEFA have been the most outspoken federation and have backing from other continental organisations. The Times reports that they're prepared to create their own tournament and UEFA have a blueprint for a global league having commissioned one in 2017, without using it.

‌



One source told the newspaper: “Everyone is very determined he needs to go, and if not we will take all the necessary steps [to remove him from power]. That includes future international competitions — would the big South American countries prefer to play France or Spain, or Lebanon or Djibouti? Everyone is very determined, there are no backward steps now.”

FA chiefs should be embarrassed by their prior support of disgraced Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump meeting not happening as third nation calls out FIFA boss READ MORE :

It remains feasible that Infantino will ignore the noise and try for re-election in March as he eyes a fourth term. Infantino’s opponents would therefore be prepared to impose a “governance boycott” which would see them refuse to take part in FIFA council or committee meetings.

A number of European associations, including England and Wales, have withdrawn letters of support for Infantino’s re-election after his World Cup sale plans fell flat. It comes after the FA had supported Infantino via a letter as recently as June.

‌



UEFA were outspoken against the FIFA president during the World Cup, heavily criticising his decision to suspended the red card handed to Folarin Balogun whilst their president Aleksander Ceferin refused to attend the final last month in New York.

View 2 Images UEFA strongly opposed FIFA's plans and want rid of Gianni Infantino (Image: Harry Murphy/UEFA via Getty Images)

Europe's governing body has signalled its intent to take legal action after FIFA and said in a letter: “UEFA hereby gives formal notice that it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa and all related matters.

Article continues below

“You and Fifa are required to take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa’s possession, custody, or control.

“These obligations arise independently of any internal retention policy you or your organisation maintain and supersede any routine document destruction or deletion policies that would otherwise apply.”

Sports.title: Liverpool set for major cash injection as club enter advanced talks after £324m reveal
Sports.content:
Liverpool set for major cash injection as club enter advanced talks after £324m reveal

Liverpool are "working hard behind the scenes" and "pretty advanced in terms of speaking to the right people" ahead of this coming Premier League season starting

View 2 Images Liverpool could become the first Premier League club to expand their retail stores into the United States (Image: Carl Recine, Getty Images)

Liverpool are said to be in advanced talks to open permanent retail stores in the United States. No Premier League club has yet to launch any physical shops Stateside, with Manchester City coming closest, but only previously running pop-ups.

‌



Paris Saint-Germain are the pioneers in this regard across European football, opening their first store in Los Angeles five years ago and have since opened two more in Miami and New York City. The latter is their largest outside of France.

‌



PSG even expanded their presence on Fifth Avenue within 18 months. Liverpool now appear next in line to make the move.

‌



Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG strike contingency plan READ MORE :

Liverpool transfer need brutally exposed as Leeds stun Andoni Iraola - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Liverpool's chief commercial officer Ben Latty told Sportico of Liverpool's ongoing discussions: "Clearly, we're not at the end of that because we haven't opened anything or announced anything yet, but I'd say we are pretty advanced in terms of speaking to the right people."

Liverpool have launched stores in Bali and London in recent months, with existing outlets already operating in Denmark, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Ireland, Singapore, South Africa and the United Kingdom.

The club's chief commercial officer is reportedly hopeful that their current tally of 26 stores will surpass 30 before the end of this season. Latty added: "We can't expect our numbers to grow organically.

‌



"We've got to work for them, and we've got to strategically put our investment where we think it's going to return the highest revenue for us as a club, so yeah, we are working hard behind the scenes."

View 2 Images Liverpool chief executive Billy Hogan spoke earlier this summer about the United States' importance (Image: John Powell, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool's most recent accounts, filed for the 2024-25 campaign, reveal that their commercial income stood at £324million. Only City (£340million) and Manchester United (£333million) posted higher figures amongst Premier League sides.

‌



Speaking while part of this summer's fortnight-long pre-season tour, where the squad was stationed in Chicago, chief executive Billy Hogan said: "The US is a really important market from our perspective.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"A huge fan base here, over 26 million supporters of the club, which, I'm told, actually, the only US sports team that has more fans is the LA Lakers. So, a pretty good indication of the popularity of the club.

‌



"It's our number one international retail market. We are the number two most-watched team in European football here in the US. So, the team is incredibly popular.

"It's an important market from our perspective. (Almost 40 per cent) of our partners are here. And so, all of that kind of comes together to make it a super-important market from our perspective."

Sports.title: Short guides Welsh Fire to crucial win over Southern Brave
Sports.content:
A superb unbeaten half-century from Matt Short guided Welsh Fire to a six-wicket victory over Southern Brave that takes them level on points at the top The Hundred table.

With both sides still in the hunt for a qualification place and coming off the back of morale-boosting victories, it was the Fire who took the honours in Cardiff to join Trent Rockets on 16 points at the summit of the table.

Opting to bowl, Fire's battery of experienced seamers were immediately into the action, Chris Woakes and Sam Cook reducing the Brave to 2-2 off seven balls as Jamie Smith and Ben McKinney both edged behind to Phil Salt.

The Cook-Salt combo also accounted for Nikhil Chaudhary after he and Marcus Stoinis had sedately taken the visitors to an underwhelming 45-3 at the halfway stage.

Not long after, Rachin Ravindra, getting big turn, snared Tristan Stubbs and Moeen Ali with successive deliveries, the latter caught by Joe Root off a skier.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Moeen Ali goes for a golden duck, leaving the Southern Brave in trouble against the Welsh Fire

The Brave were chugging along at barely a run a ball on a tricky surface but Stoinis added some muscular impetus, going to a 35-ball half-century before hitting Cook, who returned a magnificent 3-14, down deep square's throat.

David Miller hit a couple of late sixes but Short, coming on to bowl for the first time in the final five of the innings, had him caught on the edge.

Jofra Archer hit a first-ball six but was gone second ball and the Brave ended with 115-8, their lowest-ever total in The Hundred, below their 118-8 against the Oval Invincibles in 2024.

With little margin for error, Archer set the tone for the Fire, delighting in getting Phil Salt with his first ball and not conceding a run until his eighth.

But Short and Root kept things moving, knowing that one or two partnerships would be enough, and calmly took the score to 60 off 48 before Root departed, caught by McKinney off Chris Jordan.

Ravindra and Jordan Cox came and went but Tom Kohler-Cadmore kept the scoreboard ticking over as he supported Short - who reached a 37-ball 50 with a scoop off Archer and made good use of the ramp throughout to the short straight boundaries - to see his side home, an anticlimactic two wides finishing things.

Image: Matt Short (left) and Tom Kohler-Cadmore saw Welsh Fire to victory over the Southern Brave

Match Hero Matt Short said: "It was tough early and it was a pretty spicy wicket with some quick bowlers. It was nice to bat second and get a bit of dew and skid off the wicket.

"They came hard with a Test match length but the shine wears off and it gets a bit easier. When we bowled, our guys hit the right length and let the ball do the talking."

Despite having won four of their five games, the Fire have a negative net run rate of -0.081, while leaders Trent Rockets are on +0.760.

The Brave, who have now played more matches than any other side in the men's tournament, fell to a fourth defeat in six and are facing a battle to advance.

What's next in The Hundred?

The Hundred continues on Tuesday with SunRisers Leeds hosting London Spirit at Headingley. The women's fixture begins at 3pm, with the men's contest following at 6.30pm.

Sports.title: Nygren spares Hogh blushes as Celtic begin title defence with win
Sports.content:
Celtic made a winning start to their Scottish Premiership title defence with a 1-0 victory over battling Dundee at Celtic Park.

After Rangers had been held by Dundee United on Friday night and Hearts were beaten at Aberdeen on Saturday, Celtic capitalised on opening-round slip-ups from their rivals thanks to Benjamin Nygren's second-half header.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Benjamin Nygren scores Celtic's first goal of the season with a header from a great cross from Kieran Tierney to give the home side the lead against Dundee

It wasn't all plain sailing though, with goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo required to make a super stop to prevent Dundee sub Ashley Hay heading in a late leveller.

Martin O'Neill's side should have been out of sight by then but had seen club-record £11m signing Kasper Hogh spurn two good opportunities inside the first 13 minutes. He then blew a third good chance of the night on 85 minutes, shooting wide from close range before captain Callum McGregor pinged a right-foot shot against a post.

While Hogh laboured, fellow new attacker Camilo Duran looked lively cutting in from the right but it was last season's top scorer Nygren who came up with the crucial moment from Kieran Tierney's fine cross.

Image: Celtic's Benjamin Nygren celebrates scoring

Dundee boss Steven Pressley had called on his side to be "positive" at the home of the champions and his side were certainly that, with Charlie Reilly clipping the side-netting in a good first half from the visitors and on another night they could have profited from their 11 shots and Celtic's wastefulness.

Celtic's need to strengthen their squad further this summer is clear and they will need to find some more sharpness before the key Champions League qualifier against LASK in two-and-a-half weeks' time. But, unlike their title rivals, they are up and running with three points.

The key moments from Celtic Park

9: MISS! A misplaced pass at the back from Dundee sees Kasper Hogh played into the box - but he skews his shot badly wide of the near post. "That's an awful finish," said Chris Sutton on co-commentary.

13: MISS! Hogh is off target again, failing to divert Benjamin Nygren's shot into the bottom corner.

15: SIDE-NETTING! Charlie Reilly clips the side-netting with Dundee's first shot of the game.

34: SHOT! Owen Bevan has Dundee's first shot on target - but it's an easy stop for Viljami Sinisalo.

38: WIDE! Arne Engels looks primed to head Celtic in front but nods his effort the wrong side of the post.

41: SAVE! Kieran Tierney bursts into the box but his drilled shot is well saved by Owen Goodman - Celtic's first shot on target at the 10th attempt.

52: GOAL! Tierney swings in a cross for Nygren to head in the opener from close range.

67: SAVE! Hyun-Jun Yang strikes from 30 yards but Goodman gets down well to make the save.

82: BIG SAVE! Sinisalo does brilliantly to get down to his right to get a hand to Ashley Hay's header which was going towards the bottom corner.

85: ANOTHER MISS FOR HOGH! Hogh passes up his third good chance of the night, stabbing a close-range shot wide of the post.

85: OFF THE POST! Callum McGregor drives into the D and bends a right-foot shot at goal but the ball pings back off the post.

Hogh: 'I have to adapt to the grass'

Celtic's Kasper Hogh speaking to Sky Sports:

"I have to go to some shooting practice, I had a couple of chances today!

"I was just happy to be on the pitch and to help my team-mates win. It doesn't matter if it's me scoring, we won and that's the most important thing.

"I have to adapt to the grass. That's a different thing for me."

O'Neill critical of Celtic performance - but backs Hogh

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin O'Neill backs Kasper Hogh to deliver goals despite missed chances, while addressing Alistair Johnston's future, Celtic's transfer plans and their Champions League ambitions.

Celtic boss Martin O'Neill speaking to Sky Sports:

"It was tough. I didn't think we played particularly well throughout the game, yet amazingly we created some really good chances. Maybe could have scored a number of goals. But overall in terms of play, decisiveness and things, I thought that was lacking from our game. Overall, we can do much better."

On Hogh: "I think he will score goals for us. I always want a centre forward to just get hold of the ball at times, but he's getting to know the players. When he knows everybody's name, including mine, then he'll be an asset to us."

On transfers: "It would be nice if all that transfer speculation went away, which I'm sure it probably won't. It would be nice to go away and nice to get a few more players in, which we're trying to do."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kris Boyd and James McFadden believe Celtic shouldn't let either of Alistair Johnston or Arne Engels go unless they get the right price and have a ready made replacement ready to come in.

Wilson: Better to come from Celtic

Former Celtic defender Mark Wilson on Sky Sports:

"The objective is to get three points and get off to the best possible start.

"I think if you can match it with a performance that's sparkling and slick, then fantastic and you entertain the crowd. I don't think they quite got that, they got it in bits and pieces.

"Second half was certainly better than the first half and they were more adventurous with their passing at times.

"There will be better to come from this Celtic team this season, it's a wee bit transitional for them at the minute."

Pressley proud of Dundee performance

Dundee boss Steven Pressley speaking to Sky Sports:

"I thought we were really brave. Brave in and out of possession. We were aggressive, we had pressure. We showed a lot of composure with the ball against a very good Celtic side, probably their strongest side and I thought our work ethic was incredible as well tonight.

"I think we set real standards for the season tonight with the way we went about the game, so I couldn't be prouder of the group. I said pre-game that the winning of this game for ourselves isn't always the result, it's the performance and we gave it a terrific performance tonight.

"We can't underestimate the gulf in finance between the two clubs.In terms of our heart, our desire, our resilience at times, our bravery, I couldn't be prouder of the way they went about things. They showed those words in abundance."

What the result means and what's next...
