Sports.title: Serena to resume comeback alongside sister Venus in Cincinnati
Sports.content:
Serena and Venus Williams are set to play at the Cincinnati Open after being awarded a wild card for the women's doubles draw.

Serena made a sensational return to tennis during the grass-court season after almost four years out of the professional game, but the 44-year-old suffered a knee injury during a first-round singles loss which led to her and Venus withdrawing from the doubles at the All England Club.

Serena played doubles in London at Queen's Club and at the Berlin Open - but not alongside Venus on either occasion - as she prepared for Wimbledon.

Venus, who turned 46 in June, has also been given a wild card for the singles draw in Cincinnati. She is seeking a first singles victory of 2026 having lost in the first round of all eight of the tournaments she has entered this year.

Venus has had slightly more success playing doubles in 2026, claiming a sole victory at two of the six tournaments she has entered. She most recently played alongside Britain's Katie Boulter in Madrid and breakout star Alexandra Eala in Berlin.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Judy Murray discusses Serena Williams' comeback to tennis.

Among the other players to be awarded singles wild cards for the tournament were fellow Americans Sloane Stephens and Taylor Townsend.

As a doubles pairing, the Williams sisters have won 14 Major titles and three Olympic gold medals. They last took the court for a doubles match together at the 2022 US Open and will be playing the Cincinnati Open for the first time as a team.

Sports.title: Graham stars as Welsh Fire upset Southern Brave in last-ball thriller
Sports.content:
Welsh Fire turned the form table on its head to defeat The Hundred table-toppers Southern Brave in a last-ball thriller in Cardiff.

Until the last dozen deliveries, it looked like it was to be rinse and repeat for the visitors, putting up what seemed a below-par total before unleashing their formidable bowling attack to squeeze the opposition to defeat - but brilliant cameos from Heather Graham and Niamh Holland at the death saw Fire triumph in an absolute thriller to keep their hopes alive.

Having lost their last two games in addition to being hampered by the loss of their captain Sophie Devine - ruled out of the tournament with a calf injury - Welsh Fire desperately needed a win against the unbeaten league-leaders.

In their previous five wins, Brave had twice defended 126-7 and 140-3, and chased 115 and 117. They are curiously the only team in the men's or women's competition not to have gone past 140.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lizelle Lee looked to have lost control of the ball but regained her composure just in time to stump Ella McCaughan.

Today, their batting misfired again after Sophie Molineux became the first captain to win the toss and bat in this year's women's tournament.

The openers were gone after 16 balls, and Laura Wolvaardt and Jemimah Rodrigues rebuilt in uncharacteristically pedestrian style. Batting was not easy on a turning pitch, and the Brave stumbled to 121-5, Welsh Fire seemingly on top but aware of Brave's bowling threat.

Georgia Voll went past Sophia Dunkley to become the 2026 competition's leading run-scorer but departed for 11 to Tilly Corteen-Coleman's second ball, with young spinner having Ella McCaughan stumped from her fifth.

And when the economical Issy Wong hit Devine's replacement Orla Prendergast's stumps, Brave were squeezing the opposition in habitual style, despite bowling an unusual number of wides.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sarah Glenn takes a great catch to get the first wicket of the innings.

A Lauren Bell slower ball deceived Wareham to leave Fire in real trouble, needing 52 off 38 but an unexpected six-four combo from debutant Grace Thompson, in for Em Arlott, put the cat amongst the pigeons. She was then caught, and it looked like the nous and skills of Molineux and Bell would see Brave home.

But that was to reckon without another young talent in Holland. She swept and drove boundaries to leave three runs needed off two, then Lee should have run Graham out but dropped the ball to leave a single needed off the last ball. And Graham gleefully hit Bell through the infield to spark the celebrations.

Match Hero Graham said: "For Niamh to come in at the end, run really well with me, and get a few boundaries away herself; the win is more for those guys than me. It's always nerve-wracking in situations like that. I've played for a lot of years now and been in plenty of tight games, so you just rely on those past experiences to help get you over the line."

What's next in The Hundred?

The Hundred continues on Tuesday with SunRisers Leeds hosting London Spirit at Headingley. The women's fixture begins at 3pm, with the men's contest following at 6.30pm.

Sports.title: Hearn wants £1m per-year deal for Pollock from Northampton
Sports.content:
England star Henry Pollock is expected to seek a significant pay rise to remain at Northampton after agent Eddie Hearn said he is worth at least £1m a year.

Pollock's current contract with Saints expires next summer and is thought to pay around £150,000 a year.

Since agreeing that deal in December 2024, the back-row forward has made his international debut, toured with the British and Irish Lions and helped Northampton win the 2025-26 Gallagher Prem title.

"He's certainly a seven-figure player," Hearn told Telegraph Sport.

"The way rugby's going and what Pollock is doing, his value over the next couple of years will skyrocket, and I think the value of rugby will."

Sports.title: Eala beats Pegula at DC Open to claim first WTA Tour title
Sports.content:
Rising Filipina star Alexandra Eala came from a set down against Jessica Pegula to claim the first WTA Tour singles title of her career at the DC Open.

Eala had trailed by a set when the match was suspended because of heavy rain on Sunday, but the 21-year-old turned the contest round on Monday to claim a 4-6 6-4 6-0 victory.

The victory made Eala the first Filipina to win a singles title on the tour, completing the same career-defining breakthrough that the Washington tournament once gave Pegula when she claimed her first WTA Tour title in 2019.

Eala's popularity soared during the grass-court season as she beat some of the sport's biggest names on runs to the semi-finals in Berlin and last 16 at Wimbledon.

She has swiftly become a huge star in the Philippines, and the nation's flags were dotted throughout the Stadium Court in Washington as chants for Eala routinely outweighed those for Pegula.

The two traded breaks midway through the opening set, with Pegula breaking again at 4-4 and serving out the set at love. The players held through the opening three games of the second set before heavy rain suspended play on Sunday afternoon, with Eala up 2-1.

When they returned on Monday, the momentum belonged to Eala. She stormed back to claim the second set, then swept through the third.

Sports.title: Raducanu to miss US Open
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu's stress fracture will force her to miss the US Open.

The British No 1 suffered the injury to her right lower leg during the grass-court season and made a late decision to pull out of Wimbledon.

According to the Press Association, following consultation with her medical team, Raducanu has concluded she will be unable to play in New York later this month.

While the news comes as no surprise given the nature of the injury and the fact Raducanu has only recently taken her first tentative steps back on court wearing a protective boot, it is another blow to the 23-year-old.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hours before withdrawing from Wimbledon, Emma Raducanu told the media that she intended to compete despite pushing beyond anything she normally would.

Having made positive progress last summer, including winning her first matches at Flushing Meadows since lifting the trophy five years ago, it has been a frustrating 12 months for Raducanu with more persistent physical issues.

After a foot injury severely hampered her pre-season training, Raducanu then spent two-and-a-half months off court with a post-viral illness after initially falling unwell in early February.

She finally returned for the end of the clay-court season having rehired Andrew Richardson, the coach who guided her to the US Open title, but the pair's time on court together has been limited.

Sports.title: More European countries’ FAs withdraw support for Infantino as pressure intensifies
Sports.content:
European countries began turning their backs on Gianni Infantino as moves intensified across the globe to end his crisis-hit tenure as Fifa president.

The Football Association was the highest-profile of several Uefa member associations to drop its support for Infantino’s proposed re-election next year. It will write to Fifa confirming it no longer endorses Infantino for a fourth term in charge after the intense controversy surrounding his failed plan to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.

Wales and Serbia publicly confirmed that they had withdrawn their backing, following a lead taken by Finland last week. Along with the FA, those federations had all previously written letters in favour of Infantino prolonging his tenure but patience has run out across the continent. The Swedish Football Association, which was one of five European FAs not to write letters of support, issued a statement confirming it would oppose his candidature in the election in March.

The FA had previously fallen into line behind Infantino, who will helm an extraordinary Fifa congress confirming the United Kingdom’s hosting of the 2035 Women’s World Cup in November if he is still in position. But it has been consistent in condemning his doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, publicly and in private representations. On Saturday it called for a “full and robust review of Fifa’s leadership and governance”, and its latest move is a further escalation.

It is joined by the Football Association of Wales, which said in a statement: “The Football Association of Wales hereby confirms its withdrawal of support for the candidature of Mr Gianni Infantino for re-election as Fifa president for the 2027-2031 term.

“The recent failures in good governance, processes, leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgment have led us to a position where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to remain at the helm of world football. Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.”

View image in fullscreen Several Uefa nations are mobilising against the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino. Photograph: Pierre Albouy/Reuters

Striking a similar tone, the Football Association of Serbia explained recent events had “seriously damaged the reputation and credibility of both Fifa and its president”, saying a withdrawal was “the only logical and rational step”.

In a sign that consensus may not be easy to achieve, the Swiss Football Association stopped short of abandoning its countryman. Instead it asked for “another personal exchange of views with the Fifa president” and said it would “continue to review the developments surrounding Fifa” before the leadership election.

More countries are, however, expected to withdraw their support for Infantino in what amounts to a vote of no confidence. The intended effect is for the embattled president to resign although some insiders are braced for a drawn-out process. While the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Concacaf, which runs the sport in North and Central America, have both strongly criticised Infantino there has been no move by any of their individual federations to call back letters in favour of his re-election.

Ensuring they do so may be critical to the ongoing efforts to remove Infantino quickly. There is acknowledgement in some parts of Europe that other continents should be seen taking the lead if enough of a groundswell for his departure is to be reached. Only 15 countries have publicly supported Infantino since he shelved the FFE project on Saturday but there is an appetite to form a broad coalition against his re-election quickly.

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, is a contender to take over if Infantino is deposed. Montagliani is understood to be in consensus with the Uefa and AFC hierarchies that new leadership is needed at Fifa.

View image in fullscreen Victor Montagliani consoles Lionel Messi after the World Cup final. Photograph: Will Oliver/EPA

In another blow to Infantino, lawyers acting for Uefa have ordered him and other staff to identify, locate and preserve all documents related to the FFE scheme. Their letter includes Arsène Wenger, the Fifa chief of global football development, among those obliged to comply with its order. It says Uefa is “actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints ... arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan”.

Thrive Eternal, the investment firm that had been expected to lead a group taking a 20% stake in FFE, is believed to have been sent a similar letter. JP Morgan, which was enlisted for an advisory role in the scheme, is also understood to have received an order related to FFE.

On Monday afternoon the US State Department denied reports that Infantino had been scheduled to meet Marco Rubio, the United States secretary of state, in a bid to stoke up support for his continued reign as president.

Sports.title: Benjamin Nygren edges Celtic past Dundee for winning start to title defence
Sports.content:
Benjamin Nygren was quickly back on the goal trail as Celtic began the defence of their Premiership title with a 1-0 home win over Dundee. Before the game, Celtic fans cheered as the captain, Callum McGregor, unfurled the flag which confirmed again a 14th title win in 15 seasons.

It was all a bit flat in a first half with Martin O’Neill’s side struggling to get into their stride as the visitors posed problems. However, the Sweden midfielder Nygren, so prolific last season with 21 goals, struck with a close-range header in the 52nd minute and the goal proved enough to keep the three points in Glasgow as a new season got up and running for the champions.

Celtic supporters continue to call for new recruits to the squad but Camilo Durán, the Colombian striker signed from Qarabag reportedly for £5.5m, and Kasper Høgh, the Denmark forward who cost a club-record £11m plus add-ons from Bodø/Glimt, made their debuts.

Alistair Johnston and Arne Engels, both attracting transfer interest, also started for the champions while the Dundee keeper Owen Goodman came in for his debut.

Høgh fired wide in the ninth minute after being set up by Nygren, then the Dane redirected an effort from Nygren past a post. Moments later at the other end, as the ball bounced around Celtic’s penalty area, Dundee’s Charlie Reilly hit the side netting with a shot from 12 yards.

Steven Pressley’s well-drilled outfit were finding joy with the high ball, either crosses or throw-ins and in the 33rd minute defender Owen Bevan got his head to the ball in the box but the Celtic keeper Viljami Sinisalo gathered comfortably.

View image in fullscreen Benjamin Nygren races away in delight after scoring the winner for Celtic. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Five minutes later, Engels missed the best chance of the match to that point, unmarked in the visitors’ box, he headed a cross from Kieran Tierney past a post, before the Celtic left-back drew a fine save from Goodman with a close-range drive.

The home side faltered at the start of the second half but when Tierney curled in a cross from the left, Nygren headed past Goodman from inside the box and the growing anxiety subsided.

Quick Guide Celtic to play LASK in Champions League playoff Show Celtic will face LASK in the Champions League playoffs. Martin O’Neill’s side were drawn out first against the Austrian champions. The Linz-based club won the Austrian Bundesliga for the second time last season, finishing two points ahead of the defending champions Sturm Graz. The Hoops avoided a potential rematch with Kairat Almaty, who knocked Celtic out on penalties at the same stage last season following a goalless 210 minutes of action. The first leg will take place on 18/19 August, with the second leg the following week. PA Media Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

O’Neill’s side probed with more purpose, the fans got more excited and the noise levels increased while Dundee’s attacks were more sporadic and less convincing, although the pace of Joe Bevan was cause for concern for the Parkhead defence. In the 67th minute Goodman threw himself down to his right to save a long-distance drive from forward Yang Hyun-jun.

Celtic remained in control but as the second goal refused to arrive and the clock ticked on, some nerves returned. In the 82nd minute, Sinisalo pulled off a terrific save from the Dundee substitute Ashley Hay’s glancing header.

Høgh missed another chance when he slid a shot past a post from six yards before McGregor cracked the upright with an effort from inside Dundee’s penalty area; James Forrest bent the rebound wide of the target.

Sports.title: Charlton up for sale again as US owners look to cash in after three years
Sports.content:
Charlton’s US owners have put the club up for sale just three years after taking over at the Valley. The ownership group is understood to have engaged Oakwell Sports Advisory to find what would be the club’s fifth owners in the past six years.

In a sales deck sent to potential investors, which has been seen by the Guardian, Oakwell describes Charlton as “the last remaining football club upside opportunity in London”. Oakwell also claims that Charlton would provide new owners with an opportunity for five to 10 times equity growth through promotion to the Premier League, commercial expansion and investment in women’s football.

Oakwell did the deal that led to the Bournemouth owner, Bill Foley, buying the Prem rugby club Exeter Chiefs this summer, and is helping the Rugby Football League to secure external investment.

Charlton’s location in south-east London is a plus, while the Valley is a modern stadium with a capacity of 27,000, but the club do not own the ground, which belongs to the hated former owner Roland Duchâtelet. Having considered looking at alternative sites, last year Charlton extended the lease on the Valley until 2040.

Charlton have repeatedly changed hands since the fans forced out Duchâtelet in 2020, when the club had three owners in quick succession. Duchâtelet sold Charlton to East Street Investments for just £1 in January 2020, but the consortium led initially by the former football agent Matt Southall collapsed amid in‑fighting and an acrimonious court case, with the club eventually bought by the Danish-American business Thomas Sandgaard later that year. In 2023, Sandgaard sold Charlton to a group of five US investors called Global Football Partners (GFP) led by Gabriel Brener via their UK subsidiary, SE7 Partners.

Under GFP, Charlton returned to the Championship for the first time in five years in 2025 by winning the League One playoff final at Wembley, while the women’s team were promoted to WSL1 last season.

GFP paid around £15m for Charlton three years ago but, having invested in the stadium and training ground and seen Nathan Jones’s side consolidate the club in the Championship, will be looking for several times that figure. Charlton declined to comment.

Sports.title: Newcastle reject first bid from Arsenal for captain Bruno Guimarães
Sports.content:
Arsenal have stepped up their attempt to sign Bruno Guimarães by finally beginning formal transfer negotiations and making an opening offer, which Newcastle have rejected.

Guimarães met Newcastle’s incoming manager, Matthias Jaissle, for the first time on Monday at the team’s pre-season training camp at La Manga after a post-World Cup holiday in Brazil.

There had been suggestions that the 28-year-old midfielder would fly to London for a medical at Arsenal, but instead he boarded a commercial flight to Spain.

Once at La Manga, he was expected to tell Jaissle of his determination to swap Tyneside for north London, but everything hinges on whether Arsenal are prepared to meet Newcastle’s valuation for a player with two years remaining on his contract.

While executives at Arsenal believe Guimarães is worth a maximum of £70m – and a bid in that ballpark was rejected on Monday – Newcastle value their captain at around £80m.

If some sort of compromise seems likely given Arsenal – negotiating, initially, through intermediaries – have spent much of this summer in pursuit of a midfielder at the top of Mikel Arteta’s shopping list, Newcastle are under no pressure to sell.

View image in fullscreen Guimarães has had several battles with Arsenal over the past few seasons. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

Indeed, having sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively this summer, they would prefer to offer Jaissle the benefit of Guimarães’s talent and experience as he rebuilds the squad.

The 38-year-old was believed to be keen to assess the Brazilian’s mindset as he begins preparations for the opening Premier League match at home against Liverpool two weeks on Sunday. Although the former Al‑Ahli and RB Salzburg manager is still to be officially confirmed as Howe’s successor, Jaissle has been with his new squad since arriving in southern Spain on Saturday. Newcastle are waiting for the completion of some final paperwork before formalising his appointment.

One signing completed by Newcastle on Monday involved Lukas Hornicek’s £26m move from Braga. The 24-year-old Czechia goalkeeper is expected to replace Nick Pope as the team’s first choice, with Pope now likely to leave St James’ Park.

Hornicek caught Newcastle’s eye after seven clean sheets during Braga’s run to the Europa League semi-finals last season. At 6ft 6in, he cuts an imposing figure in goal and has been highly praised for the sort of high-calibre footwork that should improve Newcastle’s ability to play out from the back.

Hull had hoped to recruit Hornicek, but he turned down a move to the promoted club last month.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Chelsea sell Trevoh Chalobah and sign Jordan Henderson
Sports.content:
Trevoh Chalobah’s long association with Chelsea is to end after Como agreed a deal worth an initial £25.7m. The England defender’s departure was agreed on the same day the club completed the signing of Jordan Henderson.

Chalobah made 105 Premier League appearances for Chelsea and established himself as a first-team option during a number of turbulent periods for the club. The move will be seen as a coup for Como’s head coach, Cesc Fàbregas, with the former Chelsea midfielder pushing to bring the centre-back to Italy.

The clubs have settled on a package that includes £5.1m in performance-related add-ons and a sell-on clause. For Chelsea, the departure of another homegrown academy product – Chalobah, now 27, has been at the club since he was eight – will generate pure profit, a key factor as they continue to balance the books.

On another busy day in west London the new manager, Xabi Alonso, welcomed Henderson to the club after his departure from Brentford. The 36-year-old joined on a free transfer after playing 34 times for the Bees last season, a campaign that also earned him a place in England’s World Cup squad.

“Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down,” Henderson said. “I was so impressed with how much the ownership ‌want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.”

View image in fullscreen With Jordan Henderson following Danny Welbeck to Chelsea, the club have shown a clear intent to sign more experienced players. Composite: Guardian Picture Desk

Henderson came through Sunderland’s academy before joining Liverpool in 2011. He spent 12 seasons at Anfield, playing 492 games in all competitions, and captained the team to Champions League victory in 2019 and the ‌Premier League title in 2020.

He left Liverpool for Al-Ettifaq in the Saudi Pro League in 2023, but ​six months later joined Ajax. He moved on again last summer to join Brentford.

Henderson played six minutes at the World Cup before breaking an arm in a post-match accident after England’s last-16 victory against Mexico. He is Chelsea’s fourth English signing of the transfer window, after the record acquisition of Morgan Rogers ​from Aston Villa, Danny Welbeck from Brighton and the teenager Harrison Bettoni from Wigan.Gonzalo García has joined Fulham from Real Madrid for £34m on a five-year contract. The deal, which includes an option for the club to extend by a further 12 months, sees the 22-year-old Spanish striker reunite with former Real head coach, Alvaro Arbeloa. Garcia said: “I’m very grateful, very happy to be here. I have to thank the board and Arbeloa for the trust they’ve put in me, and I’m very, very excited to start.”Garcia had been with Real since joining in 2014 aged 10 and made 39 appearances for Los Blancos last season, registering eight goals and three assists.

César Palacios has also made the switch from the Bernabéu to Craven Cottage for an undisclosed fee. The 21-year-old attacking midfielder will wear the No 8 shirt.

Sports.title: Marc Skinner may have been a Marmite manager but Manchester United’s budget was spread thin | Tom Garry
Sports.content:
“If we want to compete at this later stage, we’ve seen what we’ve got to do, as a club. It’s our choice now, isn’t it? We have to look at what we seriously want to achieve … It takes, sometimes, a punch in the face to wake up.”

Those were the words of the Manchester United head coach Marc Skinner after his side went out of the Women’s Champions League with elimination by Bayern Munich in April. Just over four months later, the bruise from that punch has faded, but so, it would seem, have the club’s ambitions to compete in the transfer market, and Skinner has decided not to get into the ring for another round.

The 43-year-old wanted that run to the quarter-finals to trigger further investment in the starting team. The club, though, feel that the levels of spending in the transfer market are unsustainable and therefore want to focus on developing young, homegrown talent. Once that juxtaposition was firmly established this summer, it was inevitable that Skinner and United were likely to part company, as they did on Monday, to end his five years in charge.

United’s Marmite manager, Skinner certainly divided opinion in the WSL. He was the league’s longest-serving manager by a distance, but arguably also the most heavily maligned coach online. In the sport, though, there are coaches who admire the job he did on – according to the most recent set of WSL clubs’ financial accounts – a little over a third of the playing budget of Chelsea and around half that of Arsenal’s.

For members of the media, Skinner’s press conferences will probably be one of the most memorable aspects of his tenure, unique because of the extensive length of the former Birmingham and Orlando head coach’s answers. For example, before the 2025 Women’s FA Cup final, one of his answers was 1,000 words long.

View image in fullscreen Marc Skinner instructs his players in a Champions League tie against Brann in September 2025. Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters

To some, his determination to provide long, considered responses was a sign of his thoughtfulness and showed an admirable desire to be transparent. To others, his drawn-out answers demonstrated an inability to be concise and this communication problem dogged his relationship with the fans throughout much of his tenure. Often, unintentionally, his words would irritate sections of the fanbase. In 2025, one former United player privately described Skinner as a “great bloke, but he goes on a bit” and it is fair to say not every player liked his team-talk style, while others enjoyed his passion.

On the pitch, the 2022-23 season, Skinner’s second, was the club’s strongest as they finished second in the table, boosted by a robust defensive record, conceding 12 times in 22 games, and they came within a whisker of winning the title. Then there was the comparatively low moment of languishing down in fifth in the 2024-25 campaign, counteracted by winning 2025’s Women’s FA Cup, lifting United’s first major women’s trophy.

Yet, whether you loved him or loathed him at Leigh Sports Village, Skinner overachieved at United on a purely pound-for-pound basis, reaching four domestic cup finals – including three consecutive Women’s FA Cup finals – despite typically operating on a mid-table budget for much of his incumbency. He was certainly not every player’s cup of tea, and there will be lessons he will need to learn from the highs and lows of his five years at the club, but now that both of the coaches who have managed United’s women in the modern era have wanted to leave, in part, because of funding issues, there are questions for the club’s hierarchy to answer.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In the 2024-25 season, of the eight WSL clubs to publish their wage bills via Companies House, United’s ranked fourth for expenditure, and it was a similar story in 2023-24. For next season, they will operate on a far smaller wage bill than the big-spending independent club London City Lionesses and there are understood to be fears held among some staff at United that they are soon likely to be outbid for players’ wages by Tottenham too.

The club embarked on new direction this summer, establishing a long-term aim to sustainably succeed with young homegrown players and play exciting football in line with what they believe are the traditions of the club and their culture. Yet that seems to be at odds with the targets outlined during the 2024-25 season when their “Project 150” included a “Mission 1” for the women to win a first WSL title by the club’s 150th anniversary in 2028.

Whoever comes in as the club’s head coach – and an appointment is likely to happen quickly, with background checks having already been carried out on candidates – they will need to be prepared to work with youngsters and develop them rather than trying to sign established, international stars. They will also have to accept that key first-team players – such as Melvine Malard who was sold to Chelsea this summer – may well be poached by a rival.

Sports.title: Vinícius Júnior to Arsenal doesn’t make sense. That’s why it may work | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Sometimes what is needed is something different.

There is a long history in football of counterintuitive thinking being successful, of the benefits of creative tension, of adding grit to the oyster to generate the pearl, but even so, the news that talks between Vinícius Júnior and Arsenal on personal terms are progressing comes as something of a shock. Mikel Arteta’s great followers of a blueprint adding a free spirit like the Brazilian? Really?

Vinícius returns to Real Madrid this week after the World Cup with movement on his future expected relatively soon. He has 12 months remaining on his contract and Madrid are keen either to tie him down to a new deal or to sell him while he will attract at least some kind of fee. As their squad rebuild goes on under José Mourinho, Madrid’s position is readily understandable. They have already signed Bernardo Silva, Denzel Dumfries, Marc Cucurella and Ibrahima Konaté this summer; removing Vinícius’s £420,000 a week (about $30m/year) basic wages significantly increases their financial headroom.

There’s been a sense since Kylian Mbappé joined Madrid two years ago that having him and Vinícius together left the squad unbalanced. Why would you need two rapid forwards who both prefer to cut in from the left, particularly when Rodrygo, who tended to be consigned to the right before tearing his ACL in March, would also prefer to play from the left? Yan Diomandé is likely to confirm his move to Real Madrid from RB Leipzig this week. Although the Ivorian has said he would rather play on the right, he too has spent much of his career on the left.

More broadly, Vinícius does not seem a natural Mourinho player. His pace and technical excellence are undoubted, but he has never been the most diligent at fulfilling his defensive responsibilities. Mourinho likes a forward who can improvise, and worked successfully with Cristiano Ronaldo at Madrid, but it’s difficult to see how he could indulge more than one such player at a time, and Mbappé will take precedence.

But those concerns about tracking, about the willingness to stick to a gameplan, about the capacity to retain possession are just as relevant to Arteta as they are to Mourinho – arguably more so, as Arteta believes far more in structured attacking planning than Mourinho. Is Vinícius, after years of freedom at Madrid, really going to accept those rigid structures?

It’s been fairly clear since the second half of last season that Arsenal would be looking to strengthen their left side. The sale of Leandro Trossard to Beşiktaş did not come as a huge surprise. The 31-year-old is reliable and played a valuable role last season, starting 21 of the 38 league games and coming off the bench on a further 10 occasions, but there is not much stardust about him. Gabriel Martinelli started 11 league games and came off the bench 19 times, and his pace can be a great asset, but it’s no longer clear that he is at his best on the left. The signing of Eberechi Eze last summer looked like an attempt to add creativity from that flank but his tendency to drift infield when Arteta needs his left-sided forward to stay wide meant that by the end of the season he tended to be used centrally behind a striker.

Vinícius would give Arsenal greater attacking thrust. At his best, under Carlo Ancelotti, he could transform a game in seconds. His pace, dribbling ability and finishing mean that no matter how stale a game seems to have gone, no matter how under pressure his team may be, they are never more than seven or eight seconds from a potential goal. It’s easy to see why Arsenal are tempted by him. He would immediately be their highest-profile player, adding a sense of direction to a summer that, at least from a recruitment point of view, has seemed to be drifting. Arsenal missed out on Morgan Rogers, who joined Chelsea, while Julián Álvarez, who would seem a much more natural fit on the Arsenal left, appears more likely to go to Barcelona, if sufficient financial levers can be pulled.

But the fact Vinícius is not a natural fit may be part of the attraction. It was, after all, the season after signing Erling Haaland, far from a typical Pep Guardiola player, that Manchester City won the treble. A player who does not quite fit, who kicks against the general philosophy, can make a process team less predictable. The friction can produce valuable sparks.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Haaland, it’s fair to say, is a different personality from Vinícius and, as a center-forward, there was never a worry he was going to leave his full-back exposed. Vinícius is a bigger risk. He would certainly be an expensive one, not just in terms of his own salary but the inflationary pressure that could have on wages at the club more generally.

But he would also add a dash Arsenal have lacked that would make the accusation of being dead-ball plodders hard to sustain. And with Trossard gone, there is a left-sided hole that needs filling.

Sports.title: ‘They are terrified’: Como spark row with fans over controversial new stadium policy
Sports.content:
Como, the surprise package of last season’s Serie A, who qualified for the Champions League for the first time, will revoke season tickets from fans who fail to attend four home matches, under a series of new rules that have sparked a row among supporters.

The club, coached by the former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fàbregas, said on Monday that supporters “who miss more than three home matches without what it considers a valid reason risk having their season tickets revoked”. Another new rule bans fans from wearing the opposing team’s shirts or scarves anywhere in the stadium except the away section.

“Demand for tickets far exceeds supply and, for that reason, I asked the club to find ways to ensure tickets for the [Giuseppe Sinigaglia stadium] end up in the hands of genuine Como supporters – those who want to be there to back the team,” the chair, Mirwan Suwarso, said in a lengthy statement on Instagram.

“There have been too many occasions when away fans have celebrated inside our home sections, while Como supporters, who would have proudly backed the team, were unable to get a ticket.”

On the ban on wearing rival teams’ shirts, scarves and other symbols outside the away end, the club said the measure was introduced for safety reasons. “Our aim is to make the Sinigaglia the true home of our fans and a fortress for our team,” said Suwarso. “We want to ensure the Sinigaglia remains a place where grandparents feel comfortable bringing their grandchildren, where families can enjoy football together, and where passion never crosses the line into disrespect.”

On social media, many criticised the measures as overly harsh, arguing that work commitments, health issues or family responsibilities can prevent people from attending matches without making them any less loyal to the club.

La Provincia, Como’s local newspaper, said its newsroom had received dozens of calls and emails from concerned supporters. “Some worried about health problems or being unable to attend because of bad weather, as well as people who frequently travel for work,” the newspaper wrote. “They are terrified and all asking the same question: will our season tickets be taken away?”

Italy’s national newspaper, Corriere della Sera, reporting reactions from supporters on social media, quoted one fan asking: “Do we need to be accompanied by our parents when we hand in our excuse, like at school?”

In the 2018-19 season, Como were in Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football, after going bankrupt twice in the previous 15 years. Last season, the small northern Italian club finished fourth after an extraordinary campaign, producing a series of outstanding performances that surprised the football world.

Sports.title: David Sullivan 'advised to stay away from West Ham's London Stadium' amid fears of fan unrest following Panorama investigation into owner's alleged sexual misconduct
Sports.content:
David Sullivan 'advised to stay away from West Ham's London Stadium' amid fears of fan unrest following Panorama investigation into owner's alleged sexual misconduct

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

West Ham owner David Sullivan is reportedly set to defy orders to stay away from the club's London Stadium amid fears of fan unrest following allegations of sexual misconduct.

Sullivan, 77, was the subject of a BBC Panorama and The Times investigation earlier this year, which alleged sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour by the Hammers owner against seven women.

Sullivan denies any wrongdoing.

West Ham play their home matches at the London Stadium and the BBC reports that venue bosses had 'recommended' to the club that Sullivan does not attend home matches over concerns of fan unrest.

The stadium has also reportedly asked for advance notice of any planned visits so as to implement further safety and operational measures.

The report adds, however, that the billionaire businessman is expected to defy the request and has told London Stadium this.

David Sullivan is reportedly set to defy orders to stay away from West Ham's London Stadium

Sullivan stepped down as joint chairman of West Ham shortly before Panorama's investigation went to air, insisting he wanted to focus on fighting 'factually incorrect and entirely false, decades-old allegations concerning my personal life.'

The 77-year-old is the Championship club's largest shareholder.

The investigation found that Sullivan has been banned from contact with the club's women's and youth teams for the past three years due to safeguarding concerns after a historical allegation into his alleged conduct was raised with the FA in 2023.

Sullivan has denied the allegation and says he has never met any academy or women's player 'one-to-one' during his 16-year tenure at West Ham.

A spokesperson for London Stadium said that 'following media reports at the end of the season regarding a safeguarding matter being managed by the club, London Stadium sought further information to ensure it could fulfil its own safeguarding responsibilities'.

The spokesperson added that West Ham had responded, saying the 'matter was investigated and that the club does not consider there to be an ongoing safeguarding risk associated with Mr Sullivan attending the stadium'.

The London Stadium upheld its recommendation that Sullivan stay away from games due to the risk of "potential for demonstrations and anti-social behaviour by some spectators".

West Ham start their season on Saturday August 8 in the Carabao Cup against Portsmouth at the London Stadium.

Daily Mail Sport has contacted West Ham for comment.

Sports.title: Plot to 'paralyse' Gianni Infantino: FIFA president's opponents 'form alliance to stage their own international tournaments if he refuses to step down' after World Cup sell-off disgrace
Sports.content:
The leaders of UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) have reportedly formed an alliance aimed at toppling Gianni Infantino.

The FIFA president is under huge pressure after he was forced to abandon a hugely controversial proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup to a group led by Josh Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared, following a major revolt from the footballing world.

UEFA subsequently declared a loss of confidence in the Italian-Swiss administrator, while the English and Welsh FA are among several countries to withdraw their support for his re-election in next March's elections.

This has left Infantino fighting for his job, and he reportedly held crunch talks with the White House on Monday in a bid to help him survive.

And now, according to The Times, the leaders of the three confederations are preparing to 'paralyse FIFA' if he refuses to resign.

The report adds that they have several plans in place if the FIFA President insists on remaining in power and seeking re-election at next March's election.

Gianni Infantino's opponents have formed an alliance in an attempt to force him to resign

The alliance includes the leaders of UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC (pictured - Infantino with his UEFA counterpart Aleksander Ceferin in 2024)

This includes being prepared to stage their own rival international competitions, while they are also willing to impose a 'government boycott'.

This would effectively mean they would refuse to either ratify FIFA decisions or be involved in council and committee meetings.

A source told The Times: 'Everyone is very determined he needs to go, and if not we will take all the necessary steps [to remove him from power].

'That includes future international competitions - would the big South American countries prefer to play France or Spain, or Lebanon or Djibouti? Everyone is very determined, there are no backward steps now.'

It is also believed that with several countries withdrawing their support for Infantino, he has only secured the backing of around 15 nations so far.

Back in the summer, it was understood that the 56-year-old had the support of nearly all of the 211 FIFA members for his re-election in March. He needs 106 votes to win.

No candidates have yet come forward to challenge him though, and they only have until November 18 to do so.

If a significant number of nations called for Infantino to quit, it may help generate support for an emergency FIFA council meeting.

The English and Welsh FA are among the nations to withdraw their support for Infantino

Daily Mail Sport also reported earlier on Monday how several European nations, including England and Wales, had formally withdrawn their backing for the beleaguered football chief.

At the weekend, the FA had called for 'a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently'.

A statement from the Welsh FA on Monday then read: 'The Football Association of Wales hereby confirms its withdrawal of support for the candidature of Mr. Gianni Infantino, for re-election as FIFA President for the 2027–2031 term.

'The recent failures in good governance, processes, leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgement have led us to a position where Mr. Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to remain at the helm of world football. Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.'

Serbia, Sweden and Finland also publicly withdrew their support, although Morocco, Qatar, Lebanon, Kuwait and Sri Lanka were among those to back Infantino.

The latest update in this saga comes after UEFA sent Infantino a legal letter on Friday, where it threatened legal action over the abandoned plot, before adding that documents relating to the plan, known as FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), must be preserved.

The letter to Infantino read: 'Uefa hereby gives formal notice that it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints (together, the “proceedings”) arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa and all related matters as further described below.

'You and Fifa are required to take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa’s possession, custody, or control.'

UEFA went on to warn FIFA that 'any destruction, deletion, alteration, concealment or loss of relevant materials' after their letter 'may constitute spoliation of evidence'.

They then refused to rule out further action if any of the aforementioned actions took place, but the letter itself is not legal action.

The letter also insisted that FIFA must ensure that certain individuals, including Infantino, Arsene Wenger, FIFA's chief of global football development, secretary general Mattias Grafstrom and Kevin Lamour, FIFA's chief operating officer, 'specifically preserve all such materials in their possession'.

UEFA later confirmed to Daily Mail Sport that a document preservation letter was sent.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes confirms arrival in La Manga as Newcastle REJECT Arsenal bid, Chelsea agree £26m deal to sell Trevoh Chalobah to Como... and Fulham complete £44m swoop for Real Madrid duo: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Former Man United coach lands new job at Stockport

Former Manchester United coach Rene Meulensteen has been appointed as Stockport County’s new director of football methodology.

The role will see Meulensteen oversee Stockport's football philosophy and coaching methodology working day-to-day with both the first team and academy.

The 62-year-old Dutch coach arrives at Edgeley Park from a World Cup campaign where he was assistant coach to the Iraq national team.

Fulham snap up Real Madrid stars

Fulham confirmed the twin signings of £36m striker Gonzalo Garcia and £8.5m midfielder Cesar Palacios late on Monday night.

Fulham have confirmed the £36m signing of striker Gonzalo Garcia from Real Madrid

The pair have signed five-year deals with the option to extend by a further 12 months.

'I'm very grateful, very happy to be here', Garcia told the club website.

'I have to thank the board and Arbeloa for the trust they've put in me, and I'm very, very excited to start.'

Palacios said: 'I am very emotional to be here. I believe it is the perfect step in my career.

'The Club is showing a lot of trust in me, and I'm going to show it on the pitch.'

West Ham in market for Spurs outcast

West Ham are among the clubs interested in signing Manor Solomon from Tottenham, as first reported in Window Watch last week.

Solomon has impressed Roberto de Zerbi during a pre season tour of New Zealand and Australia.

De Zerbi knows the Israel international well because they worked together at Shakhtar Donetsk but the winger is set to leave after failing to hold down a place in three years at Spurs.

At 27, he is only interested in a permanent move, having spent last season on loan at Villarreal and Fiorentina and the previous season on loan at Leeds, where he sparkled as they won promotion from the Championship to the Premier League.

Fiorentina retain an interest despite not taking up the option on a permanent deal after his loan.

West Ham are among the clubs interested in signing Manor Solomon from Tottenham

Others are also monitoring the situation, and Spurs have to sell players to clear space in De Zerbi's squad and generate more income.

West Ham are in the market for a winger after selling Crysencio Summerville, but captain Jarrod Bowen has committed his future to the Hammers despite relegation.

MATT BARLOW

Preston boss hits out with Whiteman set for exit to Wrexham

Preston North End have accepted a £3million bid from Wrexham for their wantaway captain Ben Whiteman.

Manager Paul Heckingbottom voiced his displeasure at the weekend, saying Whiteman had crossed a line after telling them he had played his last game for the club in an effort to force through the move.

'Ben knew there was a line I didn't want him to cross and unfortunately he has,' Heckingbottom told BBC Radio Lancashire. 'There's a valuation on him, I just hope for Ben's sake that Wrexham are willing to pay it otherwise he's put himself in a sticky situation. He's made his bed. I'm not bothered as long as I get another player.'

The 30-year-old midfielder is now free to have a medical and complete the transfer, with personal terms not expected to be a problem.

The deal is expected to go through in the next 48 hours and Preston are looking to reinvest the money in another three or four new signings this summer.

Paul Heckingbottom says Ben Whiteman has 'crossed a line' in making his move

Hammers plot £18m bid to land Parrott

West Ham are preparing to outbid European rivals to sign former Tottenham striker Troy Parrott.

The Hammers want to bolster their attack quickly with the new Championship season looming and after being rebuffed for Sunderland's Wilson Isidor, are targeting AZ Alkmaar forward Parrott.

The Republic of Ireland international has interest from Ajax, Como, PSV Eindhoven and Real Betis but Alkmaar are reluctant to sell to a Dutch rival.

The Hammers hope an offer of around £18million will be enough to fend off the competition.

Parrott struggled while at Spurs but after an initial loan to Excelsior Rotterdam he began to find his feet and has been prolific with Alkmaar since.

Read more on this story HERE

Troy Parrott celebrates winning the Johan Cruyff Shield with Alkmaar on Sunday

Henderson's relish as he joins Chelsea

Chelsea have announced the signing of 36-year-old Jordan Henderson, after he was allowed to leave Brentford with a year left on his deal.

'Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn't turn down,' Henderson said.

'I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.

For more on this story click HERE

Jordan Henderson signs on the dotted line as he joins Xabi Alonso's Chelsea revolution

Sunderland block the door to Isidor

West Ham have asked to take Sunderland winger Simon Adingra on loan, but the Wearsiders have no plans to sell forward Wilson Isidor.

West Ham have asked about both players but after initial conversations Sunderland have made it clear that they want to keep Haiti international Isidor.

Discussions are ongoing between the clubs over a straight loan for 24-year-old Ivory Coast international Adingra.

Despite interest from a host of clubs, however, Sunderland will not entertain offers for Isidor. The 25-year-old remains an integral part of their squad ahead of their season in European competition and the club believe he can build on an excellent World Cup with Haiti.

West Ham are continuing to discuss AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott while Lazio are interested in the Hammers' German international forward Niclas Fullkrug.

Wilson Isidor is back after the World Cup and Sunderland say he is not for sale despite interest

Como agree £26m Chalobah deal... as Napoli eye Badiashile

Chelsea and Como have agreed a £26million fee for defender Trevoh Chalobah.

The deal will include a further £5.2m in add-ons for the 27-year-old England centre-back who is expected to travel to Italy on Wednesday evening.

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile continues to attract interest from Napoli. The Blues are looking to recoup funds for the French centre-back as well as for Axel Disasi who has been the subject of talks with Crystal Palace and West Ham - both are discussing offers.

Disasi had a spell on loan at West Ham last season but ideally wants a top flight offer.

Chelsea hope to make progress with Rayo Vallecano over the purchase of left wing-back Pep Chavarria.

Trevoh Chalobah is on his way to Como, managed by former Blues star Cesc Fabregas

Newcastle reject Arsenal bid for Bruno as he joins Magpies in La Manga

Arsenal's opening bid for Bruno Guimaraes has been rejected by Newcastle. As reported earlier, the clubs are now in direct talks over a deal for Brazilian.

Guimaraes has landed in Spain and is travelling to report back for Newcastle's pre-season camp in La Manga today.

Newcastle's new manager Matthias Jaissle is at La Manga with the squad and wants to meet the captain.

Bruno Guimaraes is subject of interest from Arsenal but they have not yet made a formal offer

Guimaraes confirmed his arrival in Spain on Instagram on Monday evening

Bernardo gets shirty at Real

Bernardo Silva has arrived at Real Madrid as he joins up with Jose Mourinho's side. The 31-year-old left Manchester City at the end of last season.

The Portugal star, who has returned from the World Cup, was seen signing shirts for fans after medical tests.

Man United would loan out Chido Obi for game time

Manchester United are willing to send striker Chido Obi Martin out on loan this summer.

The 18-year-old Denmark U21 international had interest from Cologne earlier in the window, but they have moved to sign Jaiden Heskey from Manchester City and are lining up Tottenham winger Mikey Moore.

Chido Obi joined United from Arsenal's academy in 2024 and has made seven first-team appearances though failed to score.

United want to ensure his next club is one where he can develop properly with competitive game time.

Join the queue for Everton's Tim

Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam is attracting increasing interest from rival Premier League clubs and from abroad.

Coventry City, Hull City and Ipswich Town have all made enquiries while two Italian clubs have also asked about the 23-year-old.

Lazio tried to sign the former England U20 international in January.

Everton are continuing to discuss a deal for Arsenal's Christian Norgaard which, if completed, could pave the way for Iroegbunam to depart once a suitable offer comes in.

Everton paid around £9million to Aston Villa for Iroegbunam in 2024.

Tim Iroegbunam joined from Aston Villa two years ago

Coventry keen on Mudryk

Chelsea have received multiple approaches about Mykhailo Mudryk from clubs following the news of his return to football – including three from the Premier League.

Coventry City, managed by Frank Lampard, who worked with Mudryk at Stamford Bridge in 2023, are believed to be among those to have enquired, sources have told Daily Mail Sport.

All options are open between Mudryk and Chelsea this summer, including whether to send him out on loan after his sudden comeback from a doping suspension.

Sports.title: Revealed: The 46 senior players - and counting - Xabi Alonso must find room for at Chelsea as incoming manager faces selection headache ahead of the new season
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso will have to make sense of a Chelsea squad stuffed with a jaw-dropping 46 senior players ahead of the start of the 2026-27 season, according to the club's website - with the number rising as new signings join the pack. The incoming Blues manager has already overseen a number of eye-catching transfers since arriving at Stamford Bridge at the start of July, including the £117million deal for Morgan Rogers, and additional signings including Marco Palestra, Danny Welbeck, Maxence Lacroix and Jordan Henderson. But worryingly for the west London side, there have been few outgoings, with the only confirmed departures Marc Cucurella for Real Madrid, Tyrique George's permanent signing for Everton, and loans for Alejandro Garnacho, Jesse Derry, and Kendry Paez. As a result, Alonso must drastically slim down his cohort while ensuring that players are not left unsettled by joining a Chelsea's 'bomb squad' - a tactic former manager Enzo Maresca deployed last season. Those who were deemed to have no future under the Italian manager - who has since taken over from his mentor Pep Guardiola at Manchester City - were sent to train separately from the first team, and even ordered to use a separate dressing room. Big names including Raheem Sterling, Axel Disasi, Joao Felix and Ben Chilwell were among those to be considered permanently outcast under Maresca. Xabi Alonso faces a selection headache as Chelsea add yet more players to their stuffed ranks

Your browser does not support iframes.

Chelsea's hierarchy will have to organise yet more loans - or permanent deals - at pace ahead of their first match of the new Premier League season on August 24, with some positions seeing eight players fight over a starting berth, according to Chelsea's own list of senior players. Nicolas Jackson has swelled the strikers' ranks after returning from his season-long loan at Bayern Munich, alongside incoming Kazakh starlet Dastan Satpayev, who was signed by the club in February 2025 but only due to arrive in the Premier League in August. Satpayev is not however listed on the club's website, although he has already featured under Alonso - nor is Denner, a young Brazilian starlet who, like Satpayev, was signed in 2025 and is set to move now that he has turned 18. Up front, Emmanuel Emegha made the move from Chelsea's sister club Strasbourg and will compete with Welbeck, Marc Guiu, Liam Delap, and Joao Pedro for minutes too. Satpayev is not the only player under consideration for Alonso that is yet to don a Chelsea shirt in competitive action, beyond this summer's signings. Former Strasbourg loanee goalkeeper Mike Penders is a similar case, while Gabriel Slonina has had back-to-back-to-back loans since his 2022 move. Chelsea will also finally get their hands on Valentin Barco, who last summer was the subject of a botched signing to BlueCo - Chelsea's parent company - before eventually moving in a permanent deal to Strasbourg. Last week, Chelsea confirmed that they have signed the Argentina midfielder who taunted Jude Bellingham and earned a clip around the ear after England were knocked out of the World Cup. Mykhailo Mudryk has rejoined the Chelsea squad after his doping case was resolved Jordan Henderson's arrival has taken Chelsea's squad up to a staggering 46 players Alonso may also have made further work for himself by bringing a number of youth stars into the fold during Chelsea's pre-season tour. In the absence of established stars who went deep at the World Cup, such as Fernandez and captain Reece James, the Spaniard was able to keep a closer eye on academy stars listed as senior players at the club such as Reggie Watson, Reggie Walsh, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, Calvin Diakite, Olutaro Subuloye, Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, Landon Emenalo and Ted Curd, bringing nine in total to Australia and Asia. A final complication is added by the return of Mykhailo Mudryk, after the Ukrainian star's multi-year doping case was resolved just days ago. Happily for Alonso, some players have already attracted close interest from top-flight sides across Europe. Chelsea are in talks with Como over a move for Chalobah, and Crystal Palace and West Ham for Disasi - who is not even listed as a senior player on their website. Forgotten forward David Datro Fofana is also unlisted. Benoit Badiashile has also caught the eye of Napoli. The Blues will look to keep hold of Fernandez but have also set a punchy asking price of £120m for their vice-captain, with Real Madrid previously keeping tabs on him. Mudryk too could find his near future away from Stamford Bridge, with Daily Mail Sport reporting on Monday that three Premier League sides had made enquiries about the player following his return to football.

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan's 'overwhelmed' family release heartfelt statement following football world's gushing tributes for England legend after his death - and set up charity fundraiser in his honour
Sports.content:
Kevin Keegan's family has thanked everyone for their condolences following the death of the England legend.

Last month, Keegan died aged 75 after a battle with stomach cancer. He left behind his wife, of 51 years, Jean and their two daughters Laura Jane, 47, and Sarah Marie, 43.

News of the Liverpool and Newcastle hero's illness broke in January, and in June he revealed that he had stage four cancer - meaning it had spread to other parts of the body.

Since his death, tributes have poured into Keegan's family as the football world pays their respects.

And speaking about the amount of support they have received, the grateful Keegan family revealed they have been 'overwhelmed' by it all.

A statement from the Keegan family, issued by the League Managers Association, read: 'Following the devastating news of Kevin's passing, we would like to thank the vast number of people who have expressed condolences and shared their memories of Kevin in recent days.

Kevin Keegan's family has thanked everyone for their condolences following his death in July

Keegan pictured with his wife, Jean, who was by his side when he died last month

'As a family we have been truly overwhelmed by the volume of tributes and are grateful for them all. We will be holding a small private funeral in the coming weeks and request ongoing privacy and respect whilst we navigate this extremely difficult period as a family.

KEEGAN'S ILLUSTRIOUS CAREER Years Club Appearances Goals 1968–1971 Scunthorpe 124 18 1971–1977 Liverpool 230 68 1977–1980 Hamburg 90 32 1980–1982 Southampton 68 37 1982–1984 Newcastle United 78 48 1985 Blacktown City 2 1 Honours: Liverpool Football League First Division: 1972–73, 1975–76, 1976–77 FA Cup: 1973–74; runner-up: 1976–77 FA Charity Shield: 1974, 1976 European Cup: 1976–77 UEFA Cup: 1972–73, 1975–76 Hamburg Bundesliga: 1978–79 European Cup runner-up: 1979–80 Individual: Ballon d'Or: 1978, 1979 FWA Footballer of the Year: 1975–76 PFA Players' Player of the Year: 1981–82 Years Club Win% 1992-97 Newcastle United 55 1998-99 Fulham 62 1999-00 England 39 2001-05 Manchester City 44 2008 Newcastle 32 Honours: Newcastle United Football League First Division: 1992–93 Fulham Football League Second Division: 1998–99 Manchester City Football League First Division: 2001–02 Individual Premier League Manager of the Month: November 1993, August 1994, February 1995, August 1995, September 1995

'Details of a memorial service hosted by Newcastle United that will take place at a later date will be communicated in due course.'

A private funeral is due to take place in the next few weeks, while Newcastle will later host a memorial service for a man who was revered both as a player and as a manager on Tyneside.

The family have also requested, in lieu of flowers, donations to two charities close to the two-time Ballon d'Or winner's heart.

They have set up a GoFundMe Page asking for donations to the Christie Charity, which funds enhanced services, pioneering research, education and additional support services for cancer patients and their families, and Football Families for Justice, a charity set up by World Cup winner Nobby Stiles' son John to support former players suffering from neurodegenerative diseases caused by heading the ball.

Keegan made his name at Liverpool in a glittering playing career. He won 63 England caps and also managed Fulham and Manchester City.

He guided Newcastle to the Premier League during the first of two stints at St James' Park and came close to lifting the title, only to be pipped by Manchester United.

Keegan started his career at Scunthorpe before being signed for Liverpool by Bill Shankly in 1971, going on to win the First Division title three times as well as the FA Cup, the UEFA Cup twice and the 1977 European Cup.

Keegan was twice named European Footballer of the Year while at German club Hamburg and returned to England to play for Southampton and Newcastle before retiring as a player in 1984.

He won 63 England caps, scoring 21 goals, playing at the 1982 World Cup and was also later captain of the national team.

In 1992, Keegan made his first step into management at his former club Newcastle, guiding them into the Premier League and to within touching distance of the 1995-96 title only to miss out to Manchester United.

After leaving St James' Park in January 1997, a brief stint at Fulham followed before he became England manager in 1999, having initially taken on the job following Glenn Hoddle's departure.

Having overseen a disappointing Euro 2000 campaign, Keegan resigned on the back of defeat by Germany at Wembley Stadium, the last match at the national stadium before it was rebuilt.

After England he managed Manchester City for four years before then returning for a brief spell at Newcastle.
