Sports.title: Featured Comment: Is F1’s use of yellow flags in qualifying a safety concern? | Brief
Sports.content:
George Russell’s pole position in Austria created controversy as the Mercedes driver passed Max Verstappen’s crashed Red Bull during his flying lap, which race control opted to cover with only a single yellow flag. That meant Russell was able to lift briefly then continue and set his lap time.

A similar situation arose in the last round at the Hungaroring: again Verstappen caused a yellow flag, this time Andrea Kimi Antonelli passed by it and set his quickest time in Q3, but he was penalised for not backing off sufficiently.

But should Formula 1 be allowing drivers to improve their qualifying times at all when they pass yellow flags? AlanD is concerned:

This is a very unsatisfactory approach. Either they say a single yellow flag is advisory and leave it to the drivers to drive whatever speed they want, (and that is a bad idea), or they stop messing about and say we’ll just go straight to double yellows in future, and if you pass through the yellow section your lap time isn’t going to count no matter what, so get off that throttle. It may sound harsh, but the point of safety regs is to protect drivers and marshals. This shouldn’t be about how fast you are allowed to go whilst claiming you were complying with the regs.

AlanD

Sports.title: Where in Europe should F1 race if the final two rounds cannot go ahead? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has said Europe will be the series’ back-up plan if it cannot hold its final rounds in 2026.

The Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix on November 29th and December 6th respectively are in doubt as the war between the US and Iran continues and shows signs of spreading to other neighbouring countries.

Europe has several permanent tracks which haven’t hosted F1 races in 2026 and have the necessary FIA grade one licence. But there is an obvious problem: weather conditions are generally much cooler in Europe in the winter than they are in the Middle East.

So if F1 has to find two alternative venues at short notice, which would be best?

Algarve, Portugal

Previous F1 races: 2

Last F1 race: 2021 Portuguese Grand Prix

Formula 1 is already due to return to Portugal’s undulating Algarve circuit next year, so why not get a head start? Average temperatures in December are around 17C which is much warmer than many other venues in the region.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hockenheimring, Germany

Previous F1 races: 37

Last F1 race: 2019 German Grand Prix

The thought of Formula 1’s energy-starved 2026 cars attempting to lap the original high-speed Hockenheimring is comical. They would suit the butchered, post-2001 version better, but likely ambient temperatures in the low single digits would present a different challenge.

Imola, Italy

Previous F1 races: 32

Last F1 race: 2025 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix

Domenicali has indicated Imola is a likely venue and there are obvious reasons why: its infrastructure is bang up to date as F1 raced there last year and championship leader Andrea Kimi Antonelli hails from the area (as does the F1 boss). The temperatures will be on the cool side, however – potentially not much warmer than Hockenheim.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Jerez, Spain

Previous F1 races: 7

Last F1 race: 1997 European Grand Prix

Southern Spain offers the best chance of a reasonably warm race, with December temperatures in the 20C region. The tight, slow Jerez circuit would also help disguise the power deficit of the current cars.

Magny-Cours, France

Previous F1 races: 19

Last F1 race: 2008 French Grand Prix

Another track Formula 1 hasn’t visited in a long time which still has the necessary FIA grade to hold a grand prix. Central France would be rather chilly, though.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Motorland Aragon, Spain

Previous F1 races: None

The only FIA grade one track in Europe which F1 hasn’t raced at, which will inevitably count against it. Motorland Aragon is a rather typical modern autodrome-style circuit. Weather conditions in December would be a good chunk cooler than Jerez if F1 sprang a surprise by choosing this circuit as a venue for a third race in Spain this year.

Mugello, Italy

Previous F1 races: 1

Last F1 race: 2020 Tuscan Grand Prix

Mugello joined the F1 calendar as a one-off during the Covid-hit 2020 season and produced one of the year’s most memorable races, not least because a series of shunts meant several restarts were required. It would be very cool in December, though all those long, fast corners should help keep heat in the tyres.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Nurburgring, Germany

Previous F1 races: 19 (new circuit), 41 (total)

Last F1 race: 2020 Eifel Grand Prix

Another track F1 last visited during the pandemic, and one with an abundance of heritage. But like many other venues on this list, cold conditions would be a factor.

Paul Ricard, France

Previous F1 races: 18

Last F1 race: 2022 French Grand Prix

Paul Ricard was not F1’s most inspiring circuit to begin with: then it was shortened, then revived as a test track. F1 later returned to the longer track, albeit with a slow chicane before one of its best corners.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

I say

When F1’s calendar was disrupted six years ago by Covid-19, it was deeply unfortunate, but at least it was understood that the cause was mere misfortune. Advert | Become a Supporter & go ad-free It is deeply saddening to see a similar situation now playing out due to those who have decided to inflict pain, suffering and death on others. Compared to that, the rescheduling of a couple of motor races matters not one iota. However the fact remains that the outside world does affect life in F1’s ‘bubble’ and will continue to. I cannot think of many circuits you could drop Losail and Yas Marina for which would not constitute an improvement. Of course what I’d most like to see is F1 take in the most spectacular and demanding tracks available – Imola is a decent choice, but Mugello would be even better. Then reality kicks in. When F1 went to Mugello six years ago the cars were monstrously fast, not the feeble new generation which coast into the quick corners to save their batteries. Around a super-quick track like Mugello they would be badly starved of energy. Given that, arguably one of the slower tracks would suit the current cars better. But I’m not going to pretend I actually want to see F1 hunting out the tightest, slowest circuits so its drivers have plenty of opportunities to charge their batteries. I’ve more than had my fill of ‘clipping’ and ‘yo-yo racing’. Forget replacing Losail and Yas Marina, I’d rather the season ended two weeks early.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford Vs. Israil Madrimov: Did Star Power Sway The Scorecards?
Sports.content:
Madrimov never accepted that he had lost. Afterward, he said he believed he had done enough as the defending champion to deserve another opportunity. Promoter Eddie Hearn went further, criticizing the widest scorecard. He argued that the cleaner, more damaging punches largely came from Madrimov. In Hearn’s view, the challenger did not receive the benefit of close rounds because he shared the ring with one of boxing’s biggest attractions.

That argument is difficult to dismiss entirely because boxing has a long history of razor-close championship fights falling in favor of the established attraction. Judges are instructed to score only the action inside the ropes. When neither fighter clearly separates himself, reputation often becomes part of the conversation afterward. Crawford entered the bout as one of boxing’s biggest stars and one of the sport’s premier attractions. Madrimov was the defending champion, yet he remained an unfamiliar name to much of the audience.

The closeness of the contest keeps that discussion alive. If the exact same punches were thrown with Madrimov cast as the established superstar defending his title against a challenger moving up in weight, several of those swing rounds may have landed on the opposite side of the scorecards. A draw or narrow decision for Madrimov would not have been difficult to justify under that scenario.

That does not mean Crawford lacked a legitimate case for winning. His jab controlled long stretches of the fight. He maintained the higher work rate. Many viewers believed he closed stronger over the final rounds. Those factors gave the judges a reasonable foundation for their verdict, even if the margins remained controversial.

Perhaps that explains why Crawford-Madrimov still generates discussion two years later. This was not a fight where one boxer clearly outclassed the other. The official verdict will never change, but the discussion probably won’t either. In a fight decided by several swing rounds, Crawford’s jab and higher work rate gave judges a defensible path to his victory. Just as easy to imagine, however, is Madrimov keeping his title if those same close rounds had been judged without the weight of Crawford’s reputation hanging over them.

Sports.title: Paulie Malignaggi Explains How To Beat William Zepeda
Sports.content:
“The only thing about that kind of style is that you’re always in range to be touched. And maybe if it’s not touching you clean, it’s still kind of touching you and the numbers game may force you to be active because a guy like Zepeda who’s very active can give you a problem,” said Malignaggi on his Youtube channel. “The answer is changing range. There is different variations of defense in boxing. “I think the catch and shoot is a very solid way of defending. Roach, his main asset is the catch and shoot. It’s the blocking and holding position. He’s not a great reflex fighter and he’s not great with his legs either. The thing that troubles Zepeda a bit more is the in-and-out. He had a lot of trouble with this against Tevin Farmer, and he had a lot of trouble with this against Shakur Stevenson.”

In Malignaggi’s view, making Zepeda miss is just as important as blocking his punches. Catching shots on the gloves or arms still tells an aggressive pressure fighter he has found his range, encouraging him to keep throwing combinations. When an opponent steps completely out of range, Zepeda is more likely to overcommit, creating openings for sharp counters before he can reset his stance.

Roach stayed disciplined throughout the contest, but he rarely mixed lateral movement into his defense. He spent long stretches catching punches on his gloves and arms while searching for counter opportunities. The longer the fight continued, the more comfortable Zepeda became throwing combinations, giving him control of the contest on the scorecards.

Malignaggi’s breakdown explains why Roach struggled, but Zepeda’s recent fights suggest the tactical picture is more nuanced. Shakur Stevenson could not keep the action at long range, as Zepeda repeatedly closed the distance and forced exchanges. Shakur prevailed through sharp accuracy, precise timing, selective clinching, and elite defensive awareness rather than simply boxing from the outside all night.

Tevin Farmer found himself in a similar position. In the rematch, Zepeda repeatedly trapped him along the ropes and unleashed relentless combinations. Frequent clinching became Farmer’s best defense, allowing him to smother the attack and recover during several dangerous stretches when the sustained pressure left him close to being stopped.

The bigger story is Zepeda’s growing commitment to the body, an element Malignaggi barely touched on. That adjustment changes the entire equation because it punishes defensive habits that usually work against pressure fighters.

Leaning back is one of Shakur’s trademark defensive moves, taking his head out of danger against most opponents. Against Zepeda, however, that adjustment exposes the body. Every time Stevenson leaned away from punches upstairs, he created openings downstairs, where Zepeda found far more consistent success. Had he committed to that attack earlier instead of continuing to head-hunt, he may have made it even more difficult for Stevenson to stay mobile.

Roach ran into the same problem. His catch-and-shoot defense protected his head reasonably well early, but it did little to slow Zepeda’s work downstairs. As those punches accumulated, Roach lost mobility and spent more time directly in front of Zepeda, exactly where the Mexican pressure fighter is most dangerous.

The blueprint against Zepeda is more complicated than simply moving around the ring. Stevenson and Farmer both tried to keep him on the outside, yet he still forced extended exchanges by cutting off the ring and steadily breaking down their movement. Once opponents can no longer maintain that mobility, Zepeda’s relentless volume becomes far more difficult to contain.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Is America’s Biggest Boxing Star, Says Gareth A. Davies
Sports.content:
“Ryan Garcia is the lynch pin for the giant fights in America right now,” Davies said to talkSPORT Boxing. “The return of Gervonta Davis for a second fight. The return of Devin Haney and those two fighting each other… The fights there with Teofimo Lopez, the fights with Shakur Stevenson. For me, he’s the golden goose because he is probably the most well-known boxer in America right now.”

This perspective places Ryan ahead of some of the sport’s biggest American names. If Davies is right, Garcia has moved ahead of Devin Haney, Shakur Stevenson, and David Benavidez as the country’s biggest boxing attraction. All three have accomplished far more inside the ring than Garcia, yet Davies believes none currently matches his mainstream recognition.

Spencer Oliver shared a similar view.

“He is arguably the biggest name in American boxing right now,” Oliver said. “His social media presence is second to none. We live in a world of numbers today. When you have that and you can fight, and you’re the current WBC world champion, you’re going to be a star.”

Ryan’s September 12 title defense against Conor Benn gives him another opportunity to reinforce that status. A victory would keep him positioned for major crossover events against boxing’s elite.

Not everyone will agree with Davies. Many fans will argue Gervonta Davis remains American boxing’s biggest attraction despite his infrequent schedule. Ryan, however, continues to occupy the center of many discussions involving the sport’s biggest potential fights, giving Davies’ opinion a solid foundation.

Sports.title: Did The Long Count Cost Jack Dempsey The Heavyweight Title?
Sports.content:
Instead of going directly to a neutral corner, Dempsey remained near his fallen opponent, waiting for the opportunity to strike again. Barry repeatedly directed him away before beginning the count. Under the rules in effect that night, the referee could not start counting until the standing boxer reached a neutral corner. Ironically, Dempsey’s own camp had requested that specific rule before the rematch.

Film of the bout later showed Tunney remained on the canvas for roughly 13 to 14 seconds from the moment he fell until he got back to his feet at Barry’s count of nine. Those images have kept the controversy alive for generations. Supporters of Dempsey maintain a standard count would have ended the fight and returned the heavyweight championship to the former champion.

Tunney always rejected that conclusion, insisting he remained fully aware after the knockdown, picked up Barry’s count at “two,” and deliberately waited until nine before standing to give himself as much recovery time as possible. He later said he could have risen much sooner if necessary. Dempsey eventually accepted that explanation, even if many fans never did.

The debate expanded one round later when Tunney dropped Dempsey in the eighth. Barry immediately started counting instead of waiting for Tunney to move to a neutral corner. Critics viewed the different application of the rule as evidence of inconsistency, while others argued the sequence happened too quickly to alter the outcome.

Removing the seventh-round controversy from the equation, Tunney boxed brilliantly for most of the night. His footwork, jab, and movement inside the large ring repeatedly frustrated Dempsey before and after the knockdown.

After surviving the seventh-round scare, he quickly regained control, scored a knockdown of his own, and closed out a unanimous decision victory.

No replay or modern analysis has settled the argument because evidence supports both sides. One camp believes Dempsey lost the heavyweight championship by hesitating for only a few seconds. The other points to the rule book, Tunney’s own account, and the champion’s performance across the rest of the fight. Nearly 100 years later, boxing’s most famous long count remains one of the sport’s greatest unanswered questions.

Sports.title: Robert Garcia Eyes Big Names As Raymond Muratalla Begins 140 Pound Push
Sports.content:
A fight with Keyshawn faces one obvious problem. Since pulling out of his ordered WBO welterweight title fight against Devin Haney, Keyshawn has repeatedly targeted 147 pounds. If he remains there, Muratalla would have to skip light welterweight entirely to make the fight. Davis also appears focused on bigger names, making a deal uncertain.

Rankings present another question. The WBO previously placed Keyshawn near the top of its welterweight rankings before he fought in the division. It is unclear whether the sanctioning body would take the same approach with the reigning IBF lightweight champion.

If Muratalla is not placed near the top of the rankings, Robert Garcia’s next move is easy to identify. Wins over contenders such as Martin or other highly ranked light welterweights would strengthen Muratalla’s standing while increasing his visibility in the division. Fighting regularly would also help his case by giving the sanctioning bodies more opportunities to move him toward a title shot.

Garcia’s comments show his team has little interest in easing Muratalla into the division. Instead, they appear focused on securing recognizable opponents who can move him toward another world title.

Sports.title: How Much Has A Year Of Inactivity Hurt Artur Beterbiev?
Sports.content:
Age is what separates this break from those earlier in Beterbiev’s career. He will celebrate his 42nd birthday in January 2027. Fighters who rely on precise footwork sometimes survive long breaks with little decline. Beterbiev’s style is different. He applies nonstop pressure, cuts off the ring, throws every punch with full power, and forces opponents to fight every second. That approach demands tremendous conditioning.

There were already signs in the rematch that Father Time was beginning to chip away at those physical advantages. Beterbiev appeared to lose steam around the middle rounds, allowing Bivol to dictate longer stretches of the fight than he had in their first meeting. His power remained dangerous, but the relentless pressure that had broken so many opponents became harder to maintain.

Beterbiev’s injury history makes the layoff even more concerning. Injuries have interrupted several training camps throughout his career, including the knee problem that postponed the first Bivol fight. At 41, simply getting through a full camp without setbacks becomes part of the challenge. Inactivity can help fighters recover, but extended breaks also make it more difficult to regain the rhythm that only active competition provides.

The difficult part is that meaningful options still exist. A third fight with Bivol remains unfinished business, while a clash with David Benavidez would immediately become one of boxing’s biggest attractions. Both fights still carry enormous appeal, but neither becomes easier to make as the calendar keeps moving forward.

Beterbiev has already secured his place among the greatest light heavyweights of his generation. The remaining question is whether the extended time away has taken away just enough of the aggressive style that made him so dominant. If the trilogy with Bivol finally happens, fans won’t just be judging who wins. They’ll also discover whether nearly two years of inactivity has finally caught up with one of boxing’s greatest pressure fighters.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Claims Devin Haney Is Passing On Bigger Payday
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson believes Devin Haney is walking away from a bigger payday by refusing to pursue a fight at 144 pounds. Responding to criticism on X, Stevenson argued Haney would make substantially more money facing him than from the WBO title fight that recently fell apart.

“Ok then no fight and u fans miss out I make a shit ton of money regardless it’s not like I’m in need of anybody.. They bid $6m’s on his fight when he can make way more than that with me don’t be stupid,” Shakur said on X.

Stevenson did not explain how much a Haney fight would generate or where the additional money would come from. His argument rests on the commercial appeal of the matchup rather than the financial advantages Haney holds as the WBO welterweight champion.

Sports.title: Aaron Pryor Dethrones Antonio Cervantes To Claim World Title
Sports.content:
Moving up from lightweight, Pryor finally landed the title opportunity he had been chasing after struggling to secure the biggest fights at 135 pounds. Cervantes, a future Hall of Famer from Colombia, brought years of championship experience into his second reign as WBA champion. Many viewed the 34-year-old veteran as a fighter nearing the end of his best years, while the younger challenger was entering his prime.

Around 10,000 fans packed the arena hoping to witness history, and they nearly saw disaster strike in the opening round. Cervantes caught Pryor charging in with a perfectly timed counter that dropped the challenger to the canvas. Pryor jumped to his feet and immediately resumed pressing the action, giving the champion no chance to slow the fight.

The pace only grew faster over the next two rounds. Pryor’s nonstop pressure forced Cervantes to fight far more often than he wanted. In the third, repeated right hands opened a cut around the champion’s eye as Pryor steadily broke down the veteran’s defense.

The ending came quickly in the fourth. Pryor trapped Cervantes near the ropes and blasted him with a crushing overhand right that sent the champion to the canvas. Cervantes failed to beat referee Larry Rozadilla’s count, bringing the fight to an end at 1:47 of the round.

Pryor earned $50,000 for the victory, while Cervantes received roughly $250,000 for the title defense. More important than the payday, Pryor became Cincinnati’s first world champion in decades and immediately found himself in demand for bigger fights.

Pryor defended the title against challengers including Gaetan Hart, Lennox Blackmoore and Dujuan Johnson before producing his unforgettable two-fight series with Alexis Arguello. Those victories secured his place among the greatest 140-pound champions in boxing history, and they all began with his knockout of Antonio Cervantes.

Ghana News.title: Fulham sign Garcia and Palacios from Real Madrid
Ghana News.content:
Gonzalo Garcia (left) made nine La Liga starts in 2025-26, while Cesar Palacios (right) has made five senior appearances for Real Madrid

Fulham have signed Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios from Real Madrid on five-year deals.

Garcia, 22, made 39 appearances for the Spanish giants last term, scoring eight goals in all competitions.

The forward, who won his first cap for Spain in June, will reunite with new Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa, for a reported fee of around £34m, with the pair having worked together at the Bernabeu.

"I'm very grateful, very happy to be here," Garcia said.

"I have to thank the board and Arbeloa for the trust they've put in me, and I'm very, very excited to start."

The highly rated striker, joint-top scorer at the Club World Cup last summer, will be joined at Craven Cottage by former Real team-mate Palacios.

The 21-year-old attacking midfielder also arrives on a contract that runs until the summer of 2031, although the club has the option to extend the agreements for both players by a further 12 months.

Palacios made five appearances for Real's senior side - all from the substitutes' bench - and has played for Spain at under-20 level.

Ghana News.title: Chief of Staff pledges government’s closer collaboration with KNUST
Ghana News.content:
The Chief of Staff, Julius Debrah, has reaffirmed the government's commitment to strengthening collaboration with the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) to advance research, innovation and entrepreneurship.

Representing President John Dramani Mahama at the investiture of Professor Christian Agyare as the 13th Vice-Chancellor of KNUST, Mr Debrah described the ceremony as more than a change in leadership, saying it reaffirmed the country's commitment to education as a key driver of national development.

He said the government would work closely with the university to ensure research and innovation translate into practical solutions that create jobs, address societal challenges and improve the livelihoods of Ghanaians.

"Government looks forward to working closely with KNUST to strengthen research, innovation, entrepreneurship and industry, ensuring that knowledge moves beyond the classroom to create jobs, solve real-world challenges and improve the lives of Ghanaians," he stated.

Mr Debrah also paid tribute to the Chancellor of KNUST, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, for his leadership and acknowledged the contributions of the immediate past Vice-Chancellor, Professor Rita Akosua Dickson.

He congratulated Professor Agyare on his appointment and expressed confidence in his ability to lead the university into a new phase of growth and excellence.

The Chief of Staff further stressed the need for Ghana's universities to produce graduates who combine academic excellence with integrity, while developing innovations capable of supporting the country's economic transformation.

Professor Christian Agyare officially assumes office as the 13th Vice-Chancellor of KNUST, one of Ghana's leading public universities, succeeding Professor Rita Akosua Dickson.

Ghana News.title: “These are not normal times; let’s all sacrifice” – Energy Ministry appeals to GPRTU over fare hikes
Ghana News.content:
Public Relations Officer of the Ministry of Energy and Green Transition, Richmond Rockson

The Ministry of Energy and Green Transition has appealed to commercial transport operators to exercise patience and reconsider plans to increase transport fares following government's intervention to reduce diesel prices by GH¢2 per litre.

Speaking in an interview on Joy FM's Top Story on Monday, August 3, the Spokesperson for the Ministry, Richmond Rockson, acknowledged the concerns of the Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) and consumers over the rising cost of fuel but insisted that the current global energy crisis requires collective sacrifice.

"These are not normal times, and I share the concerns of the drivers. I share the concerns of consumers because in the last few months, we've seen the steep rise of prices as a result of geopolitics," he said.

Mr Rockson said government’s decision to reduce the price of diesel was aimed at cushioning both consumers and commercial drivers who have been hit by rising fuel costs.

"When you have to spend extra money to buy fuel, obviously you and I will complain. But these are not normal times," he added.

His comments follow concerns from the GPRTU that the GH¢2 per litre diesel reduction will not significantly change their operating costs and may only reduce the level of a planned fare adjustment.

The transport union had earlier proposed a 30% increase in fares, citing increases in fuel prices and other operational expenses.

Mr Rockson, however, argued that although the intervention may not completely resolve the challenges facing the transport sector, it would provide meaningful relief.

"The government has intervened. It may not be enough, as some have mentioned, but definitely it is going to go a long way to cushion consumers," he said.

He urged stakeholders to monitor developments in the international petroleum market, noting that global geopolitical events continue to have a direct impact on fuel prices in Ghana.

"Let us observe, and let us see what the international market says. We are hopeful that we will see positive signs... so let us observe, and let us all sacrifice," he said.

According to him, Ghana had previously experienced reductions in fuel prices when global conditions improved and expressed optimism that similar trends could return.

"Indeed, in the last few weeks, we had seen prices come down in the international market as a result of the ceasefire. Unfortunately, it started again and then they pushed up. Just as we had seen prices go down at a point below GH¢10, we are hopeful that we'll get to those levels when normal times resume," he added.

Mr Rockson's comments come as transport operators continue to push for adjustments in fares, citing the impact of rising fuel prices on their businesses.

Ghana News.title: The forgotten heroes behind Ghana’s hospitality success (Part 2)
Ghana News.content:
The focus of this feature is on “The Hidden Cost of Ignoring Hospitality Excellence in Ghana”.

Ghana has earned a reputation as one of Africa’s most welcoming destinations. The country’s democratic stability and peace, warmth, friendliness and cultural hospitality have become powerful assets for tourism growth, investment attraction and national development.

However, beneath this enviable reputation lies an uncomfortable reality.

Across the tourism and hospitality ecosystem, including hotels, restaurants, attractions, transport providers, travel companies, tour operators and other allied partners in the value chain, there remains a tendency to underestimate the true cost of poor service culture, weak employee engagement, inadequate accountability and insufficient recognition of the people who deliver the guest or customer experience every day.

Poor service does not always appear on a balance sheet as a clearly identifiable expense. It is often hidden in the consequences. The result is a progressive decline in guest satisfaction, lower productivity and morale, reduced business profitability, higher employee turnover, fewer referrals and recommendations, a damaged brand reputation, and the loss of customers and repeat business: a silent crisis capable of weakening Ghana’s competitiveness as a destination of choice.

Ghana’s hospitality sector can boast beautiful buildings, modern facilities, luxurious rooms, attractive restaurants, sophisticated technology and impressive ambience. These can create expectations. However, it is people who ultimately deliver the experience. Guests may admire the architecture, enjoy the food, appreciate the facilities and remember the ambience, but what often stays with them longest is how they were treated by people.

His Excellency John Dramani Mahama, President of the Republic of Ghana, during the Presidential Media Encounter on 10 September 2025, expressed concern about poor service delivery within Ghana’s tourism and hospitality sector, identifying it as one of the key factors undermining the country’s ability to attract and retain more international visitors.

His observation raises a critical question beyond customer service delivery and provokes deeper reflection across the industry. Could persistent challenges such as indifferent guest reception, delayed service delivery, weak ownership and accountability, and inadequate recognition of high-performing employees be symptomatic of a deeper systemic issue: the lack of sufficient appreciation, celebration and institutionalisation of service excellence at the organisational, industry and national levels?

If service excellence is fundamental to Ghana’s competitiveness as a tourism and hospitality destination, then recognising the people who consistently deliver it should not be treated as an organisational norm. It should be regarded as a strategic investment in the culture, reputation, productivity and future competitiveness of Ghana’s hospitality industry.

To this end, the question is not merely, “How much does it cost Ghana when hospitality excellence is repeatedly ignored?” Perhaps the more critical question is: “What is the true cost to Ghana when it fails to recognise, appreciate and celebrate the forgotten heroes: the dedicated service champions whose daily commitment, professionalism and passion form the foundation of Ghana’s hospitality brand and visitor experience?”

Ghana News.title: GH¢2 diesel subsidy not enough to prevent transport fare increases – GPRTU
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) says government's GH¢2 per litre diesel subsidy will provide limited relief for commercial transport operators, insisting that the intervention does not sufficiently address the sharp rise in fuel prices.

Deputy Public Relations Officer of the GPRTU, Samuel Amoah, said while the union appreciates government's decision to reduce diesel prices, the current cost of fuel remains significantly higher than when discussions on transport fare adjustments began.

Speaking on JoyNews, Mr Amoah recalled that transport operators were asked by the Transport Ministry to suspend plans for a 30% fare increase after government indicated that measures would be introduced to reduce fuel prices.

"We were asked to hold on because they promised that government was going to work on the fuel price and that the next price would come down and all that. By then the diesel was around GH¢17, then petrol was around GH¢15. We were expecting a reduction," he stated.

However, he said the current market situation has changed, with diesel prices approaching GH¢20 per litre, meaning the GH¢2 intervention only brings prices back closer to previous levels rather than delivering a substantial reduction.

"But now during this price window, diesel is approaching GH¢20 a litre. So because government is taking GH¢2 from the diesel, it means it is coming back to where it was, and that will not have any significant effect on us," Mr Amoah argued.

According to him, the subsidy may only reduce the scale of any future transport fare adjustment rather than eliminate the need for an increase.

"What will happen is if we are to increase the fares, maybe the percentage that we were proposing is something that we may consider bringing it down," he said.

The GPRTU had earlier proposed a 30% increase in transport fares, citing rising fuel costs and operational expenses.

Mr Amoah maintained that commercial transport operators continue to face significant cost pressures and will assess the impact of government's intervention before deciding on the next steps regarding fares.

Ghana News.title: DVLA to replace faded 2026 number plates free of charge – CEO
Ghana News.content:
Chief Executive Officer of the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA), Julius Neequaye Kotey

The Chief Executive Officer of the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA), Julius Neequaye Kotey, has acknowledged widespread complaints about fading 2026 vehicle number plates and announced that affected vehicle owners will receive free replacements.

Speaking on Asempa FM’s Ekosii Sen on Monday, August 3, Mr Kotey admitted that many of the number plates issued this year had experienced fading due to production challenges.

“I will admit that most of the numbers are fading,” he said.

Explaining the cause of the problem, the DVLA boss revealed that the authority faced a major setback in January 2026 after nearly all the companies contracted to emboss number plates suspended their services.

According to him, about 160 companies were engaged by the DVLA nationwide to produce number plates, but 159 of them boycotted the exercise following a disagreement over an existing contract.

“In January 2026, we had issues with the number plate embossers. We had about 160 companies cutting number plates for the whole of Ghana. About 159 of them met and decided they would no longer produce number plates for us because they wanted me to cancel a contract that had been signed before I assumed office, and I said that would be wrong,” he explained.

“They did that so that I would be sacked,” he claimed.

He said the situation left only one company to produce number plates for the entire country, resulting in production pressure that affected the quality of the plates.

“It was only one company producing for the whole of Ghana, so I am sure the three-layer coating was not properly applied because of the pressure on them,” he said.

Mr Kotey assured motorists that the DVLA has put measures in place to address the issue and urged all owners of vehicles with faded number plates to visit any DVLA office for a replacement.

“If your number plate is fading, take it to any DVLA office and we will replace it for you at no cost,” he said.

He further disclosed that the authority is introducing a new generation of number plates that will eliminate the fading problem.

“Thankfully, all that is coming to an end. With the new number plates, it is not paint but an electronic system, so they will not fade,” he added.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
