Camp Taji is a large Iraqi military base located around 27 kilometers (17 miles) north of Baghdad. The camp formerly housed US-led international coalition soldiers until it was fully handed over to Iraqi authorities in 2020.

The specific storage contained heavy munitions belonging to the Iraqi army.

The explosion occurred during a severe regional heatwave. Temperatures in Baghdad hit 49 degrees Celsius (120 degrees Fahrenheit), while the neighboring areas reached 50 degrees Celsius.

Civil Defense units were dispatched quickly to contain the fire and keep it from spreading to other depots.

No immediate injuries or deaths have been reported.

Incidents of this type are common in Iraq because of the old infrastructure, poor safety regulations, and scorching summer temperatures.

World.title: Iraq earns $18.6 billion from oil exports in H1 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) revealed last week that the country’s oil revenues hit $18.67 billion during the first half of 2026 as exports reached approximately 268 million barrels of crude oil.

SOMO data indicated Iraq’s oil exports in the first half of 2025 were 606.58 million barrels, more than double the quantity exported in the same period in 2026.

The reported revenues for just the first four months of 2025 reached nearly $27.514 billion, exceeding the total oil revenues generated during the entire first half of 2026.

The figures show a considerable decline in both crude oil export volumes and income in the first half of 2026 compared to the same time last year.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil reported last Tuesday that the country’s crude oil exports during May and June 2026 totaled approximately 32.11 million barrels, averaging over 16 million barrels per month.

The country’s oil exports reached 9.88 million barrels in April and around 18.6 million barrels in March.

Iraqi oil export earnings in May and June 2026 reached approximately $2.33 billion, averaging $1.16 billion per month, compared to $1.87 billion in April, $1.95 billion in March, and approximately $6.81 billion in February.

The decline in exported volumes and produced profits coincides with regional tensions that negatively impacted the region’s energy supply chains and maritime traffic in recent months.

World.title: Iraq offers discounts on Basrah crude during August
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) has offered considerable discounts on Basrah crude during August to attract customers to load shipments from within the Strait of Hormuz, according to a document reviewed by Reuters.

SOMO asked potential term purchasers to designate contractual volumes of Basrah Medium or Basrah Heavy crude for complimentary onboard delivery from the Basrah Oil Terminal or other port-related infrastructure.

SOMO provided discounts ranging between $25 and $27 per barrel on Basrah Medium, according to the loading period. It provided discounts of $27.80 to $29.80 a barrel for Basrah Heavy.

According to shipping statistics released on Monday, maritime activity in the strategic waterway of the Strait of Hormuz has slowed over the weekend due to reports of assaults on vessels.

Maritime traffic in the strait decreased due to ongoing military operations in the region and heightened shipping security risks.

The significant price reduction aims to compensate for rising maritime insurance costs and freight expenses by transferring transit risk to purchasers.

World.title: US forces gradually withdraw from northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US forces have begun a phased withdrawal from Iraqi Kurdistan as part of a plan to redeploy and end their military presence in the country.

Reports indicate that US military convoys have left the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil, in the past few days, heading towards neighboring countries.

The withdrawal is being carried out in successive phases according to a set timetable, while the transfer of equipment and troops from US bases in the region continues.

The US Department of War has not yet issued an official statement regarding the details of these recent movements.

Reports also mentioned that the United States has begun withdrawing its remaining forces from Iraq ahead of the September 30 deadline, with Patriot air defense systems already removed from Erbil.

The pullout comes as regional security concerns rise, with Iranian-backed armed groups continuing to threaten the Kurdistan Region. These assaults have generated fears that reducing the United States’ military presence may make the region more vulnerable to security challenges.

The withdrawal is part of understandings reached between Baghdad and Washington over the past two years to end the mission of the US-led international coalition and transition to a new phase based on bilateral security and military cooperation.

Despite reducing its military presence, the United States has repeatedly affirmed its commitment to continued cooperation with Iraqi forces in training, intelligence sharing, and countering ISIS within a bilateral framework that does not require a large-scale military presence.

The withdrawal begins at a time when tensions in the region have risen in the past few weeks, following military operations by the US and Iran, as well as frequent drone and missile attacks on Iraqi Kurdistan.

World.title: Iraq, Iran discuss developments in the Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Aragchi, discussed on Sunday the latest developments in the Strait of Hormuz and prospects for regional de-escalation.

In a phone conversation, the two sides evaluated the most recent developments in the Strait of Hormuz during the last two days, as well as the implications for maritime security and regional stability, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

Hussein emphasized Iraq’s support of dialogue and diplomacy as effective approaches to address disagreements and settle unresolved concerns, thereby helping to improve security and stability in the region.

The discussion also addressed the recent military assaults targeting Iraq and the significance of avoiding any actions that may escalate tensions in the region.

Aragchi reviewed the most recent developments and briefed Hussein on ongoing efforts to reach an agreement that would help reopen the Strait of Hormuz and ensure the smooth flow of maritime navigation.

Iraq is closely monitoring ongoing developments and expects to reach agreements that will facilitate the reopening of the Strait as soon as possible. This effort aims to ensure the security and stability of both the region and the global economy, according to Hussein.

Given the rapidly changing situation, Hussein emphasized the necessity of ongoing coordination between the two parties, as well as his support for steps taken to enhance dialogue.

World.title: Meta CEO Zuckerberg must apologise: Parliamentary Panel
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Rejecting Meta's apology for taking down a PM Narendra Modi's video, a parliamentary committee Monday sought a personal apology from its founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg and warned of seeking removal of its safe harbour protection if he failed to comply, its chairperson Nishikant Dubey said.

Dubey said removal of the PM's video was either a serious failure of the system or there "is a deliberate attempt to tarnish the image of the PM" on part of Meta.

"If this is how they deal with the official post of the PM, what can the common people of India expect? This failure cannot be dismissed merely as a technical error. It is a serious matter and an apology must come from Zuckerberg's side. And if he does not apologise, safe harbour protection should be taken back from them," Dubey said.

Senior representatives of a host of social media platforms, including X, Google, YouTube, besides Meta, appeared before the Dubey-led committee on communications and IT, besides home secretary Govind Mohan and IT secretary S Krishnan.

Parliamentarians questioned digital platforms over their choice of algorithms and presence of unlawful content, including child sexual abuse material (CSAM), deep fake investment scams, and targeting of women, with Meta being particularly at the receiving end of their ire.





While some opposition MPs emphasised that social media must retain space of dissent and 'anti-govt' content should not be considered 'anti-national', the committee was unanimous in asking for stricter and timely measures against the content that are in violation of their own stated policies, especially involving CSAM, cyber frauds, and harassment of women.

"We are unanimous and non-partisan on all issues," Dubey said, adding that even MHA's communications is ignored by these platforms.

The BJP MP referred to the high online viewership grabbed by CJP during its recent protest, saying it, at 27 million, was more than the combined viewership of parties like BJP, Congress, AAP and SP. He blamed the platforms' choice of algorithm favouring new entrants for this.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Some MPs demanded that Meta must fix accountability for removing Modi's video, which was restored later by the social media behemoth, which owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.

Social media platforms can amplify or suppress any content's reach, remove it or attach community notes that carry abuses, and then the question is whether they are mere intermediaries as they claim or publishers, Dubey said.

"It is disturbing that in 2025 alone approximately 28.15 lakh cybercrime complaints were reported nationally, with estimated losses of nearly Rs 22,495 crore," he added.

World.title: SC: How can transgender ID cards be rendered invalid?
World.content:
NEW DELHI: SC Monday sought govt's response on pleas alleging Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, attempts to erase benefits accruing to transgenders under the old law and impinge on their right to receive hormone treatment for bringing their bodies in sync with self-identified genders.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked if the amendments are to be implemented prospectively, how could the transgender identity cards, issued under the earlier provisions of the law, be rendered invalid?

Senior advocates complained those who were midway through their hormone treatment are being denied the same as doctors are not ready to provide such treatment fearing prosecution under the new law. "The national portal for transgenders has been discontinued denying them many benefits," they alleged.

World.title: ARAI's study on E20 fuel impact may be made public
World.content:
In June 2021, petroleum ministry had directed ARAI and IOCL, in association with SIAM, to carry out the study.

NEW DELHI: Amid growing demand to make the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) study report on E20 fuel's impact on E10-compatible vehicles public, govt agencies are looking at the possibility to release it to help remove misconceptions among vehicle users .TOI has learnt that since specific two-wheelers and cars were used for the study, details of models may not be disclosed considering commercial interest of vehicle manufacturers. "Govt has referred to the study and its findings to respond to questions in Parliament. Hence, there is a view that it should be made public so that people see that E20 fuel doesn't impact engines," said an official.In June 2021, petroleum ministry had directed ARAI and IOCL, in association with SIAM, to carry out the study. The report was submitted in June 2024. The study had concluded that in case of E10-compliant two-wheelers, fuel consumption increased in the range of 1-6% and mass emission met the regulatory requirement. In the case of BS-IV cars, fuel consumption increased by 2-4%, and 2-3% in case of BS-VI-compliant cars.

World.title: After success of students protest, Kisan Morcha plans to hit streets
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Emboldened by the success of student protests at Jantar Mantar, Samyukt Kisan Morcha - the umbrella organisation of farmer groups involved in the anti-farm laws agitation five years ago - announced Monday that it would restart protests at 100 locations across India, including Delhi, from Nov 26.

The protesters will demand a law guaranteeing MSP; repeal of all FTAs, including the India-US FTA currently under negotiation; a comprehensive loan waiver to address rural indebtedness; scrapping of four labour codes; minimum wage of Rs 31,000 for workers and restoration of the old rural job guarantee scheme; withdrawal of Electricity Privatisation Bill 2025, Seed Bill 2025 and NFSA Amendment Bill; and no forceful land acquisition.

"The protests will not be called off till all seven demands are accepted," said P Krishnaprasad of AIKS.

World.title: 'Flavouring neutral alcohol isn't right in spirit'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has said alcoholic beverage manufacturers cannot add "rum flavour" to rum or "whisky flavour" to whisky and market them as standard products, saying the practice misrepresents the true nature of the beverage and misleads consumers.

The regulator said the issue is not the use of permitted flavouring substances, but addition of the flavour of the standardised alcoholic beverage itself, which serves no legitimate purpose. It said the characteristic taste and aroma of products such as rum and whisky should develop naturally through the base ingredients, fermentation, distillation and maturation. However, inspections found that some manufacturers were producing beverages largely from neutral alcohol, which has no characteristic flavour, and then adding identical flavouring substances to recreate the taste and aroma of rum or whisky.

Such products, FSSAI said, should be labelled as "rum-flavoured spirit" or "whisky-flavoured spirit", with the front of the pack clearly disclosing their true nature. Laboratory testing of rum and whisky samples from multiple manufacturers found the addition of artificial or nature-identical flavours that masked the products' natural characteristics, rendering them sub-standard under existing regulations, FSSAI said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





Based on findings, it prohibited the sale of products manufactured by units of Mohan Rocky Springwater, United Spirits, INBREW Beverages and Associated Alcohol & Breweries. It also inspected Mandexi Distilleries & Breweries in Goa and issued notices to six producers in Maharashtra.

FSSAI also objected to the "7 years old blended" claim on an Old Monk XXX Rum variant, saying the product predominantly contained neutral, unmatured spirit, while matured rum spirit accounted for less than 5% of the blend.

It said the issue is not representative of the entire industry, noting that many manufacturers continue to produce beverages in compliance with the prescribed standards.

World.title: FSSAI suspends water firm's licence, bans sale of dietary supplement
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (

) has suspended the licence of a packaged drinking water manufacturer in Tripura and prohibited the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of a dietary food supplement made by a Punjab-based company after inspections found serious food safety and regulatory violations.

The licence of M/S Matri Drinking Water, Gomati, Tripura, was suspended with immediate effect following a complaint about foreign material in packaged drinking water. Inspectors found finished products stored outside the facility and on the floor alongside non-food materials, unhygienic processing and filling areas, rusted RO water storage tanks and chemical dosing containers, inadequate pest control and sanitation, and the absence of mandatory testing, maintenance and training records.

A qualified technical supervisor was also not available during the inspection.

In a separate action, FSSAI prohibited the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of Venolex Forte, marketed by M/S Noble Healthcare, Mohali, saying the dietary food supplement contained ingredients not permitted under the Food Safety and Standards (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use, Food for Special Medical Purpose, Functional Food and Novel Food) Regulations, 2022.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





The regulator said the product contained pharmacologically active ingredients, including calcium dobesilate, diosmin and Euphorbia prostrata, which are not permitted in food supplements. It also found that the product contained 90 mg of vitamin C, which appeared to exceed the Recommended Dietary Allowance prescribed under the ICMR-NIN Guidelines, 2020.

FSSAI also said the product's labelling was misleading, creating the impression of specific regulatory approval, and that it was manufactured and marketed beyond the scope of the firm's FSSAI licence. The prohibition order has been issued under Section 36(3)(b) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

World.title: Of 39 medals won by India at CWG, military personnel bag 18 — nearly 50%
World.content:
Indian Army athletes secured 16 medals at the recent CWG. These included 8 gold, 7 silver, and 1 bronze medal. 2 Indian Navy personnel also contributed silver medals in weightlifting.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In the recently-concluded Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow, Indian military personnel have a lionâs share in winning medals for the country. The Indian Army won 16 medals of India's total medal haul of 39. Two Indian Navy personnel also won medals. If the medals won by Army and Navy personnel are combined, the services personnel bagged 18 medals out of the total 39, which is equivalent to 46% contribution of the services in winning medals.âA contingent of 20 Indian Army athletes won 16 medals for the Nationâ, the Army said, adding out of 16 medals, eight are gold, seven silver and one bronze.Praising its personnel, the Indian Army, in a post X on Monday, said, âHar Kaam, Desh Ke Naam. General Dhiraj Seth, COAS and All Ranks of Indian Army extend heartiest congratulations to the Indian Army athletes for their outstanding performance at the Commonwealth Games Glasgow 2026. âGiving details of the disciplines were the Armymen won laurels, the ADG PI said, âIndian Army athletes exceptional performance is testimony of their zeal and commitment across judo, boxing, athletics, para athletics and weightlifting. Their achievements reaffirm the Indian Army's steadfast commitment to nurturing world-class athletes and advancing the Nation's sporting aspirations through Mission Olympics 2036.The Army gave details of its Army personnel winning medals: Gold medals won by Havildar Harsh in judo (60 kg), Naib Subedar Preeti in boxing (54 kg); Naib Subedar Jaismine in boxing (57 kg); Subedar Soman Rana in para shot put; Havildar Sakshi in boxing (51 kg); Havildar Arundhati in boxing (70 kg); Havildar Sachin in boxing (60 kg) and Havildar Ankush in boxing (80 kg).Silver medals have been won by Naib Subedar Sarvesh in high jump; Nb Sub Gulveer in 10,000 m; Hav Ajaya Babu in weightlifting; Lt Col (Honorary) Neeraj Chopra in javelin throw; Hav Jadumani in boxing; Lance Naik Shubham Juyal in para shot put and Sub Narender in boxing (+90 kg). Bronze medal has been won by Nb Sub Gulveer in the 5,000-m track.Two Navy personnel â Chief Petty Officer Communication (Telegraphist) Lovepreet Singh and Chief Petty Officer (PT) Chanambam Rishikanta Singh â won silver medals in weightlifting category. In a post on X, the Navy said, âIndian Navy's Lovepreet Singh, CPO COM (TEL), powered to a SILVER medal in the +110 kg Weightlifting category at CWG2026! Total Lift of 388 kg (176 kg Snatch + 212 kg Clean & Jerk). Rewriting the history books with a 176 kg Snatch, setting a new Commonwealth Games Record! Lovepreet ! You've made the nation proud. â

World.title: Military-civil integration key to robust def ecosystem to tackle challenges: Rajnath
World.content:
Defence minister Rajnath Singh addresses the AFHQ Civilian Services Day celebrations at DRDO Bhawan in New Delhi on Monday

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Monday underlined the need to deepen integration between the military and civil components of the defence ministry to foster greater synergy within the defence ecosystem to tackle evolving security and technological challenges, while ensuring institutional memory, stability and the effective application of rules and regulations.Addressing the 85th Armed Forces Headquarters (AFHQ) Civilian Services Day celebrations in Delhi on Aug 3, he emphasised that both uniformed and civil services share the same commitment of âNation Firstâ, and when the objective is singular, every element of the system transforms into national strength.Rajnath underlined that military and administrative integration cannot proceed along separate paths, adding that, as joint and integrated structures develop, there will be a need for continuity and expertise across all areas â policy, administration, human resource management, financial processes, logistics, and institutional knowledge. He highlighted the importance of further enhancing structured cross-exposure between civilian and military officers, suggesting joint training programmes and developmental assignments for both sides to learn from each otherâs experiences.âMilitary officers bring operational experience, a command perspective, and an understanding of warfare, while civilian officers contribute through administrative continuity, policy experience, an understanding of government processes, and institutional memory.When these strengths combine, decision-making becomes more informed, balanced, and effective,â Rajnath said.Explaining with the example of âcyber warfareâ, the minister stated that if officers of the AFHQ civilian services develop defence-specific common cyber tools leveraging their expertise, it could prove beneficial to the defence forces. He said a forum could be developed for the study of Indian military history, examining it from a civilian perspective, thereby fostering fresh ideas and new perspectives. He expressed confidence that, by leveraging expertise in such areas, AFHQ civilian services will be able to make more meaningful contributions to the defence sector.Rajnath called upon the AFHQ civilian services to evolve into the âstrategic brainâ of Indiaâs defence management architecture by developing a comprehensive understanding of the defence sector, functioning effectively in a joint environment, and continuously enhancing its expertise to face the emerging challenges.While he acknowledged the AFHQ civilian services for moving ahead in sync with changing times, he asserted that, at a time when modern warfare is driven by technological dynamism, the cadre must move beyond its specific mandate of proper implementation of service rules, regulations & orders.âA military derives its strength not merely from weapons and ammunition, but also from the thousands of unseen hands that always stand in their support. AFHQ Civilian Services is one of these unseen yet decisive forces. It must focus on strengthening the security architecture through research, geo-strategic thinking & innovative ideas. Its active participation in core defence matters is essential as, being a permanent cadre of the Ministry of Defence, it possesses deep domain knowledge,â Rajnath said.

World.title: ‘Donors got mixer grinders, cash’: blood banks in Bengal under scanner over ‘illegal’ sale to other States
World.content:
At least six blood banks in West Bengal are under investigation for allegedly selling blood to individuals and private blood banks outside the State in what Health Department officials have described as an inter-State, multi-crore racket.

The sale of blood is prohibited under the National Blood Policy, which was introduced in 2002. Officials said raids have been conducted at blood banks in Kolkata, Howrah, East Burdwan, West Burdwan, Nadia, and North Dinajpur districts over the past two weeks and large quantities of plasma were found to have been sold to entities in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat, among other States.

Officials said around 11 blood banks have been barred from organising donation drives until the investigation is over. However, they are still permitted to collect blood from donors at their centres. The restrictions came into effect on August 1. Popular medical facilities and pathology labs like Ashok Laboratory, Life Care, Kothari Medical, Health Point Hospital, and several others are on the list.

The racket, worth crores, kept the health department in the dark by selling blood illegally, health department officials said.

Last week, Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee told reporters that officials found that people who donated blood at a camp in South 24 Parganas were offered gifts. “You can give food, flowers, a badge or a certificate to a donor, but you cannot give gifts. We recorded instances of donors getting fans, mixer grinders, clocks and money,” said Dr. Mukherjee.

World.title: Several WhatsApp users say their accounts 'put under review'
World.content:
Instant messaging app WhatsApp on Monday (August 3, 2026) put multiple accounts, including those in India, "under review" for 24 hours and blocked all the app features, prompting several affected users to flag the issue through social media.

When contacted, a WhatsApp spokesperson said, "We are always working to stay ahead of those trying to abuse our service and ban accounts to help keep other users safe. Sometimes we get this wrong and if we do, we try to fix it as quickly as possible to get people back to chatting."

The disruption was highlighted around 8 p.m. IST when users started facing the issue without any prior warning from the Meta group's messaging app.

The WhatsApp app on the screen displayed the message, "Account in review. Date requested: 3 Aug 2026. Your account activity and device info is being checked to make sure it follows our terms of service. We will notify you of the result typically within 24 hours."

Below these remarks, the app shows an option to learn about account issues, which include, "How to use WhatsApp responsibly. See guidance" and an option, "About stolen phone and accounts".

Some of the users on social media posted different messages.

"My WhatsApp account has been disabled without any explanation. I have already submitted an appeal, but the review page only displays a generic message stating that it will "typically be reviewed within 24 hours. Help me urgently," a user said on social media.

An account on X by the name of Saloni posted, "My WhatsApp account was suddenly disabled without any warning. I only use the official app, and my work depends on WhatsApp. Please help. This was so unnecessary."

World.title: Delhi police move against social media handles over misleading Jantar Mantar protest videos
World.content:
The Delhi police have initiated legal action against social media handles accused of circulating misleading videos falsely suggesting that protests are continuing at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The police have issued takedown notices to Meta and X as authorities move to curb the spread of misinformation.

The action follows the circulation of dozens of videos across social media platforms claiming to show “live” protests at Jantar Mantar until August 3, despite the 36-day Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) agitation having ended over a week earlier. Several of the clips garnered millions of views, prompting various departments to inquire with the police whether fresh demonstrations had resumed.

Speaking to The Hindu, a senior New Delhi police official said the process of removing the content was underway. “There are a large number of misleading videos circulating across social media platforms. We have verified that no such protests have happened and issued takedown notices to Meta and X for the removal of the misleading content. We have also started identifying the handles and warning them of legal action if the behaviour continues,” the official said.

The official said no First Information Report had been registered so far.

The government’s fact-check unit has also stepped in to counter the viral claims. The Press Information Bureau (PIB) Fact Check unit said videos being circulated under titles such as “Jantar Mantar Season 2” and “Jantar Mantar protest session 2.0” falsely claimed that protests had resumed in New Delhi.

सोशल मीडिया पर वीडियो साझा कर दावा किया जा रहा है कि जंतर-मंतर पर पुनः धरना-प्रदर्शन शुरू हो गया है।#PIBFactCheck



❌ यह दावा फर्जी है।



✅ वायरल वीडियो पुराना है, जिसे भ्रामक संदर्भ के साथ साझा कर लोगों को गुमराह करने की कोशिश की जा रही है।



⚠️ ऐसे भ्रामक कंटेंट से सावधान… pic.twitter.com/au1LdAfYW3 — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) August 2, 2026

“The viral videos are old, and an attempt is being made to mislead people by sharing them with a misleading context,” the unit said, urging the public to remain cautious while sharing unverified content online.

Among the videos circulating widely was footage showing New Delhi DCP Sachin Sharma and Joint CP Deepak Purohit interacting with organisers during the CJP protest on July 19 and 20. In the footage, the officers are heard telling organisers that Jantar Mantar is not suited for a demonstration of that scale, citing inadequate volunteer arrangements, the possibility of “criminal elements” entering the gathering, and repeated warnings allegedly issued to organisers before the protest.

The footage resurfaced on Monday (August 3), giving viewers the impression that protests had resumed. The police action comes shortly after student representatives visited Jantar Mantar to verify similar claims circulating online. They found no evidence of any protests after July 28, and urged action against accounts spreading misleading content.

World.title: Cauvery water issue: DMK members walk out from both Houses in protest
World.content:
Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) MPs on Monday (August 3, 2026) staged a walk-out from both Houses of Parliament protesting against Tamil Nadu being denied its share of Cauvery water. They also held a protest outside the Parliament on the issue.

Parliament Monsoon Session: Follow LIVE updates on August 3, 2026

The protest is centred on the alleged violation of the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s directives, which dictates that Tamil Nadu should receive 9.9 TMC of water in June and 32 TMC in July, bringing the total to 42 TMC. However, the State has “not received a single drop” thus far in 2026. The Tamil Nadu government has also approached the Supreme Court on the issue.

“The original demand of 7,000 cusecs based on the already existing backlog has to be released to us. We wanted the House to debate and pass a resolution on this,” Rajya Sabha MP P. Wilson said.

DMK MPs carried placards in both Houses of Parliament. In the Rajya Sabha, Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan named Mr. Wilson, among others, for carrying the placard. When their plea for a debate was ignored, the DMK MPs staged a walk-out.

Mr. Wilson also blamed the Congress for ignoring the issue that he said affected nearly everyone in Tamil Nadu. “The Congress is not bothered about the problems of the Tamil Nadu. They are only talking about other issues, so we have brought to the attention of the Parliament that this issue has to be, you know, sorted out by the Union government,” the DMK MP said.

World.title: Baghel asks workers to beware of ‘traitors’ within Punjab Congress
World.content:
Amid its ongoing mass mobilisation programme at the booth level in the run-up to the 2027 Assembly poll, Congress’s general secretary in-charge for Punjab Bhupesh Baghel on Monday (August 3, 2026) cautioned party workers to stay alert against “traitors within the party who could cause serious damage”.

Addressing the gathering in Bathinda, he said the next elections will not be fought by the candidates alone, but by the entire party’s rank and file, underlining the need for strengthening the organisation at the grassroots level.

Warning against the “traitors within”, he quoted senior party leader Rahul Gandhi, who he said often “warned against the sleeper cells of other parties within the Congress”. The event was disrupted after a section of party workers boycotted it and raised slogans in support of Mr. Channi. Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, though, hailed the raising of slogans in favour of Mr. Channi, saying “he was one of the senior and most respected leaders of the party”.

‘Remove AAP government’

Mr. Baghel said it was important to defeat and get rid of the Aam Aadmi Party government, which had not only pushed the State into anarchy, but had looted and robbed the State as well. He added that nobody was feeling safe in Punjab as “gangsters were running the roost and people were getting killed in broad daylight”.

The conspicuous absence of Mr. Channi, who is believed to be upset with the party’s revamp, from the event along with leaders from his ‘camp’, has triggered questions over the party’s internal cohesion.

World.title: Opposition MPs protest over Ram Temple donation theft
World.content:
Opposition parties on Monday (August 3, 2026) continued to protest in the Parliament House complex against the alleged donation theft at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya and police crackdown on the anti-paper leak student demonstrations on July 20.

Like last week, the MPs kept donation boxes near the Parliament entrance, ‘Makar Dwar’, to symbolise the alleged theft of donations at the temple and lined up around them to raise slogans against the government. Some MPs put cash in the box enacting the donations made and the “theft” that took place later.

Members of the Samajwadi Party who were present said till now more than ₹47,000 has been collected and the money would be donated to the Ram Temple at Ayodhya and a receipt would be taken.

The MPs had staged a similar skit last week, which had led to objections from Hindu outfits and the BJP who alleged that it was an insult to ‘Sanatan Dharma’.

Parliament Monsoon Session: Follow LIVE updates on August 3, 2026

Shah’s absence

The Opposition MPs also protested against the “absence” of Union Home Minister Amit Shah from both the Houses of Parliament.

The protesting MPs lined up behind a big banner that read ‘Why Amit Shah is absent from Parliament?’.

Congress’ Priyanka Gandhi, SP’s Dimple Yadav and Dharmendra Yadav, Trinamool Congress’ Mahua Moitra, Jarkhand Mukti Morcha’s Mahua Maji, Revolutionary Socialist Party’s N.K. Premachandran, were among those who were seen at the protest.

They also raised slogans against Mr. Shah on the use of force against student protesters at the anti-paper leak agitation in the national capital last week.

“Modiji should apologise, for lathi-charging and firing pellet guns at the youth...but instead of coming to Parliament, he is intimidating and threatening the children. They do not come to the House, they do not answer questions, they do not speak on the theft of donations for Shri Ram Mandir, nor do they say anything on the suppression of students. Innocent children are not traitors, do not label them as such, the real traitors are the BJP people! who are crushing democracy,” Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said.

Questioning the absence of Mr. Shah from the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, Congress general secretary organisation K.C. Venugopal said: “Why is the Home Minister not coming to Parliament? In all previous sessions, he used to be very active. Then why is he not attending this session? The atrocities and attacks against students are still continuing. We, and the entire country, need an answer from the Home Minister.”

“Our protests outside Parliament, and on the floor of both Houses, will continue until the government is held accountable,” he added.

INDIA bloc MPs have stalled both Houses of Parliament over the twin issues with Bills being passed without a debate.

World.title: New talks 'last chance' for Iran to forge deal, avoid escalation of U.S. strikes: Trump
World.content:
Newly planned talks with Tehran are the “last chance” for Iran to forge a deal and avoid an escalation of US strikes on the country, President Donald Trump said on Monday (August 3, 2026).

Mr. Trump, speaking at the Oval Office, said he expects negotiations that will reopen the Strait of Hormuz and create a pathway for Iran to address the United States' concerns about its nuclear programme will begin in the next day or two.

“The first phase is the opening of the straits. The second phase will be the denuclearisation," the Republican President said. “And that will take a little while.”

While Trump has revelled in the US military decimating layers of Tehran's leadership and devastating its air force and navy, Iran is betting it can outlast Trump as he faces diminished stockpiles of munitions and the difficulty of executing a war that is unpopular with the American electorate ahead of November's midterm election.

Mr. Trump said he decided to hold off on ordering American forces to carry out new massive strikes against Iran at the urging of Gulf allies Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates.

He said that a plan was in place for U.S. forces to carry out “the biggest attack since World War II” on Sunday. But he decided to scrap the plan and give diplomacy more time to play out after hearing from key Gulf leaders — including Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman — as well as at the request of unnamed Iranian officials.

But Mr. Trump reiterated that he's running out of patience with Iran.

“This the last chance for them to sign a good document,” Mr. Trump told reporters.

Earlier Monday (August 3), Mr. Trump had criticised Iran on social media as being “unbelievably duplicitous.”

His ire was raised by Iran claiming that its meetings with Oman on Monday (August 3) were focused solely on establishing a temporary route for safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for the global oil trade.

“They ask for a meeting, some would say 'beg,' talks begin, with more scheduled in the immediate future, and they say, openly and proudly, that they're not having any discussions, that nothing is being talked about, and they're only dealing with Oman,” Mr. Trump grumbled.

Mr. Trump said whether “Iran wants to admit it or not, we are, in fact, talking” about preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons.

Mr. Trump has threatened to escalate attacks on Iran only to edge away from his threats several times since the start of U.S. and Israel strikes on February 28.

Asked by a reporter how Americans view him repeatedly making grim threats on Tehran before backing away, Trump responded that he's showing patience out of a consideration for Iranian life.

“I want to give them every last chance before decapitation,” Mr. Trump said. He added, “Hopefully, they'll come to their senses.”

Critics see Trump reaching for a reset button in this pattern

Mr. Trump may still come to the conclusion that a massive escalation in the conflict with Iran is necessary.

But critics say his hesitation also might reflect an unspoken understanding inside the administration that U.S. military might alone may not be enough to compel Iran to back down and bring an end to a now monthslong war that Mr. Trump had earlier downplayed as a weekslong excursion.

“I think what we're seeing here is a President who has an approach that's just rather erratic,” said Sen. Mark Kelly, an Arizona Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, on CBS News' “Face the Nation.”

“At this point, he's trying to get us back to February. And I think if he could — if he had a big reset button he could hit — he would certainly take that option.”

There have been several moments over the course of the conflict when Mr. Trump has demonstrated his proclivity for the bellicose only to back off at the last minute, while declaring his threats spurred progress: — In early April, the United States and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire in an announcement that came less than two hours before a deadline Mr. Trump had set for Tehran to capitulate or face attacks on bridges and power plants — strikes he said would mean “a whole civilization will die.”

After days of dire threats against Iran, Mr. Trump announced on May 18 he was holding off on a major planned military strike because “serious negotiations” were underway, crediting Gulf allies for persuading him to show restraint.

Then in June, Mr. Trump threatened to hit Iran “VERY HARD” and seize Iran's energy base on Kharg Island to "assume total control of their Oil and Gas Markets,” he wrote on social media, only to call off the strikes in a later post after claiming that peace negotiations had progressed with high-level Iranian leaders.

Left unsaid by Mr. Trump was that such an endeavour would require U.S. troops on the ground in Iran — a risky proposition politically for a President who campaigned on avoiding foreign entanglements and criticised past administrations for getting bogged down in endless wars.

Call with Saudi crown prince affected Trump's decision

With this latest episode, Mr. Trump suggested that the Saudi crown prince played a particularly important role in him turning away from escalating the fight.

The U.S. President spoke by phone with the de facto leader of the kingdom on Saturday (August 1) before announcing he was halting strikes that he later boasted would have been one of the biggest U.S. operations since World War II.

The Crown Prince conveyed that an escalation in fighting could have a severe impact on the global economy if Tehran responded to a new U.S. bombardment by targeting some of the United States' Gulf allies, according to a person briefed on the call who was not authorised to comment publicly and requested anonymity.

Saudi officials, the person added, have underscored in their engagements with the Trump administration that the kingdom is in a good position to defend itself against further potential Iranian strikes — as are fellow energy titans Qatar and the United Arab Emirates — but that Kuwait could be more vulnerable to attacks by Iranian-backed militias in Iraq.

As Trump threatens escalation, Republicans face tough polling

Mr. Trump has insisted that November's midterm elections aren't shaping his approach to the conflict that's spurred unease across the global economy.

But it's certainly on the minds of his fellow Republicans.

About two-thirds of U.S. adults say the war with Iran has not been worthwhile, according to polling from The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research published last week. That includes the vast majority of Democrats and independents, as well as about 37% of Republicans.

One of Mr. Trump's most outspoken allies on Capitol Hill suggested on Sunday (August 2) the administration needs to modulate its approach on Iran.

Louisiana Sen. John Kennedy said on NBC's “Meet the Press” that the debate in Washington has lost perspective on the devastation the U.S. military has inflicted on Iran since the start of the war.

Still, the Republican lawmaker acknowledged that further escalating the conflict could lead to a further surge in already elevated energy prices and “a lot of inflation for the American people.”

Mr. Kennedy made the case that tightening sanctions and targeting Iran's nuclear programme — rather than escalating the conflict — might be the best bet for the moment.

“They're all hellish choices,” Mr. Kennedy said. “But for the moment I'd maintain the status quo.”

World.title: Govt to sell up to 6.5% in LIC at ₹382/share; to add ₹31k crore to disinvestment kitty
World.content:
The government will sell up to a 6.5% stake in Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) at a floor price of ₹382/share through a two-day offer for sale (OFS) beginning on Tuesday (August 4, 2026).

The issue opens for non-retail investors on Tuesday (August 4) and for retail investors on Wednesday (August 5).

If fully subscribed, the sale of over 82.22 crore shares or a 6.5% stake at the given floor price will fetch about ₹31,000 crore to the disinvestment kitty.

"Government offers to disinvest 2.5% equity with an additional 4% as a green shoe option," Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) Secretary Arunish Chawla said in a post on X.

The floor price is at a 10% discount over Monday's closing price of LIC shares of ₹424.35 on the BSE.

The stake sale will help LIC achieve the minimum public shareholding requirement mandated by market regulator Sebi ahead of schedule.

Sebi had given LIC time till May 16, 2027, to achieve a minimum 10% public shareholding.

At present, the government holds a 96.5% stake in LIC.

It had earlier sold 3.5% through an initial public offering (IPO) in May 2022 at a price band of ₹902-949 per share, raising about ₹21,000 crore.

LIC currently has a market capitalisation of over ₹5.36 lakh crore. LIC shares settled at ₹424.35 on Monday (august 3), down 0.12% over the previous close on BSE.

So far in the current fiscal, the government has mopped up ₹21,082 crore through stake sale in seven public sector undertakings and remittances from SUUTI (Specified Undertaking of the Unit Trust of India).

World.title: Govt slashes petrol price by Rs4.08, high-speed diesel by Rs2.45
World.content:
The government on Monday slashed the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.08 and Rs2.45 per litre, respectively, passing on the impact of falling oil prices after US President Donald Trump called off a planned attack on Iran and announced talks with it.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs331.95 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs389.93 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 per litre on diesel.

The Petroleum Division’s notification said the new prices would be applicable for August 4 (Tuesday).

The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: 'Tick tock': Bilawal says PML-N's 'countdown' has begun, will hold rally in AJK's Poonch ahead of polls
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Monday reiterated his warning to the PML-N that a “countdown” for it has begun, as he declared that his party’s “movement” for people’s rights will extend to the entire country.

Bilawal made the remarks in a series of video messages he shared on X, wherein he reiterated his allegations of rigging against the PML-N — his party’s ally in the Centre — during the ongoing Azad Kashmir elections.

The PPP and the PML-N have been engaged in a war of words since the latter emerged in the lead in Mirpur polls on July 27. The PML-N has also won the majority of the seats in the second phase, with the PPP accusing it of rigging and other violent tactics in both phases.

In one of the three clips posted on X on Monday, Bilawal affirmed that his party’s struggle for the people’s right to governance, ownership and employment will continue.

“This movement will not remain restricted to the mountains of Kashmir or Gilgit-Baltistan. God-willing, I will run this movement across the entire Pakistan,” he declared.

The PPP chairman added, “And my message for the friends in PML-N is just this: you can hear that voice, listen carefully, tick tock, tick tock. Your countdown has begun.”

Punjab’s Information Minister Azma Bokhari even reacted to Bilawal’s statement, quipping: “Oh no, we are scared. What will happen now?”

Bilawal had given a similar warning last week to the federal government, which is led by the PML-N in alliance with his own PPP.

Senior leaders of his party have made similar remarks in recent days, even alleging the PML-N of rigging in the 2024 general elections, which resulted in both parties being part of the current ruling coalition. Both parties have also traded barbs over governance, political mandate and provincial performance.

Last week, Punjab Governor Sardar Saleem Haider Khan claimed that “the powers that be” were unhappy with the ruling PML-N.

In his videos today, Bilawal announced holding a jalsa in Poonch division’s Bagh town ahead of the elections set for August 10 across the division.

“The PPP does not lose courage, back down or leave the field. You should be ready,” he said.

The PPP chairman urged the people of Muzaffarabad’s LA-27 (Kutla) and LA-28 (Lachhrat) — where polling will be held tomorrow (August 4) after being suspended due to issues arising from bad weather — to vote for PPP candidates Bazil Naqvi and Javed Ayoub.

Bilawal paid tribute to the people of Kashmir for “competing with the PML-N, its threats, rigging and bullets” in the ongoing elections.

He reiterated the PPP’s claims that its party worker was killed, an MNA suffered a bullet injury, and its leader Chaudhry Latif Akbar — currently the acting AJK president — was “attacked” on Sunday during polling in Muzaffarabad.

The PML-N has disputed the claim about the party worker, saying he died from a heart attack and was not part of the PPP.

In one video clip, Bilawal asserted that the elections so far have not been transparent.

“These were rigging elections, bullet elections, murderous elections and bloody elections,” he claimed.

Addressing his supporters, he said, “Despite all this, you have secured nine seats for PPP. God-willing, I will get you back the seats stolen from you in Mirpur and Muzaffarabad.”

CEC stresses law and order for polling to go ahead on all Poonch seats

Separately, AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal stressed the importance of law and order in Poonch for polling to proceed in all constituencies on August 10.

The AJK CEC told the media today that considering the situation in Poonch division, the commission would conduct polling on August 10 in three constituencies in Bagh, one in Haveli and one in Abbaspur.

However, the constituencies of Baloch and Palandri (in Sudhnoti district) were also under consideration, he said.

“If we receive positive reports from there and the way people in Muzaffarabad rejected all pressures and tactics, came out of their homes and cast their votes, people in Poonch also extend the same cooperation, God-willing, we are ready to hold elections in all constituencies except for Rawalakot city and Thorar.”

At the same time, he said: “Our preparation is complete for all constituencies. However, the law and order situation and the demands of the safety of voters play an important role in holding elections.”

Responding to a question, he said that under the AJK constitution, the current Legislative Assembly ceases to exist after August 4.

“Even if elections cannot be held in two or a few more constituencies, one cannot say that the house is not complete or those who have returned cannot take oath or perform their functions,” he explained.

He said the new assembly would still take oath after the completion of the August 10 polls.

For LA-27, where the election had been postponed across the constituency, he said polling will be held at all 197 polling stations tomorrow (Tuesday).

Polling would be held on Tuesday from 8am to 5pm at 54 polling stations in three union councils (UCs) of LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II (Lachhrat).

Polling staff and election material could not reach these areas in time due to road blockades. At two of these polling stations, supporters of a candidate had set ballot boxes on fire.

The CEC affirmed that adequate arrangements had been made to reopen the roads following bad weather.

After security personnel returned from other areas, additional forces had been deployed in view of the sensitivity of these constituencies to ensure the electoral process was completed peacefully. He added that polling staff had already been dispatched to their respective stations under security escort.

In view of Tuesday’s polling, the Muzaffarabad deputy commissioner has declared a public holiday across the district.

AJK Election Commissioner retd Justice Ghulam Mustafa Mughal addresses the media on Aug 3, 2026. — Photo provided by Tariq Naqash

Expressing regret over allegations levelled against the Election Commission, CEC Mughal said the electoral watchdog was a constitutional and autonomous institution whose responsibility was to conduct free, fair and impartial elections without favouring any party.

He said it was the state’s responsibility to provide full security and assist the Election Commission.

“We perform our duties in accordance with the Constitution and the law, and our conscience is clear.”

Speaking about the second phase of elections held on Sunday, the AJK CEC said voter turnout in the seven constituencies stood at 53 per cent.

“This was certainly a difficult election, and given the circumstances that were created, this is by no means a low turnout,” retired Justice Mughal noted.

“I congratulate the people for making the right decision. They rejected the path of violence and chose the power of the vote instead — a path of positive change that will produce beneficial results.”

Ruling coalition ‘safe’ even without PPP

The PML-N-led federal government is said to be in a safe position even if the PPP withdraws its support to the PML-N in the National Assembly, as in the house of a total of 336 members, 169 votes are required to form the government.

Presently, the NA has 333 members as three seats are vacant.

Of these, the ruling alliance comprises: PML-N with 132 seats; PPP with 74; Mutahidda Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) with 22; PML-Q with five; Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) with four; independents with four; and PML-Z, National Party (NP) and Balochistan Awami Party (BAP) with one seat each.

The numbers show that even if the PPP leaves the ruling coalition, the PML-N-led alliance will have 170 seats, which is one seat more than the required number of 169 seats.

On the other hand, the opposition has a total of 89 votes, with PTI (who are considered independents) having 74 seats, Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-F (JUI-F) having 10 seats and one seat each held by Sunni Ittehad Council (SIC), Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) and Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP).

If the PPP and the entire opposition join hands, even then they cannot topple the PML-N-led set-up, as the combined 163 members are six less than the 169 seats required to form the government.

Whereas, if the PPP continues to attach itself to the ruling alliance, the alliance’s total seats will remain 244, 20 more seats than the number required for a two-thirds majority in the house to make any legislation smoothly.

World.title: At least 3 killed in rain-related incidents across Punjab; parts of Lahore inundated
World.content:
LAHORE: At least three people were killed and three others injured in rain-related incidents across Punjab on Monday, while torrential monsoon rains inundated roads and low-lying neighbourhoods in several cities, disrupting traffic, restricting public movement and causing urban flooding.

The Flood Forecasting Division (FFD) of the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) on Saturday forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall across parts of Punjab, Sindh and Balochistan until Aug 4.

According to a loss and damage report by the Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA), a man was killed and another injured when a house collapsed in Uch Sharif area of Bahawalpur district, while two children drowned in Khushab.

Two more people were injured in separate roof collapse incidents in Mandi Bahauddin and Lodhran. The report also recorded a house damaged in Bahawalpur.

Separately, authorities reported nine deaths in incidents not directly linked to rain or flooding. These included the drowning of a child in Kot Addu, a man in Narowal, and one man and two children in Attock. Four children also died of suffocation after being trapped inside a car in Mianwali.

A PDMA official clarified that these nine deaths did not have anything to do with rain or floods, adding that the victims drowned while trying to bathe and swim in canals and rivers.

PDMA Director General Saif Anwar Jappa directed deputy commissioners across Punjab to remain on high alert as the ongoing monsoon spell was expected to continue until Aug 5.

He said Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz was personally monitoring the situation and instructed all district administrations, Rescue 1122, Water and Sanitation Agency (Wasa) and other relevant departments to keep their personnel and machinery on standby to respond to any emergency.

Jappa said the Provincial Control Room and all District Emergency Operation Centres had been activated and were monitoring the situation round the clock.

He directed authorities to ensure the immediate drainage of rainwater from low-lying areas and identified waterlogging points to minimise disruption to public life. He also advised citizens to avoid electricity poles, hanging power lines, dilapidated buildings and mud houses during the rains, urging parents to keep children away from accumulated rainwater.

Heavy rain lashed Lahore for several hours, causing extensive waterlogging in many parts of the provincial capital. Rainwater accumulated at levels ranging from one to one-and-a-half feet deep in Township, Kacha Jail Road, Haider Road and Quaid-i-Azam Industrial Estate, submerging several major roads and severely disrupting traffic.

Long queues of vehicles formed on inundated roads as commuters struggled to reach their destinations, while residents in affected localities were forced to use alternative routes.

Waterlogging in low-lying areas also affected the drainage system, slowing traffic at numerous locations and limiting people’s movement.

Residents urged Wasa and the district administration to expedite drainage operations and restore the smooth flow of traffic.

According to Wasa Lahore’s monsoon control room, the city received an average rainfall of 24.8 millimetres. The highest level of rainfall was recorded at Wasa Head Office Gulberg (66.4mm), followed by Shadipura (58.8mm), Mughalpura (55.6mm), Mannawan (46.4mm) and Johar Town (45.6mm).

Other areas receiving significant rainfall included Tajpura (38.4mm), Farrukhabad (21.8mm), Kahna (20mm), Nishtar Town (19.8mm) and Airport (15mm).

Urban flooding was also reported from several other cities, with Faisalabad receiving the heaviest downpour, recording 103mm of rainfall according to the ponding report issued by the Wasa Head Office.

Water accumulated up to 23 inches at Chaudhry Flour Mills Chowk, 20 inches at Lower Canal on Jaranwala Road, 19 inches at Saad Bela (People’s Colony No 1), 17 inches each at Riaz Shahid Chowk and Iqbal Stadium, and 15 inches at several locations, including Lasani Pulli, Millat Chowk, 66-Feet Bazar Nishatabad and D Ground.

Wasa teams continued de-watering operations at dozens of inundated points across the city.

In Gujrat, the maximum rainfall reached 68.8mm, with water accumulating between two and five inches at major locations, including Railway Road, Ghareeb Pura Road, Bhimber Road and Jalalpur Jattan Road. Wasa officials said clearance work was continuing at most locations, although several roads remained partially inundated.

Mandi Bahauddin recorded 56.8mm of rainfall at the Wasa Laboratory gauge and 30mm at the Wasa Head Office. Water accumulated up to eight inches on Jail Road, four inches at College Chowk and Committee Chowk, and two inches at several other locations after the rain.

In Jhelum, Wasa reported only 0.87mm of average rainfall and said no significant waterlogging remained by the afternoon, with all identified ponding points cleared.

The widespread waterlogging was attributed to the intensity of the monsoon downpour, inadequate drainage capacity at several locations and the accumulation of runoff in low-lying urban areas, resulting in traffic congestion, restricted public movement and temporary inundation of residential neighbourhoods.

Wasa teams and district administrations continued drainage operations across affected cities throughout the day.

World.title: AJK information secretary says 7 law enforcement personnel martyred in recent unrest
World.content:
Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Information Secretary Muhammad Rashid Hanif on Monday said that seven law enforcement personnel, including those of police and Rangers, were martyred during recent unrest in the region.

The now-proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

Clashes took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Rawalakot and Mirpur last week, which reportedly resulted in several casualties. Amid the tensions, elections are being held across the region in three phases , with those in Mirpur (July 27) and Muzaffarabad divisions (Aug 2) marred by rigging allegations by the PPP.

In a televised address on Monday, Hanif recalled a press conference held on July 27 where a police official presented weapons allegedly recovered from JAAC members.

Hanif said that seven personnel were martyred from the “same weapons”, while 45 personnel suffered serious injuries and “numerous” others sustained minor injuries. He further said that police and Rangers vehicles were also burned.

“This confirms that the blacklisted JAAC is sheltering a large number of armed elements and is attempting to undermine peace and the writ of the state,” the information secretary asserted.

Addressing allegations by JAAC regarding incidents in Rawalakot and surrounding areas between July 27 and July 31, he said they were not only false but “part of a misinformation and propaganda campaign”, which in itself was part of a broader effort to “undermine public order and the writ of the state”.

He went on to stress that “security institutions of the AJK government have demonstrated the utmost restraint and professionalism while maintaining law and order”.

The information secretary rejected allegations of unprovoked firing by security forces and withholding bodies, stating that the government had no bodies presently in its custody.

“Propaganda being circulated by this banned organisation on social media is misleading and part of an effort to further aggravate the situation,” he added, alleging that JAAC members were involved in blocking or burning vehicles carrying essential supplies and food.

Hanif also provided the casualty figures for law enforcement personnel resulting from JAAC’s “violent actions” in recent years, noting one police official was martyred in 2024 and three personnel in October 2025.

“Two armed operatives from this organisation recently admitted in their confession that they were promised Rs10 million to kill one Rangers personnel, which raises serious concerns about the source of this group’s funding,” the AJK official claimed.

AJK govt calls BBC report ‘biased’; Al Jazeera’s coverage termed ‘selective’

Hanif also termed a BBC report on the Rawalakot clashes as “angled, biased and contrary to the facts”, saying that the AJK government “rejected” it.

“The facts and figures presented in this report are not only incorrect, but they were published without verification or confirmation from the government, police or the civil administration,” he stated, describing the report as “contrary to the ethics of journalism and professionalism”.

Contending that videos and press releases from the AJK administration had provided evidence of JAAC possessing modern weapons, he noted that the BBC “should have at least taken the verified evidence into account and published a report based on facts”.

Similarly, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting criticised Al Jazeera’s coverage of the AJK elections, accusing the Qatar-based broadcaster of “selective reporting from handpicked polling stations” in Muzaffarabad.

In a post on X on Sunday night, the ministry alleged that the media outlet had “sought to misrepresent the AJK elections and the voting process” through “carefully chosen timings and scripted statements from selected individuals”.

“Such yellow journalism only confirms the agenda of external actors with vested interests who are attempting to delegitimise this electoral exercise and undermine the popular will of the people of Muzaffarabad and AJK,” it alleged.

The publication had reported that the residents of Muzaffarabad were observing a boycott of the polls following unrest in the region, where the proscribed JAAC has been protesting for several weeks.

Over the past two months, the regional administration and the JAAC have been at odds over various issues, most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 seats in the region’s Legislative Assembly, which has resulted in protests across the region.

The government has accused militant elements “pu­r­­s­u­ing a foreign age­nda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the recent unrest in AJK.

On June 5, following the announcement of the JAAC’s June 9 strike, the AJK government declared the committee a proscribed organisation and placed it under the First Schedule of the region’s anti-terrorism act (ATA).

The next day, AJK authorities launched a crackdown on the JAAC, arresting scores of its leaders and later placing 147 of its activists on the Fourth Schedule of the ATA.

World.title: Myanmar's detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi meets Red Cross official
World.content:
Myanmar’s detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi met with a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross on Monday, after years of questions over the health and well-being of the 81-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner.

Suu Kyi has been in detention since February 2021, when an elected civilian government led by her was ousted by Myanmar’s military in a dawn coup, plunging the impoverished Southeast Asian nation into turmoil.

Since then, Suu Kyi’s exact whereabouts and health condition have been difficult to determine, with no foreign leader or envoy having publicly met with her despite requests for contact from countries in the region that have excluded Myanmar’s leadership from their summits.

Suu Kyi met with Arnaud de Baecque, Resident Representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross to Myanmar, in the capital Naypyitaw on Monday, government spokesperson Khine Khine Soe said in a message via Telegram.

The ICRC confirmed that a delegate had met with Suu Kyi, without naming the official, while her son described the visit as the first positive development concerning his mother in more than five years.

In one of four photographs provided by the Myanmar government spokesperson, Suu Kyi is seen dressed in traditional Burmese attire and standing unaided, shaking hands with de Baecque.

In another, they are seated in a sparsely furnished, wood-panelled room containing only two chairs and a desk.

This handout photo taken and released on August 3, 2026 by Myanmar’s Presidential Press and Information Bureau (PPIB) shows detained former civilian leader Aung San Suu Kyi (L) meeting with Arnaude de Baecque, resident representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to Myanmar, in Naypyidaw. — via AFP

Son urges continued pressure for Suu Kyi’s release

The ICRC said the visit had met with its standards and procedures for visiting people deprived of liberty. “This included the opportunity to speak with Daw Aung San Suu Kyi in private,” it said in a statement, using a Burmese honorific.

Suu Kyi’s son, Kim Aris, told Reuters that the ICRC was not able to have a physician examine his mother but he said she seemed to be in good health and in good spirits.

“It’s the first independent proof that I’ve had that she’s actually alive for a long time now,” he said in London. “So it’s extremely meaningful.”

Aris said that while he remained cautious, he hoped to be able to speak to his mother in time, and urged other governments to keep up the pressure on Myanmar to release her and other political prisoners.

Aris told Reuters in December that he had received only sporadic, second-hand details about his mother’s heart, bone and gum problems — and had not heard from her in years.

The United Nations, whose special envoy on Myanmar, Julie Bishop, has called repeatedly for independent, verifiable reports on Suu Kyi’s circumstances, said it had taken note of the ICRC announcement and stressed the need for inclusive dialogue.

“We welcome this development and reiterate our call for the swift and unconditional release of all those arbitrarily detained, as a fundamental step towards conditions conducive to a credible and transparent political process,” UN spokesperson Farhan Haq told a daily briefing in New York.

Detained since coup

After a marathon run of secret trials following the 2021 coup, Suu Kyi, who was held under house arrest for a total of 15 years under a previous junta, was sentenced to 33 years’ detention, convicted of charges ranging from corruption and inciting election fraud to violating state secrecy rules.

Her allies maintain that the charges were politically motivated and aimed at sidelining the most popular politician in the country of 51 million people.

The sentence was later reduced, leaving her with 18 years still to serve, according to a member of her legal team.

Myanmar’s military-backed administrations have repeatedly claimed that Suu Kyi, who is the daughter of Myanmar’s independence hero General Aung San, is in “good health”, even as international pressure has grown to allow independent verification.

After a meeting between Myanmar’s foreign minister and counterparts from the regional Asean bloc last month, Thailand’s top diplomat Sihasak Phuangketkeow called for access to Suu Kyi.

Asean has barred Myanmar’s leadership from its top meetings for failure to implement a peace roadmap.

Birthday cake

In late April, following a military-engineered election that allowed former junta leader Min Aung Hlaing to become Myanmar’s president, Suu Kyi was moved to house arrest.

In another of the photos provided by the Myanmar government offering a rare glimpse inside what appears to be her residence, Suu Kyi is seen cutting a birthday cake, with a clothes rack and storage boxes visible in the background.

This undated handout photo released on August 3, 2026 by Myanmar’s Presidential Press and Information Bureau (PPIB) shows detained former civilian leader Aung San Suu Kyi cutting a cake in Naypyidaw. — via AFP

A fourth photograph is a close-up of the cake, inscribed with “Happy Birthday Aunty Suu 19.6.2026”.

Reuters was not able to independently verify the location and the date when the pictures were taken. No earlier version of the pictures was found posted online before Monday.

World.title: Death toll from suicide bombing near police station in Swat rises to 17
World.content:
SWAT: The death toll from Sunday’s suicide bombing near a police station in Swat rose to 17 on Monday, including several policemen.

The suicide bombing had taken place near the Kabal Police Station while a protest against lawlessness was under way at the adjoining public square. Police said that the suicide bomber had detonated his explosives after police personnel atte­mpted to stop and search him at the entrance to the police station.

According to a list of casualties shared by Swat police spokesperson Nasir Iqbal Karimi, seven policemen and 10 civilians have lost their lives in the incident while 18 policemen and nine civilians have been injured.

Police have revised down the death toll from an earlier tally of 19, which they shared in a statement earlier in the day.

Karimi said in the statement that a large-scale rescue operation had been launched immediately after the attack, in which more than 50 Rescue 1122 personnel participated.

“Rescue teams provided first aid at the scene before shifting the injured to various hospitals for further treatment. Authorities are continuing relief efforts as investigations into the suicide attack remain under way,” it said.

In a separate statement, Swat police said the funeral prayers of two policemen martyred in the suicide attack were held at Javed Iqbal Shaheed Police Lines on Monday.

A smartly turned-out police contingent presented a guard of honour to Constable Mukarram Khan and Constable Hussain Khan, and floral wreaths were laid on their coffins.

The ceremony was attended by Malakand Regional Police Officer (RPO) Syed Fida Hassan Shah, Swat District Police Officer (DPO) Muhammad Umar Khan, Superintendent of Police (operations) Ghulam Sadiq Khan, Superintendent of Police (headquarters) Ataullah, and other senior police officers.

Security personnel and law enforcers have been coming under attack in KP, which continues to face terrorism.

According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS) monthly security assessment released on Saturday, Security personnel deaths in terrorism incidents in KP, excluding merged districts, increased from 12 in June to 38 in July and terrorist deaths from 37 to 108, reflecting a rise by 192pc. But civilian deaths fell from 26 to seven, a decline by 73pc. One peace committee member was also killed.

Security personnel deaths in merged districts rose from six to 11 and terrorist deaths fell from 72 to 55. Civilian deaths, meanwhile, rose by 86pc, increasing from seven to 13.

CM visits Swat

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi reached Swat on Monday to meet with the martyrs’ families. He was accompanied by Special Assistant for Home Affairs Tariq Saeed, Chief Secretary Shahab Ali Shah and the KP inspector general (IG) of police, according to a statement issued by the CM office.

In Swat, he visited Sheikh Zayed Al Nahyan Hospital in Saidu Sharif and inquired about the health of those injured in the suicide attack.

The chief minister directed the hospital administration to ensure the provision of the best possible medical treatment to all the injured, the statement said.

It added that the CM also chaired a high-level meeting at the Jirga Hall in Saidu Sharif. At the meeting, which was also attended by senior officials, the CM was briefed on the overall law and order situation in Malakand Division and its Swat district.

Reaffirming the government’s commitment to restoring peace, the chief minister said there would be no compromise on law and order in Swat and Malakand. He directed the relevant authorities to launch a full-scale operation against terrorists and ensure that peace and stability were restored.

Meanwhile, KP Inspector General of Police (IG) Zulfikar Hameed visited the injured personnel and civilians in the hospital, according to a post on the KP Police’s X account.

“Our police personnel have high morale. The cowardly attacks of terrorists will be given a befitting response,” he is quoted as saying.

Lawyers, traders observe strike

Lawyers across Swat and Upper Swat observed a complete strike on Monday to condemn Sunday’s suicide bombing. Court proceedings remained suspended as members of the legal fraternity expressed solidarity with the victims and called for stronger measures for eliminating terrorism.

A shutter-down strike was also observed across Kabal tehsil, where markets remained closed.

Separately, elders of the Swat Qaumi Jirga, traders, lawyers, and youth representatives have announced a protest demonstration at Nishat Chowk in Swat’s Mingora on August 7 to condemn the recent wave of terrorism in the region.

The organisers said the planned demonstration was aimed at expressing solidarity with the victims of terrorist attacks. It was being organised to demand lasting peace and urge the government to take decisive action against terrorist groups operating in the area, they said.

World.title: Islamabad ATC hands Mushtaq Ahmad to police on 3-day physical remand in protest case
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) has handed over former senator Mushtaq Ahmad Khan and other suspects to police on a three-day physical remand in a case registered in connection with a protest.

The police produced the former senator and another person named Daniyal before Duty Judge Rukhsanda Shaheen in the ATC.

During the hearing, the prosecution requested a 30-day physical remand of the suspects, stating that the police needed to recover a vehicle and weapons allegedly connected with the case.

After hearing the arguments, the court granted the police three-day physical remand of Mushtaq and the other suspects and directed that they be produced before the court again upon completion of the remand period.

The first information report (FIR) was registered at Islamabad’s Shalimar Police Station on July 31, on the complaint of Sub-inspector Ghulam Murtaza.

The FIR said Mushtaq and dozens of others had led a crowd of about 400-500 people and gathered in the capital’s F-10.
